text: Start every new build from one small reset: `box-sizing: border-box; min-width: 0` on `*, ::before, ::after`, and give any fixed-size image, icon or avatar in a flex row `flex: none`.
why: Flex and grid items default to `min-width: auto`, so a long word or wide child overflows its track; `min-width: 0` lets them shrink, but then a sized media item shrinks too unless it opts out.
check: computed `min-width` is `0px` on a flex child; no horizontal scrollbar at 1440 and 375 with a long unbroken string in a card; fixed media has `flex-shrink: 0`.

text: Set `text-wrap: pretty` on `:root` (inherits everywhere) and `text-wrap: balance` on h1-h4. Treat `pretty` as an enhancement: Firefox ignores it.
why: `balance` evens heading lines; `pretty` makes the browser spend more effort avoiding a one-word last line (Safari also evens the ragged edge). It also applies to textareas, so set `text-wrap: stable` on a field where lines jump while typing.
check: computed `text-wrap` on h1 is `balance`, on p is `pretty`; no last line of a hero subtitle holds a single short word (still hand-break two-line subtitles per founder taste).

text: Set `font-synthesis: none` and load every weight and style the design uses; use the two macOS smoothing declarations (`-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased`, `-moz-osx-font-smoothing: grayscale`) on `:root`.
why: Without it the browser fakes a bold or italic the font lacks; with it a missing weight silently renders as regular, so the font load list must be complete. Grayscale antialiasing renders thinner type that matches Figma.
check: every `font-weight` used in the page has a loaded face (document.fonts); `font-synthesis` computes to `none`.

text: Put `scrollbar-gutter: stable` on `:root`, and pair it with `html:has(dialog:modal) { overflow: hidden }` for scroll-locking.
why: Reserving the gutter stops a sideways page shift when a modal removes the scrollbar or content grows past one screen. Trade-off documented on the site: centred content sits slightly off-centre on a page too short to scroll.
check: `body` width unchanged before and after opening a modal; computed `scrollbar-gutter` on `html`.

text: Use `100svh` for documents and heroes, `100dvh` only for app shells that pin UI to the bottom.
why: `svh` is the viewport with mobile toolbars showing, so nothing hides behind them and nothing re-lays out; `dvh` tracks the moving toolbar and re-flows on every change.
applies: landing page: svh. SaaS app UI: dvh.
check: grep `100vh` returns nothing; hero `min-height` uses `svh`.

text: Set form inputs to `font-size: max(16px, 1rem)`; never fix iOS focus zoom with `user-scalable=no` or `maximum-scale=1`.
why: iOS Safari zooms the page on focus of any input under 16px and does not zoom back; disabling zoom takes it away from users who need it.
check: computed font-size of `input, textarea, select` >= 16px; viewport meta has no `user-scalable`.

text: On controls set `touch-action: manipulation` and `-webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent`, and give every pressable element its own `:active` state in the same change. Restrict `user-select: none` to controls, never body or links.
why: `manipulation` removes the double-tap-zoom wait so `click` fires at once; removing the tap highlight removes the only native feedback, so `:active` has to replace it; people copy text from body and links.
check: every `button, a, [role=button]` has a `:active` rule; `user-select` is not `none` on `body`, `p`, `a`.

text: Never add `text-box: trim-both` to `*`, never set `text-rendering: optimizeLegibility`, and never use a reset that puts `display: contents` or one shared grid cell on every element.
why: The site measured the damage: a global trim shrank a one-line 16px/1.5 paragraph from 25px to 11px and a 40px button to 27px; the grid-cell reset stacks everything in one cell and `display: contents` on containers removes their boxes and breaks the breakout grid; MDN recommends `auto` for body text rendering.
check: grep the stylesheet for `\* *\{[^}]*text-box`, `optimizeLegibility`, `display: contents` on `div`.

text: Write spacing, borders, offsets and alignment with logical properties (`padding-inline`, `margin-block-end`, `inset-inline-end`, `border-inline-start`, `text-align: start`). The four-value shorthands (`margin`, `padding`, `inset`) stay physical, so use the `-inline` / `-block` shorthands.
why: `inline` and `block` follow `dir` and `writing-mode`, so one declaration set renders mirrored in RTL with no second stylesheet.
check: grep for `margin-left|margin-right|padding-left|padding-right|left:|right:` in authored CSS (allow in third-party); Tailwind: `mbs-`, `pe-`, `inset-bs-` instead of `mt-`, `pr-`, `top-` (4.2+).

text: Define colours in `oklch()` and derive every related colour from one base with `color-mix(in oklch, ...)` (hover: mix with black 15%; subtle tint: 12% of the base in `transparent`). Never hardcode a second hex or an `rgba()` for a hover, tint or alpha.
why: Lightness is perceptual, so scales and contrast are predictable; mixing in OKLCH keeps the hue where sRGB mixing drifts toward gray; one base drives the family.
check: hover/tint tokens are `color-mix()` expressions of a base token; no stray `rgba(` for brand tints.

text: Write grays, white and black as `oklch(L 0 none)`, with `none` (or the `white` keyword) as the hue, never `oklch(1 0 0)`.
why: A written hue of `0` is red and pulls mixes toward red; the site measured half white `oklch(1 0 0)` and half a hue-264 blue landing at hue 312 in Chrome and Safari, versus staying at 264 with `none`.
check: grep `oklch\([^)]* 0 0\)` (chroma 0 with hue 0) in token files.

text: Give each colour token both themes with `light-dark(a, b)`, declare `color-scheme: light dark` on `:root`, switch themes by setting `color-scheme` (on `html`, or on one section for an always-dark band), and add `<meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark">`. Do not redefine the tokens under `.dark`.
why: `light-dark()` resolves per element from the computed scheme, so the same tokens serve the system setting, a manual toggle and a dark section; the meta tag makes the browser paint the right background before CSS loads; `color-scheme` also flips form controls and scrollbars.
check: no duplicated token block under a theme class; `light-dark()` takes colours only (images need their own rule); Baseline since May 2024 (Chrome 123, Firefox 120, Safari 17.5).

text: Build fluid values as `clamp(min, rem + vw, max)`, never a bare `vw`, with both bounds in `rem`; derive the preferred value from two points (`slope = (max - min) / (wide - narrow)`, `vw = slope * 100`, `rem part = min - slope * narrow`) and put it in a token.
why: `clamp(1rem, 1vw, 1.75rem)` stays at 16px on every screen under 1600px because 1vw is smaller than 1rem until then, and a bare `vw` ignores the reader's font-size setting.
check: no `font-size: Nvw`; every fluid token has a `rem` term.

text: Keep a fluid font size's maximum at or below 2.5 times its minimum.
why: The `vw` part does not grow when the reader zooms, so fluid text grows less than the page; past 2.5x, 500% zoom cannot double the text at some widths, which fails WCAG 1.4.4 (Resize Text).
check: for every fluid font token, `max / min <= 2.5`. A 72px-at-1440 hero h1 that shrinks to 40px on mobile is 1.8x and passes.

text: When a design has more than two or three font sizes, derive the type and space scale from six plain-number inputs (narrow and wide viewport in rem as unitless numbers, base size at each end, ratio at each end) with `pow()`, one `clamp()` for `--fluid`, and components that only read the step tokens.
why: It replaces a per-breakpoint size table and a generator someone must re-run; steps stay within 0.001px of the formula (site-tested Chrome 150, Safari 27). Space pairs (`--space-s-l`) give small-on-phone to large-on-desktop padding (18px to 40px in the example).
check: inputs are unitless (Firefox cannot divide length by length); step `n` passes when `(size-wide / size-narrow) * (ratio-wide / ratio-narrow)^n <= 2.5`; a pair is never used for a font size. Support Chrome 120, Firefox 118, Safari 15.4.

text: Replace the `section > .container` pair with one content grid on the section: a three-width grid with named lines (`full-width`, `breakout`, `content`), where children default to `grid-column: content` and any child opts into `breakout` or `full-width` with one class. A full-width band uses `grid-template-columns: inherit` so its inner content still aligns to the page column.
why: `min(100% - 2*gutter, max)` shrinks the content column with no media query; `minmax(0, ...)` breakout tracks collapse on small screens so the page cannot overflow; named lines make `grid-column: content` work without numbers. Change widths by overriding `--content`, not the template.
check: content column x-edges equal the nav and hero left/right edges (the founder's one-left-edge rule); every direct child is placed (an unplaced child lands in the gutter track); no horizontal overflow at 375.

text: Lay out equal cards with `grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, 16rem), 1fr))`; use `auto-fill` instead when the item count changes (filters).
why: The column count follows the container with no breakpoints; `min(100%, 16rem)` lets the minimum shrink to a narrow container; `auto-fit` stretches a short last row, `auto-fill` keeps card size.
check: no card-grid breakpoint ladder; a 200px-wide container does not overflow.

text: Make card parts line up across a row with subgrid: the grid gives each card `grid-row: span N` and the card uses `grid-template-rows: subgrid` with its own `row-gap`; N equals the number of parts in the card.
why: Each card adopts the parent's row tracks, so the tallest title in a row sets the title height for all cards; titles, bodies and footers align regardless of copy length. Without the span every part piles into one row; without `row-gap` the card inherits the parent's gap.
applies: landing page feature/pricing cards; SaaS app UI card grids.
check: footers' top y equal across cards in a row with unequal body lengths. Subgrid: Chrome 117, Firefox 71, Safari 16.

text: For a pair where one side has an ideal width (media object, input plus button, page plus aside), use the wrap-on-its-own sidebar: `flex-wrap: wrap`, sidebar `flex-basis` ideal width with `flex-grow: 1`, main `flex-basis: 0; flex-grow: 999; min-inline-size: 50%`. For a sticky sidebar add `align-self: start`.
why: The huge grow factor gives the main side all free space; below 50% it wraps and both go full width. The wrap point is a share of the container, so changing `min-inline-size` moves it. A stretched sidebar has no room to stick, and a bare `img` as a side stretches and distorts (use `align-items: start`).
check: the pair stacks without a media query when the container narrows; sticky sidebar computes `align-self: start`.

text: Make any component that appears in slots of different widths respond to its container: a `container-type: inline-size` ancestor, `@container (width > 30rem)` for layout changes and `cqi` units in `clamp()` for fluid type per component.
why: A media query only knows the viewport; the same KPI card or pricing card is right in a sidebar and in a wide column. Constraints measured by the author: the container must be an ancestor (an element cannot query itself); never put `container-type` on a shrink-to-fit element (it collapses to zero); a container cannot also be a subgrid, so use separate elements; with no container above, `cqi` falls back to the viewport, so one token serves the page and every slot; never register a `cqi` token with `@property` (it computes once on `:root`).
applies: SaaS app UI (dashboard widgets) and landing page bento.
check: widget layout changes when the slot width changes at a fixed viewport; no `container-type` on an inline-sized element. Support Chrome 105, Firefox 110, Safari 16.

text: Stack overlapping layers by putting them in one grid cell (`display: grid` on the parent, `grid-area: 1 / 1` on children, `place-self` to align each) instead of `position: absolute` offsets; keep `position: absolute` for a layer that must not affect the container's size.
why: Layers stay in flow, so the container takes the size of its largest layer; absolute children add nothing to it. Later DOM children paint on top; use `z-index` only to change that.
applies: all (text over image, badge on a card, two swapping icons, hero copy over a visual).
check: the container height equals the tallest layer without a fixed height.

text: Use `safe` alignment (`justify-content: safe center`) on centred or end-aligned flex rows that can overflow (tab rows, toolbars, vertically centred modals).
why: Plain `center` pushes overflow off the start edge where scrolling cannot reach; `safe` falls back to `start` once content overflows. Auto margins on the item give the same safe centring in every browser with flexbox. Support Chrome 115, Firefox 63, Safari 17.6.
check: the first tab is reachable (scrollLeft 0 shows it) when the row overflows.

text: Cut off overflow with `overflow: clip`, not `hidden`, unless a script scrolls the element or it has `resize`; put it on the element that overflows, never on `html` or `body`.
why: `hidden` makes the element a scroll container (and sets the other axis to `auto`), which causes stray scrollbars and breaks `position: sticky` inside it; `clip` cuts and does neither. A cut-off hero visual that bleeds off the frame is the common case.
applies: landing page hero frames; SaaS app UI.
check: no `overflow: hidden` on hero or section wrappers that contain sticky children. Support Chrome 90, Firefox 81, Safari 16.

text: Give each section its own default `padding-block` and fix awkward meetings with neighbour pair rules: `A:has(+ B)` adjusts A's bottom edge, `A + B` adjusts B's top edge, `:where(A + *)` adds a divider with zero specificity. Name sections by what they are (`.hero`, `.faq`), never by page.
why: The rules describe pairs, not pages, so whatever order an editor picks, each meeting gets the right spacing and every other pair keeps the default; no spacer elements or per-page overrides.
check: zero spacer divs; no per-page padding overrides; the pair list stays short (merge pairs that share a reason, such as equal backgrounds).

text: Let the parent own vertical space between siblings: `display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap` in components whose children you know, and the margin form (`> * { margin-block: 0 }`, `> * + * { margin-block-start: var(--flow-space, 1em) }`, a heading sets `--flow-space: 2em`, what follows a heading sets 0.5em) for CMS or Markdown content.
why: A margin describes a relation between neighbours, so a child that owns its margin leaves it behind as the last child of a padded box. `gap` leaves nothing above the first or below the last and ignores hidden children (the margin form counts them).
check: no `margin-bottom` on children of a stacked container; a flex-column child button gets `align-self: start` (it otherwise stretches full width); keep the `>` in the margin form.

text: Push one item to the far end of a flex row or column with an auto margin (`margin-block-start: auto` for card actions, `margin-inline-start: auto` for an account link), and centre a title between a header and a footer with `margin-block: auto` inside a `min-block-size: 100svh` column.
why: An auto margin takes all free space on its side; two opposite auto margins split it. It replaces spacer elements and `space-between` on containers with more than two children. `gap` is the minimum when no free space remains. The centred item is centred in the leftover space, not in the section (a footer with no header pulls the title up by half the footer height). Use `min-block-size`, never `block-size`.
applies: all (card footers, nav actions, full-height hero).
check: card CTAs share one baseline y across a row of unequal cards.

text: Nest rounded elements concentrically: `outer radius = inner radius + padding`, derived with `calc()` from the inner radius (the other way round hits zero once padding exceeds the radius).
why: Two curves look parallel only when they share a centre; equal radii make the corner band look pinched. This is the same rule the engine already enforces (consistency-mechanics.md 2), here with the derive-from-inner direction and a 0.5rem / 1.5rem / 3rem padding demo.
applies: all (the hero `Frame` shell, image in card, button in input).
check: `parent radius - child radius` within 1px of the padding.

text: Decide for every user or CMS string what happens when it is too long: wrap (`overflow-wrap: break-word` on `:root`), one line with ellipsis (`white-space: nowrap; overflow: clip; text-overflow: ellipsis` on the text element), or N lines (all four of `display: -webkit-box; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; -webkit-line-clamp: N; overflow: clip`).
why: `break-word` breaks a word only when it cannot fit alone and inherits, so one root declaration covers the page; `min-width: 0` lets the item shrink but does nothing for the word, so the two need each other. Never use `anywhere` on the root: it also shrinks min-content and a content-sized box collapses to one letter per line (use it on table cells, which ignore `break-word`). Put padding on a wrapper, not on the clamped element (the next line shows through bottom padding). Truncate only text readable in full elsewhere.
applies: SaaS app UI (tables, names, URLs), landing page testimonial cards.
check: a 60-character unbroken string in every text slot causes no overflow at 375 and 1440. Site-tested: with `overflow: clip` the ellipsis and clamp draw in Chrome 150 and Safari 27; Firefox untested, fall back to `hidden`.

text: Give every media slot you do not control a stable box: `inline-size: 100%; block-size: auto; aspect-ratio: W / H; object-fit: cover` plus a background colour for the load and failure state; `object-fit: contain` for logos and product shots; avatars `flex: none` with equal sizes.
why: `aspect-ratio` computes height before the file loads (no CLS); `cover` crops where the default stretches. A fixed `height` attribute beats the ratio, an image with transparency must not get a background, and in real Safari 27 a failed image ignores `aspect-ratio` and draws a square (put the ratio on a wrapper where a failed load must not move layout).
check: CLS is 0 with images blocked; `object-fit` is `cover` or `contain` on every content image.

text: Draw the hairline edge of avatars and photos as `outline: 1px solid` at about 10% black (white in dark, via `light-dark()`) with `outline-offset: -1px`.
why: A negative-offset outline sits inside the image edge, takes no space and follows `border-radius` (Chrome 94, Firefox 88, Safari 16.4), so a white avatar on a white card still has an edge; it needs the `color-scheme` from the tokens or it stays black in dark mode.
check: computed `outline-offset: -1px` on avatars, alpha <= 0.1.

text: Use `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` on prices, table cells, `time`, timers, counters and chart labels, not globally, and only in a font that ships tabular figures.
why: Equal digit widths align columns and stop a ticking value from shifting its neighbours; proportional digits read better in prose; with no tabular figures in the font nothing changes.
applies: SaaS app UI; landing page product figures.
check: computed `font-variant-numeric` includes `tabular-nums` on every `td`, `time`, currency figure; not on `body`.

text: Centre single-line labels in buttons, badges and chips on their letters with `text-box: trim-both cap alphabetic` on the text element (the `<span>` inside an `inline-flex` button, because it has no effect on a flex or grid container), and raise the padding to keep the height.
why: A line box reserves unequal space above the capitals and below the baseline per font, so equal padding puts letters off-centre; trimming cuts to cap height and baseline so a font swap no longer moves the label. Site measurement: a 0.75rem-padded button went 48px to 35px. I measured Inter 500 18px/1.2 with 12px padding in Chromium 156: 45.6px plain, 37.1px trimmed, so pad up by ~4.25px per side to keep 45.6. Scope it to labels, one line, with no fallback (support Chrome 133, Firefox 154, Safari 18.2).
check: button height computed after the change equals the spec (Kaching hero CTA / founder 44px target): re-measure; label ink centre within 0.5px of box centre; never on `*`.

text: Size an icon beside a label by the text, not in `px`: in an `inline-flex` row with `align-items: baseline; gap: 0.5em`, give the `svg` `flex: none; block-size: 1cap; inline-size: auto`, and for a notice whose label wraps give it `inline-size: 1em; block-size: 1lh` with `align-items: start`.
why: `1cap` is the capital height so the icon reads as one more capital and resting its bottom on the baseline stands it where a capital stands; `1lh` makes the icon box the height of the first line so it stays beside line one when the text wraps. A 16px icon on 16px text is 5-7px shorter than the capitals of 32px text. Measured by me in Chromium 156: Inter 18px gives a `1cap` icon of 13.09px (cap height 0.727). Needs a `viewBox`; icon sets with built-in padding look small, so raise the number and keep the unit (`1.2cap`). With the trimmed label above, `align-items: center` also lines up at both edges. Support: `cap` Chrome 118, Firefox 97, Safari 17.2; `lh` Chrome 109, Firefox 120, Safari 16.4.
check: icon height within 1px of the label's cap height (font-size x cap-height ratio); no icon sized in `px` next to text.

text: Use one global focus style on `:focus-visible`: `outline: max(2px, 0.08em) solid currentColor; outline-offset: 0.25em`. On a filled button set the outline colour to the button's background; for a ring drawn with `box-shadow` keep `outline-color: transparent`, never `outline: none`.
why: The browser decides when a ring helps (keyboard yes, mouse click on a button no, text input always); `currentColor` and `em` make it follow each component; `outline` takes no layout space and survives forced-colors mode, which removes `box-shadow`.
check: grep `outline: *none` returns nothing; tab through the page: every interactive element shows a ring with contrast >= 3:1 against its surround.

text: Wrap every `:hover` rule in `@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`.
why: Touch browsers apply `:hover` on tap and keep it until the next tap elsewhere; `pointer: fine` also rules out styluses and Android devices that claim hover. Tailwind v4's `hover:` variant only wraps `(hover: hover)`, so the full query must be written by hand in custom CSS; touch feedback comes from `:active`.
check: every `:hover` selector sits inside the media query (the kit's `.btn-white:hover` currently uses `(hover: hover)` only).

text: Give every button and pressable surface `:active { transform: scale(0.97) }` (range 0.95-0.98) with `transition: transform 160ms var(--ease-out)` inside the reduced-motion query; drive JS feedback from `pointerdown`, not `click`.
why: A native button responds the instant a finger lands, `:active` does the same on every input; feedback on `click` arrives when the finger leaves and reads as lag; `scale()` shrinks label and icon together. Founder: Kaching press scale is 0.98, inside this range.
check: computed transform on `:active` is `scale(0.95..0.98)`; transition duration 100-160ms.

text: Extend small targets to 44px with a pseudo-element on the button: `position: relative` on the button and `::after { content: ""; position: absolute; inset: min(0px, (100% - 44px) / 2) }`.
why: The pseudo-element belongs to the button so its clicks hit the button, the negative inset grows the area to exactly 44px, and `min(0px, ...)` leaves larger targets alone. It does not work on `<input>` (wrap it in a `<label>`) and `overflow: hidden/clip` on the button cuts it off.
applies: SaaS app UI icon buttons; landing page close buttons.
check: `elementFromPoint` 22px outside the visible box of a 28px icon button returns the button. Do not combine with the card-link `::after` or the shadow `::before/::after` on the same element.

text: Make a whole card clickable with one real link inside its heading and a stretched `::after` (`position: absolute; inset: 0`) on that link; the card is `position: relative`, other buttons and links get `position: relative; z-index: 1`, and the focus ring moves to the card with `.card:has(.card-link:focus-visible)` while the link's own ring is `2px solid transparent`.
why: It keeps a real link (open in new tab, status-bar URL) and a short accessible name ("Quarterly report", not the whole card read aloud), where a wrapping `<a>` makes a screen reader read every word and a `div` click handler is not a link. No positioned element may sit between the card and the link (the overlay would size to it); text under the overlay cannot be selected; Safari ignores `outline-color` on its default ring so write the full `2px solid transparent`. Hover styles go on `.card:hover` inside the hover query.
applies: landing page blog/feature/pricing cards; SaaS app UI list rows.
check: the card's focus ring appears on keyboard focus; the accessible name of the link is the title only; click on the card padding navigates. Support Chrome 105, Firefox 121, Safari 15.4.

text: Style a parent by what it contains or the state of a child with `:has()` (`article:has(img)`, `form:has(:focus-visible)`) instead of a script-added class; on the root use it as a page-wide listener (`html:has(dialog:modal) { overflow: hidden }`).
why: `:has()` matches by descendants or following siblings and accepts state pseudo-classes. `:modal` matches `showModal()` only, so a non-modal dialog does not lock the page; keep `scrollbar-gutter: stable` with the lock; `:has()` cannot nest inside `:has()`.
check: no JS toggling a class solely to mirror child state. Support Chrome 105, Firefox 121, Safari 15.4.

text: Validate inline with `:user-invalid` / `:user-valid` driven by HTML attributes (`required`, `minlength`, `type`, `pattern`), never blur listeners plus a "touched" class, and pair the colour with text or an icon.
why: `:invalid` matches an empty required field on load; the `:user-` forms match only after the user has edited the field or tried to submit. Colour alone is not enough feedback (WCAG 1.4.1); the server still validates. Support Chrome 119, Firefox 88, Safari 16.5.
applies: forms in SaaS app UI and funnels.
check: no error styling visible on first paint of an untouched form; each error state has a text or icon cue.

text: Grow a textarea with `field-sizing: content`, bounded by `min-height` and `max-height` in `lh` (for example `3lh` to `12lh`) and `resize: none`; to animate the height, let a `ResizeObserver` copy the textarea's border-box height onto a `content-box` wrapper that transitions `height` and clips, with the border and background on the wrapper.
why: The browser measures the text, so the size is right on first paint, paste and resize with no mirror element; the textarea reaches its final height at once and only the wrapper animates. A fixed `height` brings fixed size back; past `max-height` it scrolls; a browser without support shows a fixed scrolling textarea. Support Chrome 123, Safari 26.2, Firefox 152 (Baseline newly available June 2026).
applies: SaaS app UI (chat/AI composer, comment box).
check: the composer grows from 3 to 12 lines then scrolls, with no script measuring text.

text: Put every transition that moves or scales something inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`; opacity and colour fades may sit outside. Build the state change first and add motion inside the query; never strip motion afterwards with a global `0.01ms` rule.
why: Motion then exists only inside the query, so the default is none; people who never touched the setting match `no-preference` and see it. Script-driven animation checks the same query via `matchMedia`.
check: every `transform`/`translate`/`scale` transition is inside the query (the kit's `.press` transition currently sits outside and its `:active` is cancelled by a `reduce` block instead).

text: Define two easing tokens once and use them everywhere: `--ease-out: cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)` for anything entering, leaving or responding, and `--ease-in-out: cubic-bezier(0.77, 0, 0.175, 1)` for something already on screen that moves; never use `ease-in` on UI.
why: Ease-out starts fast so the interface moves while the user watches; ease-in starts slow and reads as lag; the built-in `ease-out` keywords are weak versions of the same shape. These are Emil Kowalski's curves, in the same family as the kit's `outQuint` `[.22,1,.36,1]` (the hero load-in tokens for Kaching still own the cinematic reveal; these tokens are for CSS-driven UI).
check: grep `ease-in[^-]` returns nothing in UI transitions; transitions name their properties.

text: Keep UI transitions at 300ms or less: press 100-160ms, tooltips and small popovers 125-200ms, dropdowns 150-250ms; modals and drawers 200-500ms. Name the properties; never `transition: all`.
why: Longer reads as sluggish and `all` animates properties nobody meant (layout, colours of children). The values match the engine's own motion table, which is the stricter source for hero choreography.
check: grep `transition: *all` returns nothing; computed `transition-duration` <= 0.3s except modal/drawer.

text: When one state change should drive several values together, register a typed custom property with `@property` (for example `<number>`, `<angle>`, `<length-percentage>`, `<color>`, with `syntax`, `inherits` and a required `initial-value`), set it in the state selector, derive the children with `calc()`, and transition only the property (`transition: --progress 0.3s var(--ease-out)`); a script only writes the variable.
why: An unregistered custom property is a string and cannot interpolate; registering it lets one transition and one easing drive rotation, scale and opacity in step, which is how Stripe's cards and sales page do it. `rotate`, `scale`, `translate` do nothing on an inline element (give it `inline-block`); a registration is global, so register each name once with a specific name. Support Chrome 85, Firefox 128, Safari 16.4.
applies: landing page (card hover choreography, conic-gradient border angle, spotlight position) and SaaS app UI.
check: one `@property` per driven value; hover state changes one variable, not eight declarations.

text: On cards that lift on hover, cross-fade two pre-painted shadows by opacity instead of transitioning `box-shadow`: `isolation: isolate` on the card; `::before` carries the resting shadow, `::after` the raised one at `opacity: 0`, both `inset: 0; z-index: -1; border-radius: inherit; pointer-events: none`; on hover swap the two opacities.
why: A `box-shadow` transition repaints every frame; each shadow here is painted once and only `opacity` animates on the compositor. The author's Chrome trace of one card showed 12 paint events versus about 78 for a plain shadow transition. The end state is exactly the raised shadow, not the sum of two. The card needs its own background; it consumes both pseudo-elements, so it cannot share them with the hit-area or card-link techniques; for a single small element transition `box-shadow` directly. The engine's founder shadow budget still applies to both layers (blur <= 24px, alpha <= 0.16), which the example's 32px / 0.16 raised layer exceeds.
applies: landing page grids of many cards, bento.
check: hover on a 12-card grid triggers no per-frame paint of the shadow (DevTools paint flashing); both layers satisfy founder shadow limits.

text: On multi-page sites enable cross-document view transitions with `@view-transition { navigation: auto }` on both pages; add slides only inside the reduced-motion query.
why: On a same-origin navigation the browser snapshots old and new pages and crossfades; unchanged parts such as the header appear to stay put, replacing a router or page-transition script. The default crossfade has no movement so needs no guard. Support Chrome 126, Safari 18.2, Firefox navigates normally (progressive enhancement).
applies: landing page (multi-page marketing site: home to pricing to blog).
check: both pages contain the rule; a navigation in Chromium crossfades.

text: Make the active-item indicator (tab underline, side-nav bar) with anchor positioning: `anchor-scope: --active` on the component root, `anchor-name: --active` on the item carrying `aria-current`, and a pseudo-element on the list with `position-anchor: --active`, `inset-inline-start: anchor(start)`, `inline-size: anchor-size(inline)`, transitioning those two properties.
why: The anchor follows the attribute, so there is no separate active class and no measuring script; a longer label, bigger font or wrapped line needs no new measurement; the bar is one element, so a plain transition slides it. Without `anchor-scope` two navs on one page both follow the last active item. For a vertical list swap axes (`anchor(top)`, `anchor-size(height)`). Give the active item a second cue (weight, colour) because a browser without anchor positioning drops the declarations. Support Chrome 131, Firefox 147 (places the bar but does not slide it), Safari 26; this entry was derived from Stripe's stylesheet only, no rendered Stripe example was found by the author.
applies: SaaS app UI tab rows; landing page sticky section nav on plain-HTML builds (React builds keep `layoutId`).
check: the bar's x and width match the `aria-current` item; works with two navs on one page.

text: Animate a sticky header's tone with registered `<color>` properties and a scroll timeline: `@property --header-ink / --header-ground / --header-accent` (syntax `<color>`, `inherits: true`), a keyframe animation from the light tone to the dark tone, `animation: linear both header-tone; animation-timeline: scroll(); animation-range: 0px var(--header-bar)`, and the header reading those variables.
why: It is how good-css.com's own header turns from lilac to near-black as you scroll, from the site stylesheet (verified in `assets/index-*.css`): no scroll listener, no class toggle, runs off the main thread, and the colours interpolate in sync with scroll distance. Where scroll timelines are missing (Firefox) the header stays in its initial state, so make the initial state a complete, legible design. [engine note] An adaptation of this for a Larpo nav means the pill bar fades to its scrolled state over the first ~80px.
check: `getComputedStyle(header).getPropertyValue('--header-ground')` changes between scrollY 0 and 80 in Chromium; header text contrast passes in both end states.

text: Animate dialogs, popovers and anything toggled with `display` natively: base state `opacity: 0` (plus `translate: 0 0.5rem` inside the reduced-motion query) with `transition: opacity, translate, display 0.2s allow-discrete, overlay 0.2s allow-discrete`; open state at opacity 1; and a `@starting-style` block after the open rule that restates the closed values. Give `dialog::backdrop` its own three states and transition.
why: `@starting-style` gives the browser a "before open" state to transition from when the element leaves `display: none` (entry); `allow-discrete` on `display` delays the switch to `none` until the other transitions finish (exit) and `overlay` keeps the element in the top layer meanwhile. The fade is not motion, so it runs for everyone. Never start from `scale(0)` (use `0.95` with opacity 0). Keep `[popover]:popover-open` out of the selector list that opens the dialog (a browser that does not know one selector drops the whole rule and the dialog would open at opacity 0); inside `@starting-style` a shared list is safe. Support: Chrome 117 both directions; **site-tested Safari 27 animates the entry but dialogs and popovers close at once**, an element toggled by a class animates both ways there; Firefox 129 entry only.
applies: SaaS app UI (dialog, popover, menu); landing page mobile menu.
check: a freshly opened dialog starts at opacity 0; backdrop fades with the panel; closing keeps it visible for the transition duration in Chromium.

text: Anchor dropdown menus and popovers to their trigger with the Popover API plus CSS: `<button popovertarget>`, `[popover] { margin: 0; margin-block-start: 0.5rem; position-area: block-end span-inline-end; position-try-fallbacks: flip-block, flip-inline, flip-block flip-inline }` inside `@supports (position-area: block-end)`.
why: `popovertarget` makes the button the anchor with no anchor names, `position-area` places the popover on a 3x3 grid around it and the fallbacks flip it when it would overflow the viewport, replacing a positioning library and `getBoundingClientRect()`. Use `span-*` values, never `center` (Adam Argyle: `center` stops the flips when the popover is wider than its grid cell); a script-opened popover has no anchor and lands top-left unless it passes the trigger as `showPopover({ source: button })`; without support the popover opens centred in the viewport. Support (site): Chrome 133, Firefox 147, Safari 26.
applies: SaaS app UI menus; landing page product dropdowns.
check: a menu at the viewport edge flips instead of clipping; `@supports` guard present.

text: Animate an accordion's height with `<details>`: `:root { interpolate-size: allow-keywords }`, `details::details-content { height: 0; overflow: clip }`, `details[open]::details-content { height: auto }`, and in the reduced-motion query `transition: height 0.3s var(--ease-out), content-visibility 0.3s allow-discrete`.
why: `::details-content` is the box wrapping everything except the summary; `interpolate-size` allows a transition to `auto`; transitioning `content-visibility` with `allow-discrete` keeps content rendered until the height reaches zero (without it the close snaps). Put padding on an element inside, never on `::details-content` (it would stay visible when closed); give siblings the same `name` for one-open-at-a-time; hide the marker with `list-style: none` plus `::-webkit-details-marker { display: none }`. `interpolate-size` is Chrome 129 only (the others open and close with no animation, which is the intended fallback); `::details-content` is Chrome 131, Safari 18.4, Firefox 143.
applies: landing page FAQ; SaaS app UI disclosures.
check: the FAQ keeps keyboard and find-in-page behaviour; padding is on an inner element.

text: For a dropdown or panel that opens over the page and whose height is unknown, unroll it with `clip-path` instead of animating `height`: closed `clip-path: inset(0 -3rem 100%); visibility: hidden`, open `clip-path: inset(0 -3rem -3rem); visibility: visible`, transition both over about 250ms.
why: `inset()` clips from each edge (top, sides, bottom), 100% at the bottom hides the whole box and the percentage refers to the element's own height so nothing measures it; the negative side and bottom insets leave room for the shadow while the top stays at 0 so no shadow shows where the menu meets its trigger; layout never changes; the clipped part takes no pointer events; `visibility` flips to hidden only when the close finishes, removing links from the tab order. Works in every browser. The negative inset must exceed the shadow blur plus offset; it is for overlapping panels (a closed panel in flow leaves a gap, so use the accordion technique there); credited to the Stripe nav menu.
applies: landing page mega-menu nav; SaaS app UI dropdowns.
check: a closed menu's links are not focusable; no `height` transition on the panel.

text: Build horizontal card rows on native scroll: `overflow-x: auto; scroll-snap-type: x mandatory; scroll-padding-inline` equal to `padding-inline`; children `flex: none; scroll-snap-align: start`; `overscroll-behavior-x: contain; scrollbar-width: none`; `scroll-behavior: smooth` only inside the reduced-motion query; arrow buttons call `scrollBy` one card width, with `Math.abs(scrollLeft)` and a direction sign for RTL.
why: The browser does scrolling and landing, so swipe, trackpad, keyboard and momentum all work before any script; `scrollBy` can only scroll the carousel (unlike `scrollIntoView`, which can scroll the page); `overscroll-behavior-x: contain` stops an end-of-row swipe from triggering browser back. Never move slides with `transform` or handle wheel/touch yourself. Chrome 135 can draw arrows and dots with `::scroll-button()` / `::scroll-marker`; Firefox and Safari cannot, so use the script.
applies: landing page testimonials, logo walls, feature rows.
check: swipe with no JS loaded works; snapped card x equals the page content edge.

text: Build modal, drawer, chat and sidebar bodies as a flex column with a limit (`max-block-size: 80dvh`), a body of `flex: 1; overflow-y: auto; overscroll-behavior: contain; scrollbar-gutter: stable`, and `min-block-size: 0` on any wrapper element between panel and body.
why: A flex item will not shrink below its content except a scroll container, whose minimum is zero; an intermediate form is not a scroll container and keeps content height, pushing the footer out unless it gets the zero minimum; `auto` shows a scrollbar only on overflow; `scrollbar-gutter` does not inherit, so the root declaration covers only the page. Give a fixed-height header or footer `flex: none`. Keep `min-height: 0` out of the global reset (it lets every item of a fixed-height column shrink under its own text).
check: with 100 items the footer stays visible; with 2 items the panel hugs content.

text: Fade the edges of a possibly-overflowing scroller only when it overflows: `mask-image: linear-gradient(to right, transparent, #000 var(--fade), #000 calc(100% - var(--fade)), transparent)` with `--fade: 0px` by default, and keyframes that set `--fade: 2rem` at both ends bound to `animation-timeline: scroll(self inline)`. To fade only the side with content left, register `--fade-start` and `--fade-end` as `<length>` and use keyframes `from {0, 2rem}`, `10%, 90% {2rem, 2rem}`, `to {2rem, 0}`.
why: A scroll timeline is inactive when nothing scrolls, so the animation has no effect and the default (no fade) applies; once content overflows the keyframes apply. A mask fades the content itself, so it works over any background (an overlay gradient must match the colour behind). Write `animation-timeline` after the `animation` shorthand (the shorthand resets it); declare defaults outside the keyframes; Firefox has no scroll timelines so the row scrolls without the fade. Support `animation-timeline` Chrome 115, Safari 26.
applies: SaaS app UI tab rows, toolbars, table wrappers, logo marquees.
check: a short row shows no fade, a long row shows it; mask present on the scroller, not an overlay element.

text: Set `html { scroll-padding-block-start: <header height> }` (one shared custom property with the header) so in-page anchors clear a sticky header; keep it outside the reduced-motion query and put `scroll-behavior: smooth` inside it.
why: The browser offsets every scroll to an anchor by that padding, with no script computing offsets; reduced-motion users still need the offset.

text: On app-like pages with fixed UI, disable the desktop rubber band with `html { overscroll-behavior-y: none }` and restore it under `@media (any-pointer: coarse) { html { overscroll-behavior-y: auto } }`; use the `-y` longhand and give inner scrollers `overscroll-behavior: contain`.
why: macOS trackpad overscroll stretches the whole page and drags fixed sidebars and headers; touch devices need the default for pull-to-refresh; `any-pointer` checks every input so a touchscreen laptop or a foldable keeps it; `overscroll-behavior-x: none` would also disable swipe-to-go-back; the viewport takes its behaviour from the root element only. Never use a `touchmove` listener with `preventDefault()`.
check: computed `overscroll-behavior-y` on `html` is `none` with a fine pointer.

text: On phone-like UI add `viewport-fit=cover` to the viewport meta and pad fixed headers, bottom bars, toasts and sheets with `env(safe-area-inset-*, 0px)` (inside `calc()` always with the `0px` fallback).
why: By default the browser keeps the page inside the safe area and leaves the notch and home-indicator zones as bare background; `cover` paints edge to edge and `env()` moves content clear while the background still fills the screen; without `cover` every inset is `0px`. Normal page content needs none of it.

text: Use three radius families in product UI: pill (fully rounded) for every action, badge, chip, tab-like pill and avatar; 8px for fields, list rows, cards, nav rows, small menus; 12px for dialogs, popovers and the command palette. Sub-element chrome steps down to 6px (kbd, menu items, 24px tiles), 4px (checkbox), 2px (meter container) and 1px (meter segments).
why: A short, fixed ladder means any two adjacent surfaces differ by a whole rung or are identical; there are no 7px/9px/10px neighbours to read as drift.
check: Collect `border-top-left-radius` of all bordered/filled elements; the set must be within {1,2,4,6,8,12,pill} (measured set also includes tile radii 5/12.5/14, see next rule).

text: Make actions pills and fields rectangles: buttons, icon buttons, filter pills, tags, count chips and the profile pill are `radius: 9999px`; inputs, selects, textareas, the date field are 36px tall with an 8px radius.
why: Shape tells role: a pill is something you press, a rounded rectangle is something you type in. The split is never broken in the file.
check: Every `button` radius is pill except nav rows, row-link buttons inside cells and notification items (8px); every `input`/`select-trigger` radius is 8px.

text: Give logo and app tiles a radius of 25% of their side (24px tile 6px, 32px 8px, 50px 12.5px, 56px 14px, the sidebar logo 32px rect rx 8).
why: A fixed proportion keeps the squircle character identical at every size so the same brand mark never looks like two different shapes.
check: `radius / width` of logo tiles = 0.25 (+-0.01).
source: command palette, profile sheet, detail sheet, New Company upload tile, sidebar header

text: Step an inner radius one rung below its container's rung instead of solving concentric geometry: popup 12px with 6px inner padding holds 8px rows; popup 8px with 4px padding holds 6px rows.
why: Strict concentric math (12 - 6 - 1 = 5px) produces odd values and breaks the ladder; the one-rung step stays optically right when the inset is 4-6px.
check: Child row radius equals the next-lower ladder value than its popup.

text: Draw segmented meters with a 2px container radius and 1px segment radius; checkboxes are 16px with a 4px radius.
why: Micro-radii scale with the object; a 1px segment inside a 2px track reads as one crisp bar, 4px matches the control scale below pills.
check: meter container `border-radius: 2px`, segments 1px; checkbox 16x16 at 4px.

text: Fix one height for every action control (30px) and a second for fields (36px): buttons, icon buttons, filter pills, profile pill, nav rows, dialog/sheet footer buttons are all 30px. Nothing is 28, 32 or 34.
why: A single height makes toolbars align on one baseline and lets controls sit side by side in any row without adjustment.
check: `getBoundingClientRect().height` of all `button` elements in header/toolbar/footers is 30 (+-0.5); inputs/selects 36.

text: Derive control height from content, not a height token: single-line label at `line-height: 1` plus equal vertical padding (12px text + 9px x2 = 30px; 12px icon + 9px x2 = 30px; 14px text with `height: 30px` and zero vertical padding for nav rows).
why: When height is the sum of line box and padding, text and icon are centred by construction; there is no half-leading to compensate for.
check: For buttons: `line-height == font-size`; `height == font-size + 2 * padding-top`.

text: Set `line-height: 1` on single-line UI text (nav, buttons, table cells, tags, captions) and let `display:flex; align-items:center` do the vertical centring; keep taller line-heights (about 1.15 at 14px) only for wrapped paragraphs.
why: Default 1.5 line-heights add uneven half-leading that shifts text relative to icons; line-height 1 gives a measured cap-centre offset of 0.03px at 14px and 0.26px at 12px.
check: `line-height / font-size == 1` on `button, th, td, nav a`; text cap-centre within 0.5px of container centre.

text: Size icons by the control they sit in: 12px inside 30px text buttons and pills (Export, New Company, filter chevrons, status badge); 14px for icon-only 30px buttons, nav rows and cell icons; 16px for the 24px close button and checkboxes; 12px dots in the 24px row action. Never scale an icon to "fill" the control.
why: A fixed icon-to-control ratio (about 0.4-0.47) keeps visual weight equal across the whole surface.
check: `svg` box size per container class: 12 or 14 or 16 only.

text: Make icon-only buttons exact squares (30x30 or 24x24) with zero padding and centre the icon with flex; the icon box centre must equal the button centre to 0.00px.
why: Any padding asymmetry or inline-svg baseline gap shows up as a visibly off-centre glyph at 2x; zero padding plus flex removes both.
check: For each icon-only button: |icon centre - button centre| <= 0.5px on both axes.
source: header icon buttons, row action buttons (24 measured, max glyph offset 0.29px)

text: Put a 6px gap between an icon and its label in buttons, nav rows and menu rows (4px only inside the 20px status badge, 2px between badge dot and text); centre the icon on the label's line box, not on the cap height.
why: Aligning to the line box (which is what flex centring does) matches the cap centre within 0.3px at these sizes and avoids optical hacks.
check: `column-gap: 6px` on button/nav; icon vertical centre - label line-box centre = 0.

text: Use one icon set drawn on a 14px grid with stroke width about 10% of the grid (1.4 at 14px), round caps and joins, `currentColor`, and set the svg size to the grid size at the control's tier; stroke then scales to 1.2px at 12px and 1.4px at 14px without per-icon overrides.
why: Stroke proportional to icon size keeps line weight consistent against 12px and 14px text; mixing sets or hand-set stroke widths is the usual source of "icons look off".
check: all `svg path` `stroke-width / viewBox width` within 0.083-0.1; one stroke-linecap value.

text: Keep text-only badges optically centred with a fixed height and symmetric ink padding: 22px tag, 8px padding plus 1px border on each side (measured ink 9/9), cap-centre offset 0.03px; 16px count chip with min-width 24px and 4px padding (ink 5/5).
why: A fixed 22px height at 14px/lh1 puts cap-centre on the box centre; the border is counted inside the padding budget so left and right are equal.
check: tag `height == 22`, `padding-left == padding-right`, text range left inset == right inset.
source: table segment tags, sidebar count chips

text: Reserve the width of a tab's bold state with an invisible bold copy of the label stacked on the visible one in the same grid cell, so activating a tab never shifts its neighbours.
why: Weight change widens text; without a reserve the row reflows on every click.
check: tab trigger width identical in active and inactive state.

text: Build spacing on a 4px grid with half-steps for tight pairs: 4/8/12/16/20/24 for padding and gaps between groups; 2/6/10 only as inner gaps (icon-label 6px, chip groups 4px and 8px, meter segment gap 2px). Odd values (1/3/9/11) appear only to cancel a 1px border so the outer size lands on an even number.
why: Measured spacing: 60% of 2,600 padding/margin/gap values are multiples of 4, 88% are even; the remaining odd 12% are 1/3 (hairlines), 9 and 11 (8 and 10 plus a border).
check: Frequency table of paddings/gaps: odd values only on elements that have a 1px border or on 1px dividers.

text: Use the same panel padding everywhere in overlays: 20px vertical and 24px horizontal for dialog sections, 20px all round for sheet sections, 16px for popover header, 12px for popover list items, 6px list inset; section gaps 16px; label-to-field gap 8px.
why: One panel rhythm means a dialog, sheet and popover read as the same product; users can scan section starts by the same distance each time.
check: Dialog fieldset padding 20/24, row gap 16; sheet section padding 20, gap 16 (12 in the score card section); popover list `ul` padding 6 gap 2.
source: New Company dialog, detail sheet, notifications

text: Give structural bars fixed heights and reuse them: sheet and popover header 56px, dialog header 77px (title + description), sheet footer 62px, dialog footer 63px (16 + 30 + 16 + 1 border), command input row 48px, command column header 36px, command footer 40px, table header 38px, table row 42px (43 with the 1px divider), tab row 45px.
why: Fixed bar heights stop content from changing chrome size and give the same vertical cadence across overlays.
check: Geometry table in section 3.10.

text: Align table header text edges with cell content edges using the same horizontal padding (12px) and the same justification per column: numeric columns right-justified in both `th` and `td`, text columns left, icon columns centred; give cell links a negative margin equal to their padding so the visible content still lines up with the header.
why: Header and cell share one grid (CSS subgrid), so column edges are identical by construction.
check: For each column: `th` and first-row `td` have equal box `left`/`width` and the same `justify-content`.

text: Align sidebar section eyebrows to the outer edge of the nav rows (both start at the 12px nav padding edge), not to the icons inside rows.
why: The eyebrow and the row pill share a left edge, so the active row's pill, the labels and the dividers form one column.
check: eyebrow `left == nav row left` (12px).

text: Run product UI on two working sizes: 14px for content, nav and fields, 12px for chrome (buttons, headers, captions, labels, menu items); add 16px only for titles and 24-28px only for hero numerals.
why: Two sizes with 2px difference stay distinguishable through weight and colour, which removes decision noise and keeps density high.
check: Distinct `font-size` among text elements <= 5, with 12 and 14 covering >= 85% of text nodes.

text: Use one variable family across the whole product UI (here Geist 100-900, `antialiased`), weights 400 for content, 500 for labels/nav/active tab/page title, 600 for dialog titles and one hero numeral; never 700+.
why: One family and three weights make weight the only variable, so hierarchy is legible at a glance.
check: `font-weight` in {400,500,600}; one `font-family`.

text: Keep tracking at `normal` for UI text; apply tracking only to the brand name (-0.01em) and to uppercase eyebrows (+1px at 12px, about +0.083em).
why: Tight tracking on small UI text hurts legibility; uppercase caps need positive tracking to stay readable.
check: `letter-spacing` is 0 except `text-transform: uppercase` (+1px) and brand text.

text: Set numerals in tables and money columns with tabular figures, right-aligned, header right-aligned too; prefix currency with a muted `$` and a space (the symbol is a separate lighter span); keep large single stats (28px/600, 24px/400) proportional.
why: Tabular digits make columns of values comparable at a glance; a muted symbol keeps the number the dominant element.
check: numeric `td` has `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` and `justify-content: flex-end`; matching `th` also flex-end.

text: Define section labels as one eyebrow style (12px, uppercase, +1px tracking, weight 400 in overlays and 500 in the sidebar) and use it for every grouping label (TEAM, CONTACT, PIPELINE HEALTH, SCORE CARD, COMPANY, OWNERSHIP & DEAL).
why: A single recognisable label style makes grouping obvious without borders or boxes.
check: all group labels share size/transform/tracking.

text: Express text hierarchy with five grey levels on a fixed ladder (primary `#f9fbff`, soft `#a4a4a4`, muted `#7f7f7f`, subtle `#676767`, faint `#454545`) and change colour on hover to the next level up, not a new hue; keep body-size text at >= 4.5:1.
why: Colour level encodes importance so size can stay constant; skipping contrast on small captions is a known weakness here (subtle 3.2:1, faint 1.87:1).
check: Measure each text colour on its surface; flag < 4.5:1 for <= 14px text.

text: Build a dark surface ladder from one near-black page colour with steps of 1-3 lightness points for panels (page `#161616`, sidebar `#171717`, sidebar header `#181818`) and larger steps for interactive layers (card `#1b1d20`, control `#1e1e1e`, raised/active `#2a2a2a`, hover `#333333`); never use pure black or a pure-white-based light surface.
why: Small steps between structural panels keep the page calm; bigger steps only where state changes, so the eye reads state not structure.
check: Computed backgrounds of page, panels, controls, active states form a monotonic ladder; panel-to-panel delta <= 3/255 per channel.

text: Separate regions with 1px hairlines at `#232323` and use `#393939` (about 16 points lighter) for anything that must stand on its own: popups, inputs, cards inside sheets, kbd; use white at 4-8% alpha for dividers inside components (the filter-pill split is 1px white/8).
why: Two border strengths express "structure" versus "object"; alpha dividers adapt to the surface under them.
check: Borders in {#232323, #393939, white/4-8%, tinted tag borders}; 1px width everywhere except the 0.5px count chip.

text: Give every raised control the same three-layer micro-shadow: 1px outer ring at 40% black, 1px top inset highlight at 10% white, 1px inner ring at 6% white; primary gets a richer stack (4px 4px drop at 32% grey, 1px near-black ring, top inset highlight 20% white 4px/6px blur, 1px inset ring 15% white, bottom inner shade 15% black 8px/14px).
why: An inset top highlight plus ring reads as a physical edge on dark without any visible blur; identical recipe means every control matches.
check: `box-shadow` of all secondary controls is the same string; primary has its own single string.

text: Reserve large shadows for overlays and use one token: `0 16px 40px rgba(0,0,0,.5)` plus a 1px `#0e0e0e` ring, paired with a 1px `#393939` border and a `rgba(0,0,0,.6)` scrim with a 6px backdrop blur; apply it identically to dialog, popover, menu, select popup and command palette.
why: A dark UI needs the border for edge definition and the shadow only for separation from the scrim; one token keeps every layer at the same height.
check: All overlay `box-shadow` strings identical; scrim `backdrop-filter: blur(6px)`.
source: all overlays. [engine note] This conflicts numerically with the founder's cards rule (blur <= 24px, alpha <= 0.16), which was written for light surfaces; scope that rule to light cards.

text: Colour semantic tags as tinted triplets (background about 12% saturated tint, 1px border one step lighter, text at 85-90% lightness of the same hue) from one token set of ten (blue, purple, green, moss, red, orange, amber, teal, yellow, neutral), each with measured text contrast 6.7-11.3:1.
why: Triplets guarantee readable contrast and consistent edge weight on dark, so ten colours still read as one family.
check: Each tag has bg, border, text from the same `--tag-<hue>-*` triplet; text contrast >= 4.5:1 on its bg.

text: Put a 1px inner outline at white/10% (inset by its own width) on every avatar and logo image so light photos do not bleed into the dark surface; give stacked or overlapping avatars a 2px ring in the surface colour.
why: A hairline defines the circle edge without adding a visible border; the surface-coloured ring cuts clean overlaps.
check: avatar element `outline: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.1)`, `outline-offset: -1px`.

text: Implement reduced motion at three layers: CSS (`@media`), JS libs (`MotionConfig reducedMotion="user"`, `useReducedMotion`, `gsap.matchMedia`), and media (autoplay video/Lottie/GIF).

text: Behaviour map under `reduce`:

Distance token trick: drive travel distances from a variable that collapses under reduce, so one keyframe serves both. [engine note] ```css :root { --travel: 16px; --reveal-ms: 600ms; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { :root { --travel: 0px; --reveal-ms: 200ms; } } @keyframes rise { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(var(--travel)); } } .hero > * { animation: rise var(--reveal-ms) var(--ease-out-expo) both; } ```

SSR-safe JS hook defaults to *reduced* on the server then corrects in an effect (Josh Comeau); in non-SSR apps read `matchMedia` synchronously. With Motion use `useReducedMotion()` (`boolean | null`).
Offer a site-level override where practical (Motion `reducedMotion={userSetting}`; GSAP `gsap.matchMediaRefresh()` after toggling).

Autoplaying/looping content longer than 5s next to other content needs a visible pause control (WCAG 2.2.2, Level A) regardless of OS setting; a mechanism that only stops while focused doesn't count; one control may serve the whole page. Preloaders can be "essential" when the user cannot interact during that phase.
check: any `animation-iteration-count: infinite` / looping video outside a loading indicator => needs control or `reduce` stop.

text: No flashing above 3 per second; avoid full-viewport strobe/fast alternating high-contrast transitions.

Vestibular triggers to avoid or isolate: parallax (differential speeds), large zoom/scale, full-screen slides, scroll-jacking, spinning/rotating large elements, swim/wobble effects, auto-scrolling carousels.
source: web.dev; WCAG 2.3.3; NN/g ("avoid flashing, parallax, scroll-jacking") (verified)

text: Motion is not the only information channel: pair with static cue; pair with focus management (focus moves to the new dialog/page heading regardless of animation).

Eliminate layout thrash: never interleave DOM reads (`offsetWidth`, `getBoundingClientRect`, `scrollTop`, `getComputedStyle`) with writes in loops; batch reads, then writes, in `requestAnimationFrame`; use FLIP (First-Last-Invert-Play) rather than animating geometry (Motion `layout` and GSAP Flip do it).
