text: Run the frequency test before writing any motion: 100+ times a day (keyboard shortcuts, command palette) = none; tens a day (row hover, list navigation) = remove or drop to a 100-150ms opacity or background-color change; occasional (modal, drawer, toast) = standard animation; rare or first-time (onboarding, empty state, success, celebration) = may add delight.
why: Delight fades with repetition while the delay cost stays; frequent motion makes the product feel slower than it is.
check: list every `transition`/`animation` on repeatedly-used controls (rows, tabs, menu items); only colour/opacity <=150ms remains.
source: emil-design-eng "Animation Decision Framework" + better-ui "High-frequency interactions get no animation" (also in craft-emil-kowalski)
section: 2.1 Whether, why, and how often to animate

text: Never animate a keyboard-initiated action: no open/close animation for a command palette, shortcut-toggled panel or arrow-key list highlight; the highlight moves instantly.
why: Hundreds of repeats a day; animation reads as lag between keypress and result. Emil's reference is Raycast, which has no open animation.
check: handlers bound to `keydown`/shortcuts toggle state with no transition on the result.
source: emil-design-eng "Should this animate at all?" (also in craft-emil-kowalski)
section: 2.1 Whether, why, and how often to animate

text: Give every animation a one-line purpose from this list: spatial consistency, state indication, explanation, feedback, or preventing a jarring appearance/disappearance. "It looks cool" on something seen often is not a purpose.
why: Purposeless motion is noise that repeats; the purpose also tells you the duration and easing.
check: DIRECTION.md or PR notes map each animated element to a purpose; unmapped ones are cut.
section: 2.1 Whether, why, and how often to animate

text: Pair every animated state change with a static cue (colour, icon or label); motion is never the only feedback channel.
why: Users with reduced motion, fast users who interrupt, and screenshots all lose the motion. better-ui escalates a motion-only state change to HIGH.
check: with `*{animation:none!important;transition:none!important}` injected, every state is still distinguishable.
section: 2.1 Whether, why, and how often to animate

text: Do not animate by default: add a transition only after naming the product moment it serves, and judge reviews by what was removed as much as what was added.
why: Quality comes from many deliberate decisions; AI makes adding effects free, so the missing filter is judgement.
check: `visual` review; count animated elements per viewport and justify each.
section: 2.1 Whether, why, and how often to animate

text: Reserve expressive motion (stagger, blur-in, morph, bounce) for infrequent moments: first load of a view, a success state, an empty state. Routine interactions get instant or <=150ms feedback.
why: Expressive motion is only special if rare.
check: `visual`; entrance choreography exists on first-load surfaces only, not on tab switches or row hover.
section: 2.1 Whether, why, and how often to animate

text: Match motion personality to the product: a professional dashboard is crisp and fast, a playful consumer product may be bouncier, and one library should use one easing family and one duration scale.
why: Cohesion makes motion read as identity; Sonner is deliberately a bit slower and uses `ease` because it fits its whole look.
check: a single token file for easings/durations (the kit's `motion.ts`); no stray literals.
section: 2.1 Whether, why, and how often to animate

text: Choose easing by this order: entering or exiting the screen = ease-out; moving or morphing while staying on screen = ease-in-out; hover / colour change = plain `ease`; constant motion (marquee, progress) = `linear`; when unsure = ease-out.
why: Ease-out front-loads movement, which is the moment the eye is watching, so it feels responsive.
check: computed `transition-timing-function` per role.
source: emil-design-eng "What easing should it use?" (also in craft-emil-kowalski)

text: Never use `ease-in` for UI that enters, exits or responds to a click. A 300ms `ease-in` dropdown feels slower than a 300ms `ease-out` one.
why: Ease-in is slow during the first frames, exactly when the user is looking.
check: grep `ease-in(?!-out)` and `cubic-bezier(.42,0,1,1)` in UI components.
source: emil-design-eng + emilkowal.ski "7 practical animation tips" tip 4

text: Prefer stronger custom curves over the weak CSS keywords. Emil's set: ease-out `cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)`, ease-in-out `cubic-bezier(0.77, 0, 0.175, 1)`, iOS drawer `cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1)`. Jakub's soft icon curve: `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)`. Take variants from easing.dev or easings.co instead of inventing.
why: Built-in curves lack punch; a strong ease-out is the cheapest way to make a stock animation feel designed.
check: tokens file defines named curves; no bare `ease-out` on hero/overlay motion.
source: emil-design-eng + better-ui "Cross-fade contextual icons" (also in craft-emil-kowalski)

text: Keep UI animation under 300ms: button press 100-160ms, tooltip/small popover 125-200ms, dropdown/select 150-250ms, modal/drawer 200-500ms. Marketing or explanatory motion may run longer.
why: A 180ms select feels more responsive than a 400ms one for the same result; a faster spinner even makes loading feel shorter.
check: computed durations of app components; flag >300ms except drawers/sheets and marketing.
source: emil-design-eng "How fast should it be?" (also in craft-emil-kowalski)

text: Make pressing slow only where the user is deciding and release always fast: a hold-to-confirm fill runs about 2s `linear` on press and snaps back in about 200ms `ease-out`.
why: Slow where the human is committing, fast where the system is responding.
check: distinct press vs release transition on hold controls.

text: Make exits shorter and smaller than enters: exit with opacity, 4px blur and a fixed -12px `translateY` over 150ms `ease-out`, never the full container height. Slide fully out only where the destination carries meaning (a drawer closing, a card returning to its list), around 200ms; remove instantly when motion adds no information.
why: The element already did its job; a loud exit steals attention from what comes next.
check: exit duration <= enter duration; exit translate magnitude <= 12px unless drawer/return.
source: better-ui "Exits are shorter and smaller than enters"; enter-exit.md

text: For a subtle drawer or panel exit, move to about -70% plus fade and 4px blur instead of sliding fully out; for the full version use a spring of duration 0.45, bounce 0, from `calc(-100% - 4px)`.
why: Partial exit keeps the motion legible without a long travel.
check: `visual`.
source: jakub.kr "Details that make interfaces feel better" (exit animations section)

text: Pressable elements scale on `:active`. better-ui: `0.96` over `150ms` `ease-out`; emil-design-eng: `0.97` over `160ms` `ease-out`; allowed band 0.95-0.98. Never below 0.95 (`scale-90`, `active:scale-95` flagged), and never on a disabled button (`enabled:active:` or `:not(:disabled):active`).
why: Instant physical feedback makes the UI feel like it is listening; a disabled control that squishes lies about being clickable.
check: computed `scale`/`transform` on `:active` in [0.95, 0.98]; none on `:disabled`.
source: better-ui "Press scales to 0.96"; emil-design-eng "Buttons must feel responsive". [engine note] founder-taste fixes the marketing CTA at 0.98 (Kaching), which is inside the band and wins on marketing buttons.

text: Give pressable components an opt-out for the scale (a `static` prop or a variant), for buttons where movement distracts, such as a submit that triggers a loading morph.
why: A scale on a button that is also animating its own content double-moves.
check: component API exposes the opt-out.

text: Animate only the transform property you mean: use the `scale` property (`transition-property: scale`) for press, not `transition: all` or a wide `transform` list.
why: Narrow property lists avoid animating colours on a theme flip and avoid layout work.
check: `transition-property` lists named properties.

text: Never animate in from `scale(0)`; start at 0.95 with opacity 0 (0.9-0.93 acceptable for larger surfaces; tooltips 0.97).
why: Nothing real appears from zero size; a barely-visible starting shape reads like a deflated balloon, not a conjuring trick.
check: grep `scale(0)`, `scale-0`, `initial={{ scale: 0`.
source: emil-design-eng "Never animate from scale(0)"; emilkowal.ski tip 2 (also in craft-emil-kowalski). [engine note] the kit's `Route` end-node (`scale: 0`) and Rails nodes break this; they are 7px SVG dots paired with opacity, a justified exception to record in DIRECTION.md.

text: Anchored popovers, dropdowns and menus scale from their trigger: `transform-origin: var(--transform-origin)` (Base UI) or the Radix `--radix-*-content-transform-origin` variable. Modals stay `center`.
why: The default centre origin is wrong for nearly every popover; the mismatch is most visible for top-right triggers.
check: computed `transform-origin` on popovers differs from 50% 50% and points at the trigger.

text: Tooltips: delay the first one; once one is open, neighbouring tooltips open instantly with no animation (`[data-instant]{transition-duration:0ms}` in Base UI). Tooltip transition 125ms `ease-out`, start/end opacity 0 and scale 0.97.
why: The initial delay stops accidental opens; removing it afterwards makes a toolbar feel faster.
check: hover tooltip A then B within 300ms: B has 0 delay and 0 duration.
source: emil-design-eng "Tooltips: skip delay on subsequent hovers" (also in craft-emil-kowalski)

text: Use a 2px blur on a crossfade only when two overlapping states read as two objects and easing/duration tuning failed; keep animated blur under 20px (blur is costly, especially in Safari).
why: Blur blends the old and new image into one perceived morph.
check: `filter: blur(` values <= 20px; used as a last resort.
source: emil-design-eng "Use blur to mask imperfect transitions"; emilkowal.ski tip 7 (also in craft-emil-kowalski)

text: Drive interactive state (hover, toggle, open/close, add/remove) with CSS transitions or springs, not keyframe animations, so it retargets and reverses when the user changes their mind mid-flight. Keep keyframes for sequences that run once (enters, loaders).
why: Transitions interpolate toward the latest state; keyframes follow a fixed timeline and snap or restart. This is better-ui's HIGH severity item.
check: grep `animation:` inside `:hover`, `.open`, `[data-open]`, `.active` toggled classes.
source: better-ui "Transitions, not keyframes"; emil-design-eng "Use CSS transitions over keyframes" (also in craft-emil-kowalski)

text: Use springs for drag with momentum, gestures the user can interrupt, elements that should feel alive, and decorative pointer tracking; set `bounce: 0` for everything functional. If bounce is used, 0.1-0.3, for drag-to-dismiss or playful products.
why: Springs keep velocity when retargeted; bounce in a work tool reads as toy-like.
check: grep spring configs; functional UI has `bounce: 0`.

text: Declare springs in duration-and-bounce form (`{ type: "spring", duration: 0.3, bounce: 0 }`; Emil's playful example is `duration: 0.5, bounce: 0.2`), reserving mass/stiffness/damping for when you need finer control.
why: Duration/bounce is easier to reason about and tune than physics parameters.
check: spring tokens use `duration`+`bounce`.
source: emil-design-eng "Spring configuration". [engine note] the kit's `spring` uses stiffness 420 / damping 36, which is a critically damped fit (bounce 0); keep it but also expose a duration/bounce token.

text: Decorative pointer-following (tilt, parallax, cursor glow) goes through a spring (`useSpring`), not a direct 1:1 mapping; for anything functional (a chart in a banking app) use no animation at all.
why: Direct mapping feels mechanical, springs add momentum; but decoration must not impede reading data.
check: `visual`.

text: Skip default-state animation on first render for toggles, tabs, icon swaps and segmented controls (`AnimatePresence initial={false}`), but never around an intentional staged entrance such as a hero.
why: Otherwise the resting UI animates in on every page load; the opposite mistake skips the hero choreography entirely.
check: full-page refresh: toggles do not animate; hero still does.
source: better-ui "Skip state animations on first render"

text: Use `mode="popLayout"` when an item leaves a flowing list, so the exiting item leaves document flow on the first frame and siblings reflow immediately.
why: Otherwise the list has a ghost-sized gap until exit finishes.
check: `visual` removing a row in a list.
source: better-ui icon-transitions.md (used on every swap) (also in craft-emil-kowalski)

text: Combine opacity and height changes for lists by trial: there is no formula; tune until the fade and the collapse feel like one move.
why: Opacity finishing before height closes (or the reverse) reads as a pop.
check: `visual` at 10% playback speed.

text: For a staged entrance, split content into semantic chunks (title, description, actions), stagger them 100ms apart, and enter each with opacity 0->1, 4px blur->0 and 12px `translateY` over 300ms ease-out. For word-by-word headlines use 80ms between words.
why: Sequence expresses hierarchy; short chunks are readable quickly; blur softens the rise.
check: per-chunk delays are multiples of 100ms (80ms for words) and total settles in about 1s.
source: better-ui "Stagger infrequent entrances by 100ms"; enter-exit.md. [engine note] the kit's Kaching tokens (70ms, 28px, 6px, 1.2s) are the shipped, founder-approved variant and win for heroes; use these numbers for in-app first-load panels.

text: Jakub's own site recipe for a hero enter: keyframes from `translateY(8px)`, `blur(8px)`, `opacity 0` over 800ms with `cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.46, 0.45, 0.94)` and `both` fill, delay = base x index; description as one block, buttons individually.
why: Slower and softer than the skill's default; suits a calm editorial/marketing page.
check: `visual`.
source: jakub.kr "Details that make interfaces feel better" (opinion; conflicts with the skill's 300ms default, see section 5)

text: Keep stagger gaps short (30-80ms for list items) and never block interaction while a stagger plays.
why: Long cascades make the page feel slow; stagger is decoration.
check: per-item delay <= 80ms; no `pointer-events:none` during the cascade.

text: Put the hidden state in the `from` keyframe (with `animation-fill-mode: both`), never `opacity:0` in a base rule that only an animation reveals.
why: If the animation never runs (reduced motion, JS failure, print) the content must still be visible.
check: grep base rules with `opacity: 0` and no matching `@keyframes ... from`.

text: To enter from `display: none` (popover, dialog), use `@starting-style` plus `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` and `transition-property: opacity, translate, display, overlay`; set the longer duration on the open state and the shorter on the closed state. Fall back to a mounted-flag `data-mounted` pattern where unsupported.
why: There is no prior style to interpolate from otherwise; separating open/closed durations gives free asymmetric timing.
check: popover CSS has `@starting-style`; `overlay` is Chromium-only so verify the Safari/Firefox fallback is an instant show.
source: better-ui enter-exit.md "Entering from display: none"; emil-design-eng "Animate enter states with @starting-style"

text: Cross-fade an icon that swaps on an infrequent state change (play/pause, copy/copied, like/liked): scale 0.25 -> 1, opacity 0 -> 1, blur 4px -> 0, spring `{ duration: 0.3, bounce: 0 }`. Without a motion library keep both icons in one grid cell and cross-fade 300ms with `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)`.
why: The overlap of shrinking and growing, blurred glyphs reads as one icon morphing rather than two swapping.
check: the icon button uses a grid-stacked pair or `AnimatePresence mode="popLayout"`.

text: Do not animate tab or navigation icon swaps, hover-revealed row actions, or decorative always-visible icons; those swap instantly or with a <=150ms opacity change.
why: They are high-frequency.
check: nav/tab icon components have no spring.

text: Animate icons in a toolbar that appears on selection, loading and success indicators; these are infrequent and benefit from the cross-fade.
why: They mark real state changes users should notice.
check: `visual`.

text: Use a clip-path duplicate for colour-inverting tab indicators: duplicate the tab row with active styling, clip it to the active tab, and animate the clip on change (also for hold-to-delete fills, image reveals with `inset(0 0 100% 0)` to `inset(0)`, comparison sliders).
why: Colour transitions on individual labels never line up with a moving indicator; a clip reveals the pre-coloured copy exactly.
check: `visual`; duplicate is `aria-hidden` with `tabindex=-1`.

text: Name the exact properties in `transition-property` (`scale, opacity`, `box-shadow`, `background-color`) and never write `transition: all` or Tailwind `transition-all`. Bare Tailwind `transition` is a curated list, still wider than most elements need.
why: `all` animates unintended properties (colours on theme flip) and re-runs layout on width/padding.
check: grep `transition:\s*all|transition-all`.
source: better-ui "Transition only what changes"; performance.md; emil-design-eng review checklist

text: Animate only `transform` (including `translate`, `scale`, `rotate`) and `opacity`; `filter` and `clip-path` with care. Avoid animating `width`, `height`, `padding`, `margin`, `top`, `left`.
why: Compositor properties skip layout and paint.
check: animated properties in computed transitions/keyframes.

text: Add `will-change` only after you see a first-frame stutter, name the property (`scale`, `transform`, `opacity`, `filter`), and never use `will-change: all`; never put it on layout or paint properties (`background-color`, `padding`, `top`). Note it makes the element a containing block for `position: fixed` descendants and creates a stacking context.
why: Each promoted layer costs memory; a will-change on a modal's ancestor breaks its fixed tooltip.
check: grep `will-change`.
source: better-ui "Name the animated property in will-change"; performance.md

text: While dragging or scroll-linking, write `element.style.transform` on the moved element directly; do not update an inherited CSS custom property on a parent of a large subtree, and in React write to `ref.current.style` rather than state.
why: An inherited variable forces style recalculation on every descendant; state causes a re-render per frame.
check: pointermove handler.
source: emil-design-eng "CSS variables are inheritable"; performance-cheatsheet.md (also in craft-emil-kowalski)

text: Prefer CSS (or WAAPI) for predetermined motion and JS libraries only for dynamic, interruptible motion; test motion while the page is still loading. Emil claims Motion's shorthand props (`x`, `y`, `scale`) run on the main thread and recommends the full `transform` string for GPU acceleration.
why: rAF-driven animation drops frames when the main thread is busy loading; CSS runs off-thread. Vercel's tab animation fixed this by moving to CSS.
check: record a trace of the hero load with CPU throttling and look for dropped frames in `Reveal`/`Word`.
source: emil-design-eng "Framer Motion hardware acceleration caveat"; "CSS animations beat JS under load" (contested, see section 5)

text: Use WAAPI (`element.animate`) for programmatic animation that needs CSS-level performance and interruptibility without a library.
why: Hardware accelerated and cancellable.
check: n/a.
source: emil-design-eng "Use WAAPI for programmatic CSS animations"

text: Suppress all transitions during a theme switch: inject `*,*::before,*::after{transition:none !important}`, force a style flush (`void document.body.offsetHeight`), remove the style after two `requestAnimationFrame`s. `next-themes` offers `disableTransitionOnChange`.
why: Otherwise every colour-transitioned element fires at once and the switch smears.
check: toggling theme shows no fade on borders/backgrounds.
source: better-ui "Suppress transitions on theme switch"; animations.md

text: Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, keep a short opacity cross-fade and remove movement, scale, blur and parallax; do not remove the element instantly. Pattern: base style transitions opacity 150ms; inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` add `translate, scale, filter` at 300ms.
why: Reduced motion targets vestibular triggers, not comprehension; a fade preserves the change cue.
check: emulate reduced motion: no transform or filter animation, opacity fades remain.
source: better-ui "Gate motion behind the reduced-motion preference"; animations.md; emil-design-eng "Accessibility"; better-accessibility motion-and-zoom.md

text: In Motion, `MotionConfig reducedMotion="user"` disables transform and layout animation but still runs `filter` (blur), so branch on `useReducedMotion()` wherever a recipe animates blur.
why: Blur in/out is motion for sensitive users and the global switch does not cover it.
check: grep `filter: 'blur` in motion props and confirm it is conditional.
source: better-ui animations.md "Reduced-motion fallback". [engine note] the kit's `reveal(..., {blur:true})` and `Word` currently animate blur under reduced motion; fix.

text: Disable (not merely reduce): parallax, autoplaying video/GIF/looping decoration, large travel. Replace: slide/scale/zoom with fades, smooth scroll with instant jump, auto-rotating carousels start paused. Keep: spinners, progress, instant hover/focus colour, press feedback.
why: Distinguishes vestibular triggers from feedback.
check: emulated reduced motion walkthrough.
source: better-accessibility motion-and-zoom.md "What to disable vs reduce"

text: Put hover styling behind `@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` (Tailwind 4's `hover:` already compiles under `hover: hover`; Tailwind 3's does not). Where a control draws its own pressed state, set `-webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent`.
why: On touch, `:hover` latches after a tap and looks like a stuck selected state.
check: grep `:hover` outside the media query in plain CSS; on an emulated touch device a tapped card does not stay in hover.
source: better-ui "Hover effects only on hover-capable pointers"; emil-design-eng "Touch device hover states". [engine note] kit components that set hover via `onMouseEnter` (`PillNav`) latch on touch too.

text: Anything that moves by itself for more than 5 seconds (muted looping hero video, ticker, auto-carousel) needs a visible pause control.
why: WCAG 2.2.2.
check: visible control exists.

text: Nested surfaces with a visible even inset use concentric radii: outer radius = inner radius + padding + border width (12 inner + 8 padding = 20 outer). Beyond about 24px of padding, or with deliberately asymmetric padding, treat the layers as separate surfaces.
why: Equal radii on nested rounded boxes make the gap look pinched at the corners.
check: for parent with padding p and child radius r: parent computed radius ~ r + p (+ border).
source: better-ui "Outer radius equals inner radius plus padding"; surfaces.md; jakub.kr. [engine note] the kit's `Frame` already does this (inner 16 + pad 6 = 22).
section: 2.9 Surfaces: radius, shadow, outline, optical alignment

text: Where a border exists only for depth, use a layered, transparent `box-shadow` ring instead. Light mode, three layers: `0 0 0 1px oklch(0 0 0/.06)`, `0 1px 2px -1px oklch(0 0 0/.06)`, `0 2px 4px 0 oklch(0 0 0/.04)`; hover steps to .08 / .08 / .06. Dark mode keeps one ring `0 0 0 1px oklch(1 0 0/.08)`, hover .13. Transition `box-shadow` 150ms ease-out.
why: Transparent layers adapt to any background (photos, gradients), a solid border colour does not; depth shadows vanish on dark so dark mode needs only a white ring.
check: computed card `box-shadow` has 3 layers in light, 1 in dark; no solid border colour used for elevation.
source: better-ui "Shadows for elevation, borders for structure"; surfaces.md "Shadow recipes"; jakub.kr
section: 2.9 Surfaces: radius, shadow, outline, optical alignment

text: Under every shadow ring keep `border: 1px solid transparent`.
why: Forced-colors mode removes `box-shadow`; the transparent border is painted instead, and keeps the box size equal to the border it replaced.
check: elements with shadow ring have a transparent border.
section: 2.9 Surfaces: radius, shadow, outline, optical alignment

text: Keep real borders for dividers, separators, table cells, selected states and form inputs (input boundary needs 3:1 non-text contrast).
why: Those borders carry structure, not depth.
check: inputs have a contrasting border.
source: better-ui "Shadows for elevation, borders for structure"
section: 2.9 Surfaces: radius, shadow, outline, optical alignment

text: Give content images (photos, screenshots, avatars) a 1px inset outline in pure black or white at 10% opacity: `outline: 1px solid oklch(0 0 0 / .1); outline-offset: -1px`, white at .1 in dark mode. Never a tinted neutral, palette near-black or the accent colour; skip transparent artwork such as logos.
why: Tinted outlines show as a coloured fringe on the image edge; an outline never changes layout size, unlike a border, and follows the corner radius.
check: `img` outline colour is `rgba(0,0,0,.1)` or `rgba(255,255,255,.1)`, offset -1px.
source: better-ui "Outline images in pure black or white"; surfaces.md "Image outlines"
section: 2.9 Surfaces: radius, shadow, outline, optical alignment

text: In a button with an icon, give the icon side about 2px less padding than the text side (for example `ps-4 pe-3.5`), and judge by eye.
why: Equal padding makes the icon look pushed outward.
check: `visual`: crop the button and compare optical margins.
source: better-ui "Align optically where geometry looks off"; surfaces.md
section: 2.9 Surfaces: radius, shadow, outline, optical alignment

text: Nudge play triangles about 2px toward their point (physical `translateX(2px)`), and fix asymmetric glyphs (stars, arrows, carets) in the SVG path or `viewBox`; only nudge the wrapper when the asset cannot change.
why: A triangle's geometric centre sits left of its visual centre.
check: `visual` on icon buttons at 2x.
section: 2.9 Surfaces: radius, shadow, outline, optical alignment

text: The same surface detail must not be done two ways in one project (two radii for the same card, two shadow recipes); a deliberate project convention is preference, inconsistency is a finding.
why: Polish reads as consistency.
check: grep distinct radius/shadow values per component family.
section: 2.9 Surfaces: radius, shadow, outline, optical alignment

text: Match icon stroke to the adjacent text weight, in rendered pixels: 1.5px beside regular (400) 14-16px text, 2px beside medium/semibold (500-600), 2.5px beside bold or an emphasised standalone icon. Scaled SVGs shrink stroke (24px grid drawn at 16px paints `stroke-width="2"` as about 1.33px), so use the library's absolute-stroke option or `vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke`.
why: Mismatched stroke and weight makes icon and label look drawn by different hands.
check: rendered stroke width of icons next to labels vs the text `font-weight`.
source: better-ui "Match icon stroke to text weight"; icons.md

text: Use one icon library per surface; size inline icons 1em-1.25em of the adjacent text; use the 16/20/24 grid that matches the render size; test recognisability at 16px; always SVG.
why: A 24px drawing scaled down lands off the pixel grid and renders soft.
check: one icon package per page; sizes in the grid.

text: Draw icons with `currentColor` and take hover, selected and disabled from CSS colour and opacity (disabled about 0.4); strip hard-coded `fill="#..."` / `stroke="#..."` on import.
why: One asset recoloured by state keeps variants in sync.
check: grep `fill="#` in icon SVGs.

text: Use outline as the default icon state and fill as the active/selected state (active tab, toggled bookmark, liked heart); cross-fade only for infrequent toggles, swap instantly for tabs.
why: The variant becomes a state cue that survives without colour.
check: active nav item uses solid variant.

text: Under `dir="rtl"` mirror only icons whose meaning follows reading direction (back/forward arrows, nav chevrons, list/indent glyphs, send); leave logos, checkmarks, physical objects and media playback alone; use one flip mechanism per element.
why: Two flips compound back to unflipped.
check: `[dir=rtl]` screenshot.

text: Apply `text-wrap: balance` to headings and short descriptions (not paragraphs; Chromium ignores it past about 6 lines) and `text-wrap: pretty` to paragraphs to avoid a single word on the last line.
why: Even line lengths read as designed; orphans read as unfinished.
check: computed `text-wrap` on `h1-h3`, `p`.
source: better-typography "Wrap deliberately"; jakub.kr "Details that make interfaces feel better"
section: 2.11 Type details (from better-typography, which better-ui defers to)

text: Use `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` on counters, timers, prices and numeric table columns (not prose); right-align numeric columns. Some fonts (Inter) change numeral shapes when it is on, so check the face.
why: Changing digits otherwise shift neighbours sideways.
check: computed `font-variant-numeric` includes `tabular-nums` on number cells and `CountUp`.
source: better-typography "Tabular numbers on changing values"; jakub.kr
section: 2.11 Type details (from better-typography, which better-ui defers to)

text: Set `-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased` (and `-moz-osx-font-smoothing: grayscale`) once on the root, never per component.
why: Thinner, crisper text on macOS; per-component values drift.
check: exists on `body`/`html` only.
section: 2.11 Type details (from better-typography, which better-ui defers to)

text: Line-height by role: display 1.1, headings 1.2-1.3, body 1.5-1.6, always unitless; anything that can wrap to 3+ lines is at least 1.4. Letter-spacing in `em`: headings from 24px up -0.01em to -0.02em, uppercase labels at 14px or less +0.05em, body 0.
why: Fixed px leading breaks when font size changes; tight leading is for short text.
check: computed line-height ratio per role.
source: better-typography "Line-height by role", "Letter-spacing by size". [engine note] the kit's h1 is -4.5% (founder-approved), tighter than this band for 72px display; heroes are the exception.
section: 2.11 Type details (from better-typography, which better-ui defers to)

text: Below 18px use weight 400 or heavier; weights 100-300 only at 28px+ and checked on the background. Cap long-form measure at 60-75 characters. Rarely more than three fonts.
why: Light weights fall apart at small sizes; long lines lose the eye.
check: computed weight vs size; `max-width` in `ch`.
source: better-typography "Fewer fonts, sizes and weights", "Cap the measure"
section: 2.11 Type details (from better-typography, which better-ui defers to)

text: Inputs render at 16px minimum on mobile (iOS Safari zooms the page below 16px): either `text-base sm:text-sm`, or keep 16px and shrink with `transform: scale()` inside a wrapper that draws the field surface.
why: iOS auto-zoom on focus breaks the layout.
applies: SaaS app UI, landing page (email capture).
check: computed input font-size >= 16 at 375px.
section: 2.11 Type details (from better-typography, which better-ui defers to)

text: Use typographic punctuation in rendered strings: curly quotes, en dash in ranges, em dash for asides, the `...` ellipsis character `…`, and non-breaking spaces between value and unit. Store text in natural case and apply case with `text-transform`.
why: Keyboard stand-ins look unfinished; natural-case storage survives redesigns.
check: grep rendered strings for `...`, ` -- `, straight quotes.
section: 2.11 Type details (from better-typography, which better-ui defers to)

text: Use `font-weight` and `font-variant-numeric` properties, not raw `font-variation-settings`/`font-feature-settings` tags; leave `font-optical-sizing: auto`; load every face the design uses so the browser does not synthesise weights.
why: Properties keep working when a non-variable fallback renders; synthesised faces look distorted.
check: grep `font-variation-settings`, `font-feature-settings: "tnum"`.
source: better-typography "Properties over raw tags", "Load the faces the design uses"
section: 2.11 Type details (from better-typography, which better-ui defers to)

text: Trim text-box in tight components (`text-box: trim-both cap alphabetic`) as progressive enhancement to remove the extra space above caps in buttons and badges.
why: Font metrics reserve space that makes labels sit low (Chromium 133+, Safari 18.2+).
check: visual centring of label in 32-40px controls.
source: better-typography "Trim text boxes in tight containers"
section: 2.11 Type details (from better-typography, which better-ui defers to)

text: Keep targets at least 24x24 (WCAG AA), aiming for 44x44 on touch; if the visible element is smaller, expand the hit area with a pseudo-element on a wrapper or the `<button>` (not on the `<input>`), centred with `top/left:50%` and `translate(-50%,-50%)`. Shrink the pseudo-element where it would collide with a neighbour; two 20px targets need a 4px gap.
why: The visible size can stay small while the hit area stays usable; form controls do not render pseudo-elements reliably.
check: computed bounding box (or pseudo-element box) >= 24px (44px touch); no overlapping hit areas.
section: 2.12 Hit areas, focus, targets, timed UI (from better-accessibility)

text: Give each decorative layer over interactive content (scrim, glow, sheen, full-bleed `::after`) `pointer-events: none`; leave it on a layer the user must hit (a dismissing modal scrim).
why: Invisible layers swallow clicks: the control looks live and does nothing.
check: `elementFromPoint` at each CTA centre returns the CTA.
section: 2.12 Hit areas, focus, targets, timed UI (from better-accessibility)

text: Keep the browser focus ring or define one explicitly: `:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid <token>; outline-offset: 2px }`; never `outline:none` without a replacement; check the ring's contrast against every surface it crosses.
why: Keyboard users need to see where they are; bare `currentColor` outlines can fail on coloured surfaces.
check: tab through the page; ring visible on every control.
section: 2.12 Hit areas, focus, targets, timed UI (from better-accessibility)

text: Pad sticky chrome: `scroll-padding-top` equal to the sticky header height (and `scroll-padding-bottom` for sticky footers/banners), plus `scroll-margin-top` on anchor targets.
why: Focused or jumped-to elements otherwise land hidden behind the header.
check: Tab to a form field under a sticky header: it is visible.
section: 2.12 Hit areas, focus, targets, timed UI (from better-accessibility)

text: Give scrollable dialogs, drawers, menus and side panels `overscroll-behavior: contain`.
why: Scrolling past the end otherwise scrolls the page behind.
check: computed `overscroll-behavior` on overlays with `overflow:auto`.
section: 2.12 Hit areas, focus, targets, timed UI (from better-accessibility)

text: Toasts: use auto-dismiss only for low-stakes confirmations; a toast that carries an action, an error or information the user may need stays until dismissed; if it times out, at least 5 seconds, paused while hovered or focused; never put the only link to an undo in a timed toast.
why: A vanished toast with the only undo is data loss on a timer.
check: toast config has hover/focus pause and persistent variant for error/action.
section: 2.12 Hit areas, focus, targets, timed UI (from better-accessibility)

text: Group with space first, background shapes second, hairline separators last; the gap between groups is at least 2x the gap within a group (8px inside, 16px+ between).
why: Proximity carries the structure; lines used to compensate for uniform spacing add noise.
check: measure inter-group vs intra-group gaps.

text: Controls must look different from content: action text gets a background, border, underline or consistent placement; a non-clickable badge shaped like the buttons beside it collects dead clicks.
why: Affordance.
check: `visual`.

text: Use logical properties for anything that mirrors (`ms-4`, `pe-6`, `text-start`, `inset-inline-start`); `translateX` and `background-position` have no logical form and need `[dir=rtl]` overrides.
why: Physical left/right breaks in RTL.
check: grep `ml-|mr-|pl-|pr-|text-left`.

text: Prefer `100dvh` over `100vh` on full-height mobile panes, `width:100%` over `100vw`, `minmax(0,1fr)` / `min-width:0` for tracks holding long text, container queries inside reusable components; size text containers with `min-height`/`max-width`, never fixed height.
why: Avoids toolbar/keyboard overlap, horizontal scroll from scrollbar width, and grid blowout.
check: grep for `100vh`, `100vw`, fixed `height` on text boxes.

text: Give each view one primary action; once secondary actions exceed 3 put them behind a menu.
why: Focus and decision speed.
check: count of primary-styled buttons per viewport = 1.

text: Buttons: pressed scale (2.3), named-property transitions (`transition-[scale,background-color]`), `static` opt-out, a loading state that morphs content (with 2px blur on the cross-fade if it looks like two objects), and hover colour only on hover-capable pointers.
why: The sum of these is what a polished button feels like.
check: component source has `:active` scale, no `transition-all`, loading variant.
section: 2.14 Component craft (buttons, inputs, menus, toasts, drawers)

text: Menus and popovers: origin-aware scale from 0.95 with opacity, 125-200ms ease-out in, shorter out; item hover is a <=100ms background change (or none); keyboard navigation moves highlight instantly; open/close not animated if the menu is a high-frequency right-click or command surface.
why: Combines the frequency, origin and speed rules; Jakub's macOS context menu example animates only closing and skips item hover colour.
check: computed transition per state.
section: 2.14 Component craft (buttons, inputs, menus, toasts, drawers)

text: Toasts (Sonner pattern): enter from `translateY(100%)` via a mounted flag or `@starting-style` with a CSS transition (about 400ms `ease`), leave in the same direction, stacked toasts offset about 14px with scale 1 - 0.05 x index, 4s default lifetime paused on hover and on `document.hidden`, bridge gaps with a pseudo-element, imperative API with one mount point.
why: Same-direction enter/exit makes swipe-to-dismiss intuitive; transitions survive rapid adds; hidden-tab pause prevents missed toasts.
check: `visual` + timers.
source: emil-design-eng "The Sonner Principles" (also in craft-emil-kowalski). [engine note] the 4s default conflicts with the accessibility rule in 2.12 for action/error toasts; follow 2.12.
section: 2.14 Component craft (buttons, inputs, menus, toasts, drawers)

text: Drawers and sheets: use `translateY(100%)`/percentage translates instead of pixel values; `cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1)` at around 500ms for finger-driven sheets; damping past the boundary; ignore extra touches after the first.
why: Percentages adapt to content height; the iOS curve plus damping feels native.
check: computed curve; test on a physical device.
source: emil-design-eng "CSS Transform Mastery", "Gesture and Drag Interactions" (also in craft-emil-kowalski)
section: 2.14 Component craft (buttons, inputs, menus, toasts, drawers)

text: Ship good defaults over options and handle edge cases invisibly (pause timers when the tab is hidden, bridge hover gaps, capture pointer during drag); users never notice and that is the goal.
why: Most users never customise; the default is the product.
check: review checklist.
section: 2.14 Component craft (buttons, inputs, menus, toasts, drawers)

text: Dismiss by velocity as well as distance: dismiss if `abs(distance) >= threshold` or `abs(distance)/elapsedMs > 0.11`; apply damping/friction past the boundary rather than a hard stop; call `setPointerCapture` once a drag starts; ignore additional touch points after the drag begins.
why: A flick should be enough; invisible walls and finger-switch jumps feel broken.
check: drag handler has velocity branch, capture, multi-touch guard.
source: emil-design-eng "Gesture and Drag Interactions" (also in craft-emil-kowalski)

text: Swipe rows (Jakub's iOS-style example): `drag="x"` with `dragElastic` about 0.05 and `dragMomentum={false}` so the row lands on snap points (-116, 0, +116 px); commit threshold 58px; reveal action 1 at 44px and action 2 at 88px (pixel thresholds, not percentages); action buttons enter from opacity 0 / scale 0.5; indicators scale 0.75 with the origin at their corner; spring 0.3s bounce 0.
why: Fixed snap points make the outcome predictable; pixel thresholds are easy to tune.
check: `visual` on device.

text: Give every drag a single-pointer alternative (move up/down buttons, a menu) and set `touch-action: none` only on the surface that implements its own gesture, not at page level.
why: WCAG 2.5.7 and 2.5.1; page-level `touch-action:none` disables scrolling.
check: keyboard path exists for reorder.

text: With shared layout animations give each moving element its own `layoutId`, keep elements that should not fade outside `AnimatePresence`, and pass animated border radius through `animate`, not `className`.
why: Same `layoutId` on two elements in one state breaks the animation; className radius cannot interpolate.
check: `PillNav` / `Segmented` unique ids; radius set in `animate` where it changes.

text: Report review findings as a table `Severity | Location | Before | After | Why` grouped by the violated principle, one row per root cause, and finish with Block (any HIGH remains) or Approve; mark checks you could not run as Not verified.
why: Forces specificity and prevents approving unseen coverage.
check: review output format.

text: Review animations at 10% speed (DevTools Animations panel) or 2-5x duration, frame by frame, on a real device for touch, and again the next day; check colour crossfades, easing starts, `transform-origin`, and sync of coordinated properties.
why: Timing drift between coordinated properties is invisible at full speed.
check: the ledger entry says it was slow-motion reviewed.
source: better-ui "Verification"; emil-design-eng "Debugging Animations", "Review your work the next day"

text: Detection table to run mechanically before finishing: padded parent + child with equal radius; `box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px` ring without transparent border; `outline-slate/zinc` or hex on `img`; `transition-all`; `animation` on a toggled class; `active:scale-95`/`scale-90`/`whileTap` below 0.96; scale on `:active` without `:disabled` exclusion; `bounce` != 0; transform/filter animation without reduced-motion gate; colour transitions with a theme toggle and no suppression; `will-change: all`; hex `fill`/`stroke` in icon SVG; `:hover` outside `@media (hover: hover)`; overlay with `overflow:auto` and no `overscroll-behavior`.
why: Each is a known regression pattern with a one-line fix.
check: add as grep checks in `tools/check.mjs` (see section 8).

text: [founder-ref] Before building, pick the page's world from a different family than the last two accepted builds: image-led (engraving, painting, photo, generative scene), product-led on plain canvas, type-led, or object-led. Never ship two consecutive builds from the same family.
why: Founder: "you're a bit repetitive... we need a lot of different styles and aesthetics" (after Kestrel and Margin, both product-led on a plain grey canvas).
check: DIRECTION.md names the family and the last two builds' families.

text: [founder-ref] In an image-led hero, keep the art behind a crisp white product surface and keep the headline over the quietest part of the image (sky, mist, paper); text contrast is measured against the actual pixels behind it.
why: Native, the CRM and Xenora all keep copy on the calm zone and the product on solid white; busy art behind text kills legibility.
check: sample the pixels behind the h1 box: contrast >= 4.5:1 for subtitle, >= 3:1 for the h1.

text: [founder-ref] A framed page (site as a rounded sheet on a backdrop) uses a 12-20px backdrop margin, 16-24px sheet radius, and a backdrop that belongs to the brand world (tint, painting, photo); the nav and hero live inside the sheet.
why: Xenora (pale blue margin) and Aakib's HR and finance pages (painting / photo margin) read as presentations; the margin is part of the identity.
check: body background differs from the sheet; sheet offset 12-20px; radius 16-24.

text: [founder-ref] Mono voice: when the brand is operational or technical, set nav links, primary buttons and section tags in uppercase mono at 12-13px with +2-4% tracking, paired with a grotesk display; keep body copy in the grotesk.
why: Xenora's mono nav and buttons give an operator tone at a glance; mono body copy would tire.
check: nav/button font-family is mono and text-transform uppercase; body p is not mono.

text: [founder-ref] Sharp-control brands use 2-6px radii on buttons and inputs and keep cards at 8-14px; do not mix pill buttons into a sharp system.
why: Xenora's and LaunchKit's square buttons are a deliberate counterpoint to soft SaaS pills.
check: button radius <= 6 when the system is sharp.

text: [founder-ref] A workflow product shows a node canvas: dotted grid at 16-24px, 3-5 node cards with title, sub-line and 2-3 rows, connectors with small status chips ("Success"), an inspector panel, and a cursor or selection mid-action.
why: Xenora proves "automation" in one look by showing the flow, not a dashboard of numbers.
check: visual: nodes connected, at least one status chip, one live selection.

text: [founder-ref] Use-case bento in greyscale: one motif per tile (concentric rings around a dark node, wired avatars, single-line chart with a dark value pill and cursor, branch card), one status colour across the whole grid, tile title centred under the visual.
why: Opero's grid feels designed because every tile shares a monochrome language and differs only in motif.
check: saturated pixels in the bento < 3%; one accent hue.

text: [founder-ref] Honest proof grids may alternate real logo or category tiles with diagonally hatched empty tiles; never fill gaps with invented customer logos.
why: Xenora's hatched tiles imply breadth without fake proof; fits the engine's never-invent-proof rule.
check: every logo shown is real and permitted, or tiles show categories.

text: [founder-ref] A statement footer (giant wordmark, cropped by the sheet edge, on ink) is allowed once per brand as the closing beat; keep link columns small above it.
why: LaunchKit's cropped wordmark ends the page with identity instead of a link dump.
check: wordmark >= 160px and cropped by the container.

text: Headline 48-64px at 1440 is the default; to be distinctive, go to <=40px *or* >=84px, never in between. Cap fluid type (`clamp`) at 64px for default-range sites; sites above 80px scale with vw (Darkroom ~13.9vw, Pitch, Granola, Notion).
why: 48-64 is the shared template zone (25% to 75% quartiles = 48 to 64).
check: computed `font-size` of the hero headline.

text: Headline line-height 0.9-1.15 (median 1.07), never the 1.3+ body ratio. Below 0.95 only above ~64px (Pitch 0.8, Darkroom 0.8, Granola 0.93).
why: large display type reads as a shape; leading is the gap between lines, which looks wider as size grows.
check: `lineHeight / fontSize` on h1; flag >1.25.

text: Headline tracking -0.02em as default, tightening to -0.04..-0.06em for big/regular-weight display (Vercel -0.06 at 64px/400; Notion -0.048 at 96px/600; Resend h2 -0.05 at 56px). Positive tracking only for uppercase/mono/labels (Rive +0.01, TBC +0.15em, Darkroom labels).
why: large type opens up optically; tight tracking restores density.
check: `letterSpacing / fontSize` on h1/h2.

text: h2 about 0.74x the h1 (IQR 0.64-0.81); absolute median 44px (range 24-56). Section heading size changes <=1 step across the page (Linear: 48 on all four chapters).
check: h2/h1 and distinct h2 sizes per page.

text: Hero lede 16-20px (median 18), lh 1.3-1.5, colour at 60-70% of the ink (Linear `#8a8f98` on `#08090a`; Resend `#a1a4a5`); column 350-640px, not the container width.
why: muted contrast makes the headline the first read.
check: lede colour contrast vs headline (1.5-2.2x less).

text: Nav height 64px (IQR 64-72; range 42-102 incl. banners), sticky or fixed, transparent or bg-matched, with a 1px hairline or `backdrop-filter: blur(16-20px)` *or* nothing; link text 13-16px at weight 400-500. Reserve tall navs (>=96) for brand devices (Arc's 96px blue bar).
check: `getBoundingClientRect().height` of the fixed/sticky ancestor of `header`.

text: Hero primary CTA height 38-48px (median 41; range 34-58), 14-16px label, weight 400-600. Radius is one of {pill 7 of 22, 5-8px 7, <=4px 4, 9+px 4}. Pick one radius and use it for CTAs, inputs and chips together.
check: CTA `height`, `border-radius`; consistent across button/input/chip.

text: Content container 1200-1360px at 1440 (median 1274, range 1048-1392), expressed as `max-width` ~1280 + 24-40px side padding. Narrow text columns inside it: hero text 480-740px.
check: width of h1 ancestor chain.

text: Section vertical padding 96-128px (median 104, range 60-160); the set clusters on 96 / 120 / 128 / 160. Keep it uniform across sections (Resend 96 x9, Linear 128 x4 with near-identical section heights 1220-1232px, Framer 120).
check: padding-top/bottom of top-level `section`s; stdev across them.

text: Card radius 8-16px (median 12; 29 sites: min 4, max 24); controls 4-8px; pills only for chips/CTAs. Nested radius = outer minus padding.
check: histogram of `border-radius` on elements >180x100.

text: Borders: 1px at 6-12% white on dark, `#e5e5e5`-class on light; shadows only for floated media/popovers (Cursor `0 28px 70px .14`; Stripe `0 30px 45px -30px` tinted `50,50,93`).
check: count of non-"none" box-shadow vs 1px borders.

text: Type scale is small and sparse: 7-21 distinct font sizes sitewide (median ~11); Vercel uses 7, PostHog/Neon/Dub ~20.
check: `new Set(computed font-sizes)`.

text: Pair a display voice with a mono or utility voice: a monospace face is loaded on ~25 of 38 sites (Linear Berkeley Mono, Cursor Berkeley, Vercel Geist Mono, Resend Commit Mono *outweighing* its body font, Rive/Tomorrow, Darkroom mono at weight 200).
check: `@font-face` families.

text: Motion: transitions 150-300ms (200ms is the mode), `ease-out` or a strong bezier: `cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)` (Anthropic, Ramp, OpenAI), `(.22,1,.36,1)` (OpenAI, v0), `(.32,.72,0,1)` (Linear, Granola, Supabase), `(.25,1,.5,1)` (Stripe), `(.23,1,.32,1)` (Raycast, Locomotive), `(.33,1,.68,1)` (Clerk, Mercury). Reserve >=500ms for entrances and decorative loops.
check: parse `transition-duration` and `-timing-function`.
source: measured n=40 (top durations 200ms x31, 150 x26, 300 x21, 400 x8, 100 x8).

text: Responsive headline: size at 390px is 0.44-0.89x desktop (median 0.63x); big-type sites scale continuously (Notion 42 -> 89.7 @1024 -> 96; Granola 48 -> 68 -> 110; Darkroom 104 -> 142 -> 267) while default sites step and cap (Vercel/Linear/Stripe cap at 64/64/48 beyond 1440).
source: measured n=24. One site (Mercury) had horizontal overflow at 1024 and 1920: verify `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`.

text: Use `text-wrap: balance` on headings: present in 33 of 40 CSS bundles (Notion 84 uses, OpenAI 99, Vercel 41, Linear 28).
check: computed `text-wrap` on h1/h2.

text: Only semantic tokens (or Tailwind utilities that resolve to them) appear in generated markup/CSS. Zero raw `#hex`, zero arbitrary `[13px]`, zero `style="padding: 14px"` outside a token-definition file.
why: Raw values are where inconsistency enters; this is the single most enforced rule in Primer's agent guide.
check: regex over generated CSS/HTML for `#[0-9a-f]{3,8}`, `\[\d+px\]`, inline `style=` px values; allowlist = token files.

text: Name pattern: `category.role[.variant][.size]` in JSON; CSS var = dots to hyphens (`space.stack.md` -> `--space-stack-md`). Surface tokens come with `-foreground` partners; the word "background" is omitted (`--card`, `--card-foreground`).
why: Predictable names make lint rules and agent prompts possible; the fg/bg pairing guarantees contrast.
check: every `--color-*`/semantic surface has a `-foreground` twin; contrast(surface, foreground) >= 4.5.

text: Map to library namespaces: spacing base -> `--spacing`; radii -> `--radius-xs..4xl`; type -> `--text-*` (+ `--text-*--line-height`); breakpoints -> `--breakpoint-*`; containers -> `--container-*`; fonts -> `--font-sans|mono|heading` (never `--font-geist-sans`); easing -> `--ease-*`.
why: coss/shadcn/Tailwind components read these names; mismatched names silently fall back to defaults (coss docs list the font-variable mismatch as the common pitfall).
check: computed `getComputedStyle(root).getPropertyValue('--font-sans')` non-empty; `--font-heading` defined.

text: Base unit 4 px (`--spacing: 0.25rem`). Allowed step set: 0, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64, 80, 96, 128, 160 px (`space.0 .. space.40`). 2, 6, 10, 14 only inside controls <= 40 px and badges.
why: Matches every surveyed ramp; ramp coarsens with size so optical steps stay ~25-50 %.
check: >= 95 % of computed non-zero padding/margin/gap values in the allowed set (or multiples of 4).

text: Semantic spacing tiers: `inset` (padding inside a container), `inline` (gap in a row), `stack` (gap in a column), `section` (page rhythm). Defaults: inset sm 12 / md 16 / lg 24 / xl 32; inline xs 4 / sm 8 / md 12 / lg 16; stack xs 4 / sm 8 / md 16 / lg 24 / xl 32 / 2xl 48; section sm 48 / md 80 / lg 128 (fluid).
why: Primer `stack-gap` 8/16/24 and `stack-padding` 8/16/24, Polaris `space-card-padding` 16, coss Card `p-6` (24) / Dialog `p-6` / Alert `px-3.5 py-3` (14/12).
check: card padding 16-24 (app) / 24-40 (marketing); intra-card gap <= inter-card gap / 2.

text: Fluid values via `clamp(min, intercept + slope*vw, max)` with vmin = 360 px and vmax = 1280 px only for: display/h1/h2 type, section padding, page gutter. Everything else is stepped.
why: Utopia method; fluid body type/controls change layout unpredictably and break pixel snapping.
check: `clamp(` appears only in tokens flagged `fluid`.

text: Density knob = `--scale` (0.9 / 0.95 / 1 / 1.05 / 1.1) multiplying `--spacing`. Warn: in Tailwind-based libraries (including coss) it also scales every `h-*`/`size-*` including control heights, so keep the 44 px coarse hit-area expander in absolute `rem` (coss uses `min-h-11`, which is spacing-based: 11 x spacing).

text: Radius is derived from one knob `radius.base` (default 8 px; presets sharp 0-2, tight 4, default 8, soft 12-16, pill 9999). Roles: `radius.control = base`, `radius.chip = max(2px, base/2)`, `radius.surface = min(base*1.5, 24px)`, `radius.overlay = min(base*2, 28px)`, `radius.full = 9999px`.
why: shadcn derives sm/md/lg/xl/2xl/3xl/4xl from `--radius` by 0.6/0.8/1/1.4/1.8/2.2/2.6x; Radix multiplies a ramp by `radius-factor` (0, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 1.5+full). Observed role relationships: control 6-10, card 12-16, dialog 16 (coss), M3 dialog 28.
check: control radius / card radius in [0.4, 0.8]; card < overlay.

text: Nested radius: `radius.inner = max(0, radius.outer - padding - border-width)` (CSS: `max(0px, calc(var(--r-outer) - var(--pad) - 1px))`). If padding >= outer radius, inner = 0 and clip the child.
why: concentric arcs; coss uses `calc(var(--radius-lg) - 1px)` for its inset highlight; Apple toolbars use radii concentric to the bar.
applies: card > image/input/button, popover > item, segmented tabs.
check: for each rounded child fully inside a rounded parent: |parentR - gap - childR| <= 1 px.

text: Generate long penumbras with the doubling ladder: layer i has `y = blur = k * 2^i` and `spread = -y/2` at constant alpha: Clerk `0 0 0 1px; 0 1px 1px -.5px; 0 3px 3px -1.5px; 0 6px 6px -3px; 0 12px 12px -6px; 0 24px 24px -12px` all at ink 19 19 22 / .05; AlignUI the same with ink 41 41 41 / .04 and a `0 48px 48px -24px` tail.
why: Negative spread of half the offset keeps the shadow under the card (no side leakage), so the stack can be long without looking like a halo; constant alpha is simpler than per-layer tuning (Comeau's ladders also double y and blur).
check: each layer spread = -y/2 and y = blur; drop layers beyond 24px blur if the founder blur cap binds.

text: Do not use decorative light sources (lamp, spotlight, aurora, beams, meteors, sparkles, stars) as hero backgrounds unless the brand's world literally is light or sky, and record the override.
why: These are the most recognisable AI-landing clichés and replace a concept with atmosphere.
check: hero has no blurred gradient layer >= blur 24px or animated beam/star canvas.

text: Use scroll-linked 3D only to reveal a real product state, keep the transform under ~20deg and complete it within one viewport of scroll.
why: The device proves product when the screen is real; long or extreme transforms read as showreel and cause motion sickness.
check: visual + reduced-motion fallback shows the flat final frame.

text: Never rotate headline words (Flip Words, Typewriter) for the main claim.
why: The visitor reads a different headline depending on timing; the claim must be one sentence that holds still.
check: `h1` text content constant over 5s.

text: Word-by-word text generation at 0.5s per word with blur is too slow for headlines longer than five words; cap total reveal at 1s or skip it.
why: Reading speed is ~4 words/s; slower reveals make the visitor wait for the claim.
check: total entrance time of h1 <= 1000ms.

text: Model the theme as `algorithm(seed) -> map -> alias` with algorithms as swappable, composable functions (default, dark, compact), so a dark or compact variant is generated from the same seeds instead of hand-maintained.
why: Consistency across variants is guaranteed by construction, and a brand change is a seed change.
check: Project token build has an input file of <= 40 seeds and an output file generated for each of light, dark, compact; diff of hand-edited generated values is empty.

text: Name colour tokens `color.{property}.{role}.{emphasis}.{state}` and consume only semantic tokens in product code; keep raw palette values behind the semantic layer.
why: A structured name makes misuse greppable (a `text` token on a `background` slot) and lets a linter reject it.
check: lint: no hex/rgb in product CSS; every `var(--ds-*)` resolves to a known token (inventory of 467 colour/elevation tokens in the light theme).

text: Use accent colours only as decoration that could be swapped for another accent without losing meaning; use a role (danger, success, warning, information, discovery, brand) whenever the colour carries meaning.
why: Meaning attached to arbitrary hues cannot be themed, localised or made colour-blind-safe.
check: review: any accent-coloured element that communicates state is a FAIL; accent usage count by hue (swap test).

text: Hold contrast at 4.5:1 for text smaller than 24px and 3:1 for text 24px and larger and for UI essential to understanding; text on bold fills uses the paired inverse token.
why: Emphasis ladders are only safe if the bold end has a dedicated foreground. [computed] white on brand-bold `#1868DB` 5.2:1; white on success-bold `#5B7F24` 4.66:1; `#292A2E` on warning-bold `#FBC828` 9.14:1.
check: computed contrast on every text/background pair; `warning.bold` background must use dark text.

text: Express "selected" with the `selected` tokens plus a second cue (check, underline, border or shape), never with brand, link or focus tokens; if an element is both selected and focused keep the selected treatment and add the focus ring; reserve `color.border.focused` for focus.
why: One token one meaning; a colour alone fails colour-blind users and collides with hover.
check: selected element has non-colour differentiator; `border-focused` appears only in `:focus-visible` rules.

text: Pair surface and shadow by level (`surface.raised` with `shadow.raised`, `surface.overlay` with `shadow.overlay`), give default and sunken surfaces no shadow, limit raised to movable or focal items (one focal point per screen), and use sunken only as a backdrop for default-surface content (never on raised or overlay).
why: Stacked cues must agree about height or the stack reads as broken; overuse of raised destroys the emphasis.
check: any element with an overlay shadow has overlay surface and z-index >= 300; count of raised cards in one viewport focal region <= 1 per focal group.

text: In dark mode make higher elevation lighter (default `#1F1F21` < raised `#242528` < overlay `#2B2C2F`), keep the shadow pairing, add a 1px hairline ring to overlays, and contrast-check overlays separately.
why: Shadows are barely visible on dark backgrounds, so surface lightness carries depth.
check: luminance(overlay) > luminance(raised) > luminance(surface); overlay text contrast >= 4.5:1.

text: Indicate scrolled content with a border at the cut-off for sticky headers/footers/navigation, and use the overflow shadow (`0 0 8px #1E1F2129`) only on small UI or bordered tables where a border could be missed.
why: A visible edge tells users more content exists without adding a second elevation level.
check: sticky header has border/shadow when scrollTop > 0.

text: Space with the 8px-based scale (2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64, 80); use 0-8px inside compact UI, 12-24px for button padding and card inner space, 32-80px between page sections; group related items closer than unrelated ones; apply optical adjustment instead of equal spacing when visual weight differs.
why: A named scale removes arbitrary values; the range guidance tells which scale step fits which tier.
check: padding/margin/gap values within the scale; related-group gap < between-group gap.

text: Structure content with heading styles (7 sizes), one h1 per page, no skipped levels, never bold or enlarged body as a heading; default to body 14/20, use body-large 16/24 only for long-form, body-small 12/16 sparingly; reserve metric styles for emphasising numbers and the code style for code blocks.
why: Semantic order is accessibility; role-specific styles prevent ad-hoc hierarchy.
check: DOM: one `h1`; heading levels monotonic; computed sizes match token table.

text: Assign radius by role (badge 2, tag/lozenge/tooltip 4, button/input 6, card/dropdown 8, modal/page container/table 12, avatar full) and draw the focus ring 2px outside the element with radius = element radius + 2.
why: A role map avoids one-off radii; a derived focus radius keeps the ring concentric.
check: computed radius of component classes in the role set; `outline-offset` 2px and ring radius = radius + 2.

text: Time motion by tier: interactions (hover, press) 50-150ms, transitions 150-400ms scaled to element size, exits faster than entrances (popup in 150ms, out 100ms; modal in 250ms, out 200ms), start motion immediately, lead with one focal motion, and make reduced motion instant.
why: Large elements need time to be perceived; exits that outlast intent block work.
check: computed `transition-duration` on hover/press <= 150ms; modal enter <= 250ms; reduced-motion media query present.

text: Use bold-ease curves for large structural entrances (panels, flags: `0,0.4,0,1`), practical-ease for small ones (popups, hover fades: `0.4,1,0.6,1`), and the in-practical curve (`0.6,0,0.8,0.6`) for every exit.
why: Matching curve to element size and direction makes motion feel intentional and consistent across components.
check: transition-timing-function in {the four tokens}; exits use in-practical.

text: Use one primary button per page or area; avoid disabling buttons (keep them pressable and explain via validation); never put tooltips on disabled buttons; align the primary with the group's alignment (right-aligned group: primary right; left-aligned: primary left; centre only in benefit modals and login); label in sentence case, verb first, no articles, no punctuation.
why: Disabled buttons are not focusable and cannot explain themselves; alignment keeps the primary where the eye ends.
check: primary button count per region <= 1; `disabled` submit buttons = 0; tooltip not attached to `[disabled]`.

text: Write errors with an optional title of 3-4 words (not explaining the fix), a 1-2 sentence body (reason, what to do, what happens if not), and a 1-2 word specific verb CTA with a visible dismiss; use "you" not "we"; avoid "sorry" and "please" unless the consequence is severe and irreversible.
why: "Sorry" inflates severity, "please" makes required steps sound optional, "we" assigns blame.
check: regex: `\bsorry\b`, `\bplease\b`, `\bOK\b` as CTA; title word count <= 4 (excluding articles).

text: Tune tone to the user's emotional state: bolder and more optimistic for ambitious daily users, more prescriptive and less optimistic for new or confused users, no wink in error or warning states, delight only after trust, concise, global-audience-safe humour.
why: The same line can encourage a power user and condescend to a new user.
check: copy review per state; error/warning strings contain no emoji/jokes.

text: Map z-index to layer meaning (navigation 200, inline dialog 300, popup 400, blanket 500, modal 510, flag 600, spotlight 700, tooltip 800) and elevation style (navigation default; dialog/popup/modal/flag/spotlight overlay; blanket and tooltip none).
why: A single ordered table eliminates z-index wars.
check: computed z-index values of overlay components ⊂ the table.

text: Expose colour to components through a small fixed set of intents (primary, success, warning, danger, default), each defining rest, hover, active, disabled and foreground values.
why: One prop gives consistent meaning across every component and both themes.
check: component colour props accept only intent names; each intent has all five state tokens.

text: Use a dark foreground on warning (orange/yellow) fills and white on primary/success/danger fills.
why: Orange/yellow mid-tones cannot reach 4.5:1 with white text.
check: contrast(fg, warning bg) >= 4.5:1.

text: Choose a body line-height that yields an integer line box (14px x 1.28581 = 18px) and compute control padding as (controlHeight - lineBox) / 2.
why: Sub-pixel line boxes blur baselines and make text sit off-centre in buttons and inputs.
check: computed line-height in px is an integer for body/UI text; text vertically centred within 0.5px in controls.

text: For dense desktop tools set default control height to 30px (small 24, large 40) with 14px text; reserve 40px+ for touch contexts.
why: Power users scan and click many controls; smaller controls fit more data per screen.
check: default `button, input` height 28-32px in desktop builds.

text: Include the 1px edge inside each elevation shadow (first layer `0 0 0 1px rgba(0,0,0,.1-.15)`) instead of a separate border.
why: Edge and depth then scale together and never double up or disagree.
check: elevated surfaces have no CSS border and a box-shadow whose first layer is a 0-blur 1px spread.

text: In dark themes, draw surface edges with inset white hairlines (inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(255,255,255,.2)) and double drop-shadow opacity.
why: Dark shadows on dark backgrounds vanish; a light inner edge restores the surface boundary.
check: dark elevated surfaces have an inset light box-shadow layer.

text: Scope the dark theme to a container class so dark and light regions can coexist (e.g. dark navbar or dark side panel inside a light app).
why: Analyst tools mix map/graph canvases (dark) with forms (light).
check: theme class works on a non-root element; nested components inherit dark tokens.

text: Keep UI motion at 100ms for state changes and 200ms for larger movement (drawers, tree carets, tab indicators).
why: Desktop power users perceive anything slower as lag.
check: transition durations <= 200ms except loaders.

text: Use a single 4px radius across controls and surfaces in a tool-like product.
why: One radius reads as precise and keeps dense grids of controls visually quiet.
check: distinct border-radius values in UI <= 2 (excluding pills/circles).

text: Provide a categorical palette of at least 10 hues x 5 lightness steps for data, tags and entity colour-coding, separate from intent colours.
why: Analytical products need many distinguishable categories without overloading status meanings.
check: categorical colours do not reuse intent tokens.

text: Specify every colour with the same eight roles (contrast, fg, subtle, muted, emphasized, solid, focusRing, border), each defined for light and dark, so any component recipe can be written once and re-hued by swapping the palette.
why: Uniform role names remove per-hue special cases and make adding a brand colour mechanical.
check: For each palette in the system spec, assert all 8 role keys exist for both modes; assert solid vs contrast >= 4.5:1 in both modes.

text: Components may reference only semantic tokens (bg.*, fg.*, border.*, colorPalette.*), never raw scale steps; raw steps appear only inside the semantic layer.
why: A single indirection point makes dark mode, rebrands and white-labelling a token edit.
check: Grep component CSS/recipes for raw scale references (blue.600, #hex); count must be zero outside the semantic token file.

text: Encode each component as a recipe with explicit axes: variant (solid, subtle, surface, outline, ghost, plain), size (e.g. 2xs 24, xs 32, sm 36, md 40, lg 44, xl 48, 2xl 64 px heights), and palette as an independent third axis; declare defaultVariants.
why: Separating axes prevents variant x colour x size explosions and makes the spec complete by construction.
check: For each component, list variant, size and state coverage in the spec; every cell of the grid must be defined or explicitly marked not-applicable.

text: Derive hover from the variant, not from a global dim: solid hovers to solid at 90%, subtle and surface hover to the muted step, outline and ghost hover to the subtle step; expanded uses the same colour as hover.
why: Each emphasis level moves one step in its own ramp, keeping hierarchy under interaction.
check: Computed hover background of each variant differs from rest by one ramp step (or 10% alpha) and never crosses into another variant's rest colour.

text: Couple font-size to line-height (and, from 36px upward, to -0.025em tracking) in a named text style: 12/16, 14/20, 16/24, 18/28, 20/30, 24/32, 30/38, 36/44, 48/60, 60/72, 72/92.
why: A size without its leading is a common source of cramped or loose type; naming the pair enforces consistency.
check: For every text element, (font-size, line-height) must match one of the style pairs; headings at >= 36px must have letter-spacing <= -0.02em.

text: Use three semantic radius layers: inner l1 (2px), control l2 (4px), container l3 (6px), such that the container radius equals the inner radius plus its padding intent; tune brand character by re-pointing the three tokens.
why: Nested rounded shapes only look concentric when radii step consistently.
check: Inspect border-radius for nested pairs (card > button); inner radius < outer radius.

text: Draw outline and surface borders as 1px inset box-shadow (not CSS border) in the palette's muted or border role, and keep a real 1px border only where the element needs focus-inside geometry (inputs).
why: No 1px layout shift between variants; borders stack cleanly with other shadows.
check: Compare offsetWidth/Height of the same component rendered in solid vs outline variant; they must be equal.

text: Disabled is a single shared layer style (opacity 0.5 plus a dedicated cursor token not-allowed) applied by condition, not re-specified per component; define cursor tokens (button pointer, checkbox default, disabled not-allowed, menuitem default).
why: One rule keeps disabled consistent and keeps native-feeling cursors on form primitives.
check: Every :disabled control computes opacity 0.5 and cursor not-allowed; checkbox/radio/option cursor is default.

text: Pick focus geometry per component class: outside ring (2px, offset 2px) for buttons and links, inside (1px, no offset, border recoloured) for text fields and tab panels, in the palette's focusRing colour at 500.
why: Rings that match the component's edge condition stay visible without overlapping neighbours.
check: On :focus-visible, outline-width >= 1px; buttons show outline-offset 2px; inputs show border-color changed to the focus colour.

text: Make exit animations shorter than enter animations (select: fast 150ms in, fastest 50ms out; popover and menu: fast 150ms in, faster 100ms out) and tie durations to a named scale (50, 100, 150, 200, 300, 400, 500ms).
why: Closing feels responsive while entering reads as intentional.
check: Computed animation-duration for [data-state=closed] <= that of [data-state=open] on popovers and selects.

text: Give shadows a dark-mode counterpart: light = gray.900 at 10% soft layer plus a 1px hairline at 20-30%; dark = black at 64% plus a 1px inset light edge (gray.300 at 20-30%).
why: Drop shadows vanish on dark surfaces; an inner highlight edge preserves elevation.
check: In dark mode, elevated surfaces have an inset 1px light-alpha edge or a lighter surface step; box-shadow alone on #09090B is insufficient.

text: Store each token's mode variants inside the token ({light, dark}, {comfortable, compact}, {default, disabled}) and resolve by mode at runtime, rather than maintaining parallel theme files.
why: A token can't exist in one mode and be missing in another; every axis is visible in one place.
check: token JSON: every colour token has both light and dark; every scaled spacing token has both densities.

text: Split spacing into scaled tokens (component padding, shrink in compact by about one 4px step) and static tokens (layout gutters, never change).
why: Density should tighten controls without collapsing page structure.
check: compare comfortable vs compact computed styles: gutters equal, control paddings smaller.

text: Ship comfortable density as the default; offer compact only as a user preference for full-page data views, applied consistently app-wide, never to one isolated page or component.
why: Compact hurts readability and can overwhelm; mixed density looks broken.
check: default render uses comfortable tokens; density toggle exists in preferences; no page-scoped compact class.

text: Keep informational components (alerts, help text, validation messages) and small-target controls (dropdown options, date cells, charts) at comfortable spacing even in compact mode.
