check: border colour of any input/button vs adjacent surface >= 3:1; decorative border <= 3:1 is acceptable; text >= 4.5:1.

text: Define all five interactive states for every control (rest, `:hover`, `:focus-visible`, `:active`, disabled) and express disabled with dedicated disabled tokens, never `opacity`.
why: Opacity lowers contrast unpredictably and stacks with other alpha tokens; dedicated tokens can be contrast-tuned. `:focus` alone shows rings on mouse clicks.
check: for each `button, a, input, select, [role=button]` rule set: presence of `:hover`, `:focus-visible`, `:active`, `:disabled` or `[aria-disabled=true]`; no `opacity` < 1 on disabled selectors.
source: DESIGN_TOKENS_GUIDE.md "Interactive States Checklist" and golden button example

text: Draw the keyboard focus indicator as a 2px solid outline in `focus-outlineColor` (accent blue) with a -2px (inset) offset on controls that sit inside a container.
why: An inset ring cannot be clipped by `overflow:hidden` parents and keeps its 3:1 contrast against the control itself.
check: computed `outline-width` = 2px and `outline-style` solid on `:focus-visible`; outline colour contrast vs both the control and the page >= 3:1.

text: Use only the five control heights 24, 28, 32 (default), 40, 48 px, with paddingInline from {condensed, normal, spacious} = {8, 12, 16} (xsmall {4, 8, 12}); on coarse pointers raise the target to at least 44px.
why: A closed set of heights lets controls align in a row without per-pair tuning; density is then a single switch.
check: computed `min-height`/`height` of controls in set; `@media (pointer: coarse)` target >= 44px.

text: Set text with the role shorthand (weight, size/line-height, family together); body-medium is 14/21, title-medium 20/32.5, caption 12/15 and is single-line only; keep measure near or under 80 characters, left-aligned.
why: Splitting size, line-height and weight lets them drift; caption's tight 1.25 leading fails for multi-line reading.
applies: SaaS app UI | marketing (product pages only)
check: computed font-size/line-height pairs match the role table; `max-width` of paragraphs <= ~80ch; no `font-weight` outside {300, 400, 500, 600}.

text: Cap UI transitions at 300ms (100ms hover, 200ms state change, 300ms enter), make exit faster than enter (200ms easeIn), use no motion token over 500ms, and replace motion with an instant change under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
why: Interface motion that outlasts the user's intent feels like lag; faster exits keep dismissed elements from blocking the next action.
check: computed `transition-duration` <= 300ms on interactive elements; presence of `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` zeroing transitions.

text: Tie elevation to stacking: resting shadows with default/sticky layers; `floating-small`/`medium` with dropdown (200) / overlay (300); `floating-large`/`xlarge` with modal (400) / popover (500); add a 1px ring (`0 0 0 1px`) to floating shadows so edges survive dark themes.
why: Shadow size predicts how far an element floats, so z-index and shadow disagreeing reads as a bug; on dark backgrounds blur shadows disappear.
check: each element with `z-index` >= 200 has a floating shadow; dark floating shadow starts with a 1px ring.

text: Validate forms on submit; do not disable the submit button; with three or more errors show an error summary Banner of anchor links that focus each input, otherwise focus the first invalid input; mark invalid inputs `aria-invalid="true"` and link messages with `aria-describedby`; hide the caption while the error shows.
why: Disabled submit buttons explain nothing; focus management replaces live regions for validation so screen-reader users land on the problem.
check: `button[type=submit]:disabled` count = 0 on an empty form; invalid inputs expose `aria-invalid` and a resolvable `aria-describedby`.

text: Pick the loading indicator by expected duration: under 1s none, 1-3s indeterminate (spinner), 3-10s determinate (progress), over 10s determinate plus background task; use skeletons for large regions and avoid layout shift.
why: An indicator flashing for under a second is more distracting than the wait; known duration deserves a determinate cue.
check: visual / review: indicator type vs measured latency; CLS of region swap ~0.

text: Put one primary Button in a view, at the end of a ButtonGroup, paired with a secondary; use the secondary (default) variant most of the time; label in sentence case with no line break; show selected values inside selector buttons (`2 selected`), not comma lists.
why: Primary loses meaning when repeated; the default variant keeps hierarchy readable.
check:
count of `primary` buttons per viewport region <= 1; button label has no `
`/wrap and matches sentence case.

text: Make Dialog header title and close button mandatory (title may be visually hidden; close must be visible), keep a 16px safe area and 8px close inset, put primary actions on the right and secondary on the left, never dismiss on backdrop click when a form is dirty, nest at most two Dialogs, use full-screen on narrow viewports when inputs exist.
why: A dialog without a title or a visible exit traps users and screen readers; dirty-form backdrop dismissal destroys work.
check: every `[role=dialog]` has an accessible name and a visible close control; dirty-form dialog ignores backdrop click.

text: Provide `inactive` as a distinct state from `disabled`: inactive looks muted for every variant but stays focusable, keeps compliant contrast, and must open a dialog or tooltip that explains why.
why: Disabled controls are unreachable and silent; a blocked-but-explainable action needs an accessible alternative.
check: inactive control is in tab order; has an explanatory dialog/tooltip; contrast >= 4.5:1.
source: primer.style button guidelines [secondary]; @primer/react Button prop `inactive` docs (generated/components.json)

text: Ship the system spec as an LLM-readable guide: RFC 2119 keywords (MUST, SHOULD, NEVER), decision trees (easing choice), a golden example, and a hallucination guard that makes an unrecognised token name carry a `/* check-token */` marker.
why: Agents invent plausible token names; explicit guard text turns silent failure into a greppable one.
check: tool: extract every `var(--*)` from generated CSS and diff against the token list; report unknown names.

text: Write copy in sentence case with no end punctuation on headings, labels or buttons, imperative verb first ("Save preferences"), no exclamation marks, no "Oops", no humour in errors or loading, error text says what to do ("Enter a credit card number", not "Field required"), link text never "here".
why: Predictable wording is faster to scan and localises; blame-free errors reduce abandonment.
check: regex on UI strings: Title Case buttons, trailing `.` on labels, `!`, `Oops`, `click here`.

text: Name button variants by intent and cap their use: primary = the single main action per context, secondary = alternatives (several allowed), tertiary = dismissive actions (cancel, skip), danger = destructive; never name or choose a variant by visual treatment (solid, flat, bordered).
why: Hierarchy is decided by the action's role, so the same intent re-skins correctly in any theme.
applies: SaaS app UI | landing page | forms
check: Per view, count primary buttons <= 1 per context; visual rule: only one filled accent button in the viewport.

text: Define each colour role once (base + foreground) and derive hover (accent 90% + foreground 10% in oklab), soft background (15% light, 12% dark over transparent), soft hover (20% / 16%) and soft foreground (accent 70% + foreground 30%) by formula instead of authoring each.
why: Derivation guarantees every state stays on-hue and lets a theme change one variable.
check: In the system spec every colour role has exactly one authored value; hover and soft values are expressions. Verify soft-foreground on soft-background >= 4.5:1.

text: Separate surface tokens (in-flow containers: surface, surface-secondary, surface-tertiary) from overlay tokens (floating layers) and give each its own foreground and shadow; in dark mode drop the surface shadow and give overlays a 1px inset light edge.
why: Elevation is communicated by lightness steps and edges on dark backgrounds, since drop shadows disappear.
check: In dark mode, elevated components have inset edge or lightness step vs background (engine heuristic: surface vs background contrast >= 1.1:1); light mode cards sit on a grey page (#f5f5f5) as white.

text: Drive the radius scale from one base value with fixed multipliers (xs 0.25x, sm 0.5x, md 0.75x, lg 1x, xl 1.5x, 2xl 2x, 3xl 3x, 4xl 4x) and a separate field multiplier (1.5x) so inputs and containers can diverge from controls.
why: Changing character (sharp to soft) is a one-variable edit while proportions stay coherent.
check: All border-radius values in the built CSS must be scale multiples or full.

text: Make form fields borderless by default (border width 0, tinted or white fill, soft field shadow) and reveal state by mixing the border toward the field foreground: hover 88/10, focus 74/22, plus a 2px focus ring with 0 offset; invalid = 1px danger outline that becomes a 2px ring on focus.
why: Quiet idle fields reduce visual noise; state is clear without layout shift because width is token-controlled.
check: Compare field box size at rest, hover, focus, invalid: unchanged. Focus ring contrast against surface >= 3:1.

text: Put an offset ring (2px ring + 2px background-coloured offset) on :focus-visible for buttons, and a flush ring (2px, 0 offset) for fields; style disabled with a single shared utility (opacity 0.5, cursor not-allowed, pointer-events none).
why: An offset ring stays visible over filled controls; one disabled utility prevents drift.
check: Tab through; ring width >= 2px with the focus colour; disabled controls report cursor not-allowed and opacity 0.5.

text: Scale press feedback with control size (sm scale 0.98, md 0.97, lg 0.96) and animate transform at 250ms with colour at 100ms; apply hover only under a hover-capable media query.
why: Consistent physical feedback; avoids sticky hover on touch devices.
applies: SaaS app UI | landing page | mobile
check: Computed :active transform scale matches the size; hover rules are inside @media (hover:hover).

text: Size touch controls larger than pointer controls: 36 / 40 / 44px (sm / md / lg) by default and 32 / 36 / 40px at the md breakpoint and above; widen sub-24px hit areas with a transparent 24px overlay (touch-target utility).
why: Finger targets need more size; WCAG 2.5.8 sets a 24px minimum target.
check: At 375px viewport button/input height >= 40px for md; any interactive element < 24px has an enlarged hit area.

text: Treat reduced motion as part of the system: a motion-reduce variant keyed to an explicit attribute first and prefers-reduced-motion second, and put it after every transition declaration.
why: Specificity and order decide whether reduced motion actually wins; an explicit attribute allows user override.
check: With prefers-reduced-motion emulated, computed transition-duration of buttons, inputs and tabs is 0s.

text: Do not copy v3's accent/danger pairings blindly: white-ish foreground on accent oklch(0.6204 0.195 253.83) measures about 3.59:1 and on danger about 3.48:1, below 4.5:1 for 14px labels.
why: [engine note] Measured from this study's oklch conversion; teams should darken the fill or enlarge/bold the text.
check: Contrast of -foreground on base for every role >= 4.5:1 (or >= 3:1 only for 18.66px bold or larger text).
source: variables.css; this study (WCAG formula, conversion error under +/-0.05)

text: Pick the type set by the user's task: productive (14px base, fixed headings, compact body) for task-focused product pages; expressive (16px base, fluid headings) for reading, exploring and marketing; blend only with a full-width "moment" that contains no containers, and never use fluid or display styles inside a container.
why: Dense task work needs predictable sizes; reading and persuasion need larger, responsive type; mixing inside boxes breaks both.
applies: SaaS app UI | marketing | design systems
check: computed font-size of text inside `.card/.tile/.modal` containers <= 32px and not from a fluid style; display/fluid classes have no container ancestor.

text: Generate sizes from a scale formula (or a documented ladder) and pair compatible body/heading tokens: body-compact-01 with heading-compact-01; body-01 with heading-01; body-compact-02 with heading-compact-02; body-02 with heading-02.
why: Pre-paired leading values keep baselines consistent when body and heading sit next to each other.
check: sizes in {12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36, 42, 48, 54, 60, 68, 76, 84, 92}; adjacent heading/body pair use same family of line-heights.

text: Limit weights to 300, 400, 600; use semibold for headers and labels only, not for long text; use light weight only where the size is much larger than body; use italic only for emphasis; keep running text neutral and reserve colour for links, status and code.
why: A heavier weight at the same size is stronger, but a lighter weight can outrank it if much larger; colour as decoration lowers signal.
check: computed `font-weight` ∈ {300, 400, 600}; weight 300 only at font-size >= 24px.

text: Add positive tracking to small text (12px: 0.32px, 14px: 0.16px), none at 16px and above, and tighten (-0.64px, -0.96px) only on display sizes above about 60px.
why: Small sizes need extra letter spacing for legibility; huge type looks loose without negative tracking.
check: computed `letter-spacing` vs font-size: 12px ≈ 0.0267em, 14px ≈ 0.0114em, >= 16px 0, display >= 60px negative.

text: Use a layering model: page = `background`; first container = `layer-01`; nested container = `layer-02`; third = `layer-03`; in light themes alternate White and Gray 10; in dark themes step one palette grade lighter per layer; never make a component darker than its background in a dark theme unless using high-contrast inverse.
why: One rule creates visible hierarchy without shadows and keeps contrast predictable at any nesting depth.
check: nested container luminance differs from parent by one step; in dark mode child luminance >= parent luminance.

text: Derive interaction colour by rule: hover half a step, active two steps, selected one step, focus 2px `focus` border with a 1px `focus-inset` so the ring holds 3:1, disabled in the gray family with no hover or focus.
why: A rule scales to every component and theme without hand-picking values.
check: state colours differ from rest by the expected step; focus indicator contrast >= 3:1 vs adjacent colours.

text: Never use midtone fills in light themes, never use hover colours outside hover, and never use a component token outside its component.
why: Midtones fail contrast; reusing hover or component tokens couples unrelated parts and breaks theming.
check: lint: `button-*` and `tag-*` tokens appear only in their own component files; hover tokens only in `:hover`.

text: Meet 4.5:1 for text under 24px (19px semibold), 3:1 for large text, UI components, graphics and focus indicators, and never rely on colour alone.
why: WCAG AA; in this system chroma semantics (red/yellow/green) are reinforced by icon shape.
check: computed contrast; each status has an icon or text as well as colour. Note [computed] `support-warning #f1c21b` on white is 1.68:1, so a yellow status needs a dark glyph or container.

text: Lay out on the 2x Grid: 4, 8, 16, 16, 16 columns at 320, 672, 1056, 1312, 1584; margins 0 (sm), 16, 16, 16, 24; 8px mini unit; default wide gutter 32px, narrow 16px, condensed 1px; fixed components with labels (inputs, dropdowns) must use the wide gutter; type never hangs into the gutter; containers may hang in narrow and condensed modes.
why: Hanging containers align text inside and outside boxes without moving type off the columns; forms need breathing room.
check: column count at breakpoint; text left edges coincide with column edges; form field containers do not extend into the gutter.

text: Space with the scale 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64, 80, 96, 160 px; use Stack for equal gaps; use percentages only for page division and max/min widths; avoid increments outside the scale; do not change tokens by breakpoint, step up or down the scale instead.
why: One scale across components and layout keeps rhythm; exceptions are allowed but "should be avoided".
check: padding/margin/gap values ∈ scale.

text: Fix control heights to 24 (xs), 32 (sm), 40 (md), 48 (lg), 64 (xl), 80 (2xl) and pair sizes: small button with small input, medium with medium, large with 14px body (productive) or 16px body (expressive); never mix sizes in a button group.
why: Equal heights align rows; mismatched sibling controls look broken.
check: computed height of controls ∈ set; same-row controls share height.

text: Limit button hierarchy: one primary per page (not counting app header, modals, side panels); secondary only paired with a primary; ghost and tertiary for lower emphasis; danger kinds for destructive actions and never icon-only; more than three actions go into a menu button; icon-only buttons need a tooltip; use {verb}+{noun} labels in sentence case; left-align labels; never truncate (wrap).
why: A clear emphasis ladder removes choice friction; an icon alone is ambiguous.
check: primary buttons per page <= 1; button group size <= 3; tooltip on `[aria-label]`-only buttons.

text: Order button groups by context: on full-page designs put the primary first (left); in dialogs and wizards put the primary last (right); equal widths in a group set by the longest label; stacked groups put the primary on top; gutter between grouped buttons 16px.
why: Reading order and thumb position decide where the most likely action should sit.
check: DOM order and flex direction of group by container type; equal computed widths.

text: Give buttons the asymmetric geometry padding-left 16px / padding-right 64px (label then trailing icon), icon 16px (20px expressive), at least 16px between label and icon, 1px inset focus, and label never within 16px of an edge.
why: Reserving the right side for an icon aligns label baselines across a column of buttons and signals direction.
check: computed paddings; icon size; focus ring is inset.

text: Match motion to mode: productive easing (`0.2,0,0.38,0.9`) for tasks, expressive (`0.4,0.14,0.3,1`) for rare significant moments; use entrance easing for appearing, exit easing for removed, standard easing when the element stays visible or leaves but stays near (side panel); micro-interactions 70-110ms; small expansions 150ms; toasts and system messages 240ms; large expansion 400ms; background dim 700ms.
why: Distance and significance should drive duration; an element that stays on screen should not use exit curves.
check: computed `transition-timing-function` ∈ the six curves; micro-interaction duration ≤ 110ms.

text: Write all UI text in sentence case; do not use title case or all-caps; capitalise only proper nouns, products and trademarked names; do not treat UI elements as proper nouns; use short, everyday words and consistent action labels from the glossary.
why: Title case needs subjective "importance" decisions that drift across a large org; all-caps slows reading and wastes space.
check: regex on UI strings for Title Case buttons/labels and `text-transform: uppercase` on body-length text.

text: Document each component with four tabs (Usage, Style, Code, Accessibility) and in Style publish structure tables (px / rem / spacing token) and colour tables (element, property, token) for every state and kind.
why: If the spec is tabular, completeness is checkable: a missing cell is a visible gap.
check: for each component spec: every kind x state cell filled; every padding has a token.

text: Generate every theme (light, dark, high-contrast, custom) from three inputs: a base colour, an accent colour and a contrast scalar, computed in a perceptual space (LCH/OKLCH); do not store per-theme lists of hand-picked variables.
why: Hand-authored themes drift (98 variables per theme at Linear before the change); a generator keeps surface, text and border ratios identical across themes and makes accessibility themes a parameter.
check: theme file contains at most 3 authored inputs per theme; every semantic token is an expression of them.

text: Make tracking a function of size and store it with the type token: about -0.011em to -0.013em at 14-15px, -0.012em at 17-24px, -0.022em at 32px and larger; line-height steps down 1.6, 1.4, 1.33, 1.125, 1.1, 1.0 as size rises.
why: Inter at display size looks loose with default tracking; fixed -0.02em at every size would crush small text.
check: computed letter-spacing / font-size per heading and body style; compare to the table above (tolerance 0.004em).

text: Pick one non-default variable weight as the brand weight (Linear: 510) and define the whole weight ladder as tokens (400, 510, 590, 680); do not use 500/600/700 literals in components.
why: An odd, tokenised weight is hard to copy by accident and keeps UI text from jumping between near-identical weights.
check: computed font-weight values on a page come from a set of at most 4 tokens.

text: Use explicit `transition-property` lists with 100-160ms durations and an ease-out curve for hover and focus; keep 400-700ms only for decorative transforms; never `transition: all` on interactive controls.
why: Interaction feedback should be perceived as instant; `all` animates layout properties and causes jank.

text: Use at most one ambient or edge-light effect per page, and none from the cliché column without an override in DIRECTION.md.
why: Beams, shimmer, aurora text and grid backgrounds now signal "AI template" and spend attention on decoration instead of proof.
check: count of animated background/border-light components per page <= 1.

text: Section entrances: 300-400ms, translate <= 8px, optional blur <= 6px, once per element, triggered in view.
why: Magic UI's defaults (0.4s, 6px, 6px blur; text 0.3s) are short enough to never block reading; larger offsets read as gimmick.
check: entrance animation duration 300-400ms and translate <= 8px.

text: Every looping or entrance effect must have a `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` path that renders the final state without motion.
why: The sampled components ship no reduced-motion handling; vestibular-sensitive users get infinite loops.
check: with reduced motion emulated, no element has a running animation after load.

text: Animate numbers only when the number is real, sourced and final; never tick to placeholder metrics.
why: Counting motion draws the eye to the claim; an invented number becomes a highlighted lie.
check: each Number Ticker value has a source note.

text: Run marquees slowly (>= 30s per loop), pause on hover/focus, and only for real logos or real quotes.
why: Fast marquees are unreadable; fake logos break the never-invent-proof rule.
check: animation-duration >= 30s; hover pauses.

text: Define every brand hue as a 10-step ramp (lightest to darkest) and bind variant roles to shade INDICES (filled 6 light / 8 dark, hover = filled + 1, soft bg 1, soft text 9 light / 0 dark, text-on-dark-scheme 4); never pick per-component hex.
why: Index maps make every variant of every hue consistent and make a rebrand a 10-value change; hex-per-use drifts.
applies: SaaS app UI | landing page | all
check: For each brand ramp, assert that the soft-variant text (shade 9) against the soft bg (shade 1) is at least 4.5:1 and that filled text vs filled bg meets 4.5:1 (Mantine blue.9 on blue.1 = 4.93:1).

text: Give light and dark schemes separate primary shade indices (default light 6, dark 8) and re-derive dark soft backgrounds by darkening the darkest shade (50% base, 30% hover) rather than reusing the light fill.
why: The same fill needs a different lightness against a dark canvas to hold contrast and avoid glow.
check: Compute contrast of text on the filled colour in both schemes; both must reach 4.5:1 for body-size labels (Mantine blue: 3.56:1 light-6 fails, 5.02:1 dark-8 passes).

text: Use one control-height ladder for all form controls and buttons: 30 / 36 / 42 / 50 / 60 px for xs / sm / md / lg / xl, default sm (36px), with matching icon-button sizes in input context, so same-size controls share one height in a row.
why: Mixed heights break the baseline of toolbars and form rows.
check: Computed height of Button and Input at the same size attribute must be equal; all control heights must belong to the ladder.

text: Pair body font-size steps with growing line-heights (12px/1.4, 14px/1.45, 16px/1.55, 18px/1.6, 20px/1.65) and heading steps with shrinking ones (34px/1.3, 26px/1.35, 22px/1.4, 18px/1.45, 16px/1.5, 14px/1.5).
why: Small text needs relatively more leading for legibility; large display text looks loose at body leading.
check: Computed line-height / font-size: body 1.4-1.65, h1-h2 1.3-1.35; flag headings above 1.4 when size is 26px or larger.

text: Express text-on-colour as a rule, not a hope: default to white text on filled colours but switch to black when the fill's relative luminance exceeds a threshold (Mantine 0.3), and allow it per component.
why: Light brand colours (yellow, lime, cyan) fail with white text.
check: For every filled colour in the palette compute luminance; if > 0.3 text must be black; verify contrast >= 4.5:1.

text: Model Disabled as three tokens (background gray-2, text gray-5, border gray-3 in light; dark-6 / dark-3 / dark-4 in dark) shared by every control, and Error/Success as a border plus text plus placeholder plus section-icon colour change together.
why: Partial state styling (only a red border) reads as a bug and differs across components.
check: For each form control, enumerate the CSS properties that change in disabled and error states; they must match across Input, Select, Textarea.

text: Expose a single global radius token (default md = 8px) that every component reads, with a 5-step scale 2 / 4 / 8 / 16 / 32 px; allow per-component override by scale key.
why: Radius is the cheapest lever for brand character; one token keeps every component coherent.
check: Collect border-radius on button, input, card, popover; each must equal one scale value or the global default.

text: Show keyboard focus with a 2px solid ring in the primary filled colour at 2px offset, only on :focus-visible, and make the policy a theme switch (auto, always, never) with auto recommended.
why: Visible, consistent keyboard focus without a ring on every mouse click.
check: Tab through interactive elements; each shows a >= 2px ring with contrast >= 3:1 against adjacent colours; mouse click shows none.

text: Give every interactive element a physical pressed response: translateY(1px) on :active, disabled inside disabled fieldsets; loading buttons slide the label (150ms transform, 100ms opacity) and show a loader rather than swapping the size.
why: Feedback without layout shift confirms input.
check: Compute :active transform on buttons; loading state keeps width and height unchanged.

text: Build depth shadows as a tight 1px contact shadow plus one or two large, negatively spread ambient layers (e.g. 0 1px 3px .05 + 0 20px 25px -5px .05 + 0 10px 10px -5px .04), never a single blur.
why: Layered shadows read as soft elevation without a muddy halo.
check: Parse box-shadow on elevated surfaces: >= 2 layers, opacity <= 0.1 each in light mode.

text: Keep a tokenised motion scale; do not copy Mantine's per-component literals (100/150/200/250ms) as a system.
why: [engine note] Mantine hard-codes durations per component and makes reduced motion opt-in, which is the weakest part of its spec.
check: Collect all transition-duration values in a built page; they should come from a small set.
source: Button.module.css, Tooltip.tsx, Popover.tsx, Modal.tsx; theme.respectReducedMotion default false

text: Define every text style as a single token holding the full font shorthand (weight, size, line-height, family) plus a sibling letter-spacing token, one pair per size and weight combination.
why: It stops per-component recombination of size, weight and tracking; the table is checkable.
check: computed (font-size, line-height, font-weight, letter-spacing) of every text node is a row of the type table (tolerance 0.5px / 0.002em).

text: At display sizes (>= 42px) set tracking per weight: regular at about -0.043em to -0.065em, semibold and bold at about -0.033em to -0.048em; below 24px use at most -0.012em.
why: Lighter strokes need more compression to hold a heading together; bold needs less to avoid collisions.
check: for headings >= 42px letter-spacing/size between -0.065em and -0.03em; for text <= 24px >= -0.012em.

text: Name state inside the token (background, -hover, -focus, -active, -selected, -disabled) for every interactive component and fill all of them, even when values are identical.
why: Missing states are visible as gaps in the token list; an audit becomes a diff.
check: for each `--*-button-*-background` token there are `-hover`, `-focus`, `-active` siblings.

why: Core brand stays stable while launches rotate; campaigns can be deleted wholesale.

text: Use alpha-black (or alpha-white) for text and hairlines on warm light surfaces only after verifying contrast on every background the text meets; use solid grey-600 (#615d59, 6.53:1) for captions on tinted chips.
why: Alpha greys inherit the background; a pastel chip can drop a 54% black label under 4.5:1.

why: An ease-in curve delays the first frames of feedback and feels laggy.

text: Layer 4 to 6 shadows with opacities between 2% and 10% and growing offsets/blur (0.2px to 36px offset, up to 89px blur) for floating cards instead of one visible shadow.
why: Approximates real light falloff; edges stay soft and nothing reads as a border.

text: Reserve the brand/product colour for elements that move the user forward (primary button, button-link, text link); use a separate interactive colour (blue) for hover, focus, selection and drag feedback.
why: The brand colour then always means "next step", which speeds scanning in long funnels.
applies: landing page, SaaS app UI, forms.
check: elements with product colour are all `a[href]`/`button` that submit or navigate; selection/focus styles use a different hue.

text: Use the Light shade of a hue as background and its Dark shade for text/icons on it; never use a Dark shade as a background.
why: The shade ladder is built so Dark-on-Light of one hue clears contrast; Dark backgrounds break the ladder.
check: status component: fg/bg same hue family and contrast >= 4.5:1; no bg with Dark-step token.

text: Map elevation to actionability: non-clickable cards are flat (1px border, no shadow); clickable tiles get a small shadow; hover raises one level; overlays (popover/tooltip/drawer) and modal take the top levels.
why: Shadow becomes a clickability affordance instead of decoration.
applies: SaaS app UI, landing page cards.
check: elements with box-shadow at rest are interactive (`a`, `button`, `[role=button]`, `[tabindex]`); non-interactive cards use border only.

text: For panels anchored to the bottom of the viewport (mobile popovers, fixed footers) use a reversed shadow (negative y offset).
why: Light comes from above; a bottom sheet should cast upward.
check: bottom-fixed elements: box-shadow y-offset < 0.

text: Build heading hierarchy with size steps first; add weight or colour only for emphasis, keep a single heading colour, and don't combine a 40px Display with a 28px Title 0/24px Title 1 on one page.
why: Too large a jump from display to body disconnects information; one heading colour keeps scanning predictable.
check: distinct heading colours = 1; page does not contain both display and title-1 class; no skipped heading levels.

text: Use only the 4px-grid spacing steps 4/8/12/16/24/32/40/52: 4 to tie an error to its field, 8 between a header and its description, 16 mobile inner padding, 24 section side padding, 52 between illustration and header.
why: Closer = related; a fixed scale keeps relationships readable.
check: computed margins/paddings modulo 4 == 0 and in the allowed set.

text: Make default form controls and buttons 44px tall (small 32px, large 52px) and touch targets at least 44x44 CSS px.
why: Travel booking is mobile-heavy; WCAG 2.5.5 target size.
check: `button, input, select` bounding box height >= 44 at default size.

text: Give the icon side of a button one padding step less than the text side (e.g. 12px icon side, 16px text side).
why: Icons carry built-in whitespace; equal padding makes icon buttons look lopsided.
check: buttons with leading icon: padding-inline-start < padding-inline-end.

text: Avoid pure black text on pure white; use a near-black ink (#252A31).
why: Orbit's accessibility guidance flags the extreme contrast as hard for dyslexic readers.
check: body text colour != #000 on #fff backgrounds.

text: Expose theming as a small foundation object passed to a token-generating function, and derive every component token from it.
why: One object swap re-brands everything consistently; component tokens can't drift from the foundation.
check: component token values reference foundation keys, not literals (except documented exceptions).

text: Build the colour system from one accent hue and one gray whose hue matches it (mauve for pink to violet, slate for blue/indigo/cyan, sage for green/teal, olive for grass/lime, sand for yellow/amber/orange); use plain neutral when the accent is arbitrary.
why: A tinted gray echoes the accent hue, which makes surfaces and borders feel designed rather than assembled; neutral avoids clashes when unsure.
applies: SaaS app UI | landing page | all
check: In the project spec, the gray ramp's hue angle is within about 30 degrees of the accent hue, or the gray is chroma < 0.01 neutral.

text: Give every hue and gray a 12-step ramp per mode whose steps have fixed jobs (1 canvas, 2 subtle bg, 3 component, 4 hover, 5 pressed, 6 border subtle, 7 border interactive, 8 border strong/focus, 9 solid, 10 solid hover, 11 low text, 12 high text) and a matching 12-step alpha ramp.
why: Role-bound steps make state colours predictable and make light and dark mode a swap of values, not of logic.
check: For each ramp assert luminance monotonic over steps 1-8 (direction per mode) and step 11 text on step 2 background >= 4.5:1 (measured blue.11 on blue.2 = 4.53:1; red.11 on red.2 = 4.94:1).

text: Fix a shared variant vocabulary (solid, subtle, surface, outline, plain) and implement each as bg / border / fg with hover and active tokens, tinted variants from alpha steps (subtle: a3, hover a4, active a5, fg a11; surface: bg a2, border a6, border hover a7; outline: border a7, hover bg a2, active a3; plain: hover a3, active a4).
why: One vocabulary lets any two components sit together; alpha tints stay correct on any canvas.
check: Component spec table: every component lists which of the 5 variants it supports; hover differs from rest by one alpha step.

text: Align heights across component families with two ladders: primary controls 24 / 32 / 36 / 40 / 44 / 48 / 64 px (2xs..2xl) and secondary controls (badge 18-28, switch 16-22, checkbox 18-20) tied to the same size keys; the same size key yields the same height for Button, Input and Select.
why: Adjacent controls of the same size line up on one baseline and keep rhythm in toolbars and forms.
check: Button and Input at size md both measure 40px; the heights set is {24,32,36,40,44,48,64}.

text: Use bright-palette foreground overrides: for amber, yellow, lime, mint and sky solid fills use dark text (gray.12 in light, gray.1 in dark) and keep white text for other hues; document the exception per palette.
why: High-lightness fills cannot carry white text (amber.9 with gray.12 = 10.32:1; white would be 1.58:1).
check: For each solid fill compute both foreground candidates; choose the one with >= 4.5:1 (or >= 3:1 if text >= 18.66px bold); fail the palette otherwise.

text: Use nested radius tokens l1 < l2 < l3 (2 / 4 / 6 px by default) and apply them by layer: inner elements l1, controls l2, panels/containers l3; the outer radius should be about the inner radius plus the padding between them.
why: Concentric corners only look right when radii step with the nesting depth.
check: For nested rounded boxes, outer radius > inner radius; the set of radii used on the page is a subset of the tokens.

text: Pair open and close durations asymmetrically using a small duration scale (50, 100, 150, 200, 250, 300, 400ms): floating panels 150ms in and 100ms out, selects 250ms in and 50ms out, dialogs 200ms in and 150ms out.
why: Entering needs to be legible; leaving should not block the next action.
check: Computed animation-duration of [data-state=closed] <= [data-state=open] on every overlay component.
source: theme/tokens/durations.ts; recipes/menu.ts, select.ts, dialog.ts, popover.ts, tooltip.ts

text: Encode disabled once as a shared layer style (cursor not-allowed, opacity 0.67, grayscale 100%) and focus once as a utility with two geometries (outside for actionables: 2px ring at 2px offset; inside for fields and panels: 1px at 0 offset) coloured with the palette's solid step.
why: One definition prevents per-component drift; the geometry fits each component's edge.
check: Disabled controls compute opacity 0.67 with grayscale filter; focus-visible shows outline-width 2px offset 2px on buttons.

text: Keep the preset small and copy recipes into the project; define custom variants by editing the recipe, not by wrapping or overriding the component.
why: The recipe is the single source for variant x size x state; wrappers fragment it.
check: Grep component sources for className overrides of colour/spacing set by recipes; count should be zero in system components.

text: Do not assume solid fills meet AA: measured white text on blue.9 is 3.26:1, red.9 3.91:1, green.9 3.16:1; require a darker solid step, bold 18.66px+ text, or a different foreground.
why: [engine note] Radix step 9 is tuned for chroma, not for WCAG 2 contrast with white; the Radix guarantee covers steps 11-12 text on step 2 backgrounds, not step 9 fills.
check: Contrast(fg, solid.bg) >= 4.5:1 for text under 18.66px bold.
source: this study (WCAG 2 relative luminance); Radix docs

text: Organise tokens in three layers (palette -> base -> semantic) and forbid components from referencing palette tokens; base tokens only when no semantic token fits.
why: Themes remap the semantic layer; any palette reference becomes a theme bug.
check: grep component CSS for palette-layer names (e.g. `--pf-t--color--`): count must be 0.

text: Name tokens general-to-specific with fixed segment order (scope, component, property, concept, variant, state) and omit segments that don't apply rather than filling them with "default".
why: Predictable names are guessable and sortable; omitted segments keep names short.
check: token names parse against the schema regex.

text: Name spacing tokens by the relationship they separate (text-to-element 8, control-to-control 4, action-to-action 16, group-to-group vertical 24 / horizontal 48) with compact and spacious variants.
why: Designers pick intent, not pixels; density changes stay coherent.
check: spacing values used between label/control, buttons, and groups match the relationship table.

text: Deliver high-contrast and high-contrast-dark as first-class themes that compose with brand themes, turning on borders that are transparent in the default theme.
why: Users who need more contrast get it without losing the product's brand theme.
check: a high-contrast class exists and toggles visible borders on controls/cards.

text: In dark mode, express elevation through surface lightness: the page is darkest, cards lighter, floating menus lighter still (#151515 < #292929 < #383838).
why: Shadows disappear on dark backgrounds; lighter = closer matches perception.
check: dark theme: luminance(floating) > luminance(card) > luminance(page).

text: Use a non-brand hue for the info status when the brand/link colour is blue (PatternFly uses purple #5e40be).
why: Info banners in link-blue read as clickable and dilute the brand colour.
check: info status colour hue differs from link colour hue by >= 30 degrees.

text: Name motion durations by purpose and size (icon 50/100/200, fade 100/200/300, slide-in/out 300/400/500 ms) with three curves: decelerate (0,0,.2,1) entering, accelerate (.4,0,.7,.2) leaving, default (.4,0,.2,1) moving.
why: Components choose intent; the scale stays tunable globally.
check: transition durations used in components are members of the purpose table.

text: Give actions (buttons) pill radius and form controls a small radius (6px) so actions and inputs are distinguishable by shape.
why: Shape difference separates "do" from "enter" without relying on colour.
check: button border-radius >= height/2; input radius <= 8px.

text: Use two line-heights only: 1.3 for headings and 1.5 for body/UI text.
why: Fewer values, consistent rhythm, adequate leading for 14px body.
check: computed line-height ratio on headings 1.25-1.35, body 1.45-1.55.

text: Put multi-script fallbacks (Noto Sans Arabic, Hebrew, JP, KR, SC, TC, Thai, Malayalam) directly in the global font stacks.
why: Every component handles localised content without per-locale overrides.
check: font-family stack includes script-specific fallbacks.

text: Change a theme's temperature by swapping the neutral ramp (background, border, surface, muted) to a tinted near-grey of chroma 0.002-0.03, not only the accent.
why: Neutrals cover 80-90% of pixels; a khaki or olive-grey neutral changes mood more than any button colour.
check: neutral tokens resolve to oklch with chroma > 0 and a shared hue.
source: preline themes harvest.css, olive.css; theme.css preline-khaki ramp

text: Tokenise interaction state per role (`primary-hover`, `-focus`, `-active`, `-checked`; `navbar-nav-hover`) so themes own state colours.
why: Opacity-based hovers look muddy on tinted themes; explicit state tokens keep hue control.
check: hover colours come from tokens, not `opacity`/`/90` utilities.

text: Distinguish a "layer" style (same colour as its container, separated by a line) from a "surface" style (filled tint) for secondary controls.
why: White-on-white buttons need a border and a hover tint; grey-filled controls need no border; mixing them per component causes inconsistency.
check: secondary controls use one of the two recipes consistently.

text: For a brutalist/retro direction set every radius to 0 and draw every border in the foreground colour; keep one saturated accent.
why: Preline's retro theme achieves the whole look with these two moves.
check: all border-radius 0; border colours = foreground colour.

text: Label low-contrast "comfort" themes as such and verify muted text against AA before using them for body copy.
why: Harvest/cashmere/olive are deliberately low-contrast; their muted-foreground-1 (khaki/stone-500..600) can fall near the AA line.
check: contrast(muted-foreground-1, background) >= 4.5 for text under 18px.

text: Assign every colour step one job (1-2 background, 3/4/5 component bg normal/hover/pressed, 6 non-interactive border, 7 interactive border, 8 strong border and focus ring, 9 solid, 10 solid hover, 11 low-contrast text, 12 high-contrast text) and have components reference steps, never raw hex.
why: A fixed job per step lets one component recolour across every hue and both themes with no per-hue exceptions.
check: grep component CSS for hex literals outside the token layer; every `background`, `border-color`, `color` resolves to a `--accent-N`/`--gray-N` token.

text: Use step 11 for secondary text and step 12 for primary text on a step 1-2 background; never use step 9-10 as body text colour.
why: The scale is built so 11 and 12 reach APCA Lc 60 and Lc 90 on step 2; 9-10 are only guaranteed against white or dark foreground.
check: compute APCA/WCAG for each text token against its background; text on step 2 must be >= Lc 60 (secondary) and >= Lc 90 (primary).

text: Put dark text (not white) on solid step 9/10 fills for sky, mint, lime, yellow and amber; white on all other hues. Store the on-solid colour as its own token (`--accent-contrast`: amber #21201c, lime #1d211c, mint #1a211e, sky #1c2024, yellow #21201c, else white).
why: Light, high-luminance hues fail contrast with white text at step 9.
applies: forms | SaaS app UI | landing page
check: contrast of button label on its step-9 fill >= 4.5:1 for each hue used.

text: Choose the neutral to match the accent: tinted gray nearest hue (tomato/red/ruby/crimson/pink/plum/purple/violet -> mauve; iris/indigo/blue/sky/cyan -> slate; teal/jade/mint/green -> sage; grass/lime -> olive; yellow/amber/orange/brown/gold/bronze -> sand), or pure gray for a neutral look. Avoid saturated grays as app backgrounds when many coloured badges appear, especially in dark mode.
why: Matching tints harmonise; saturated grays clash with many coloured components.
check: `grayColor` equals pairing table or is `gray`; visual check badges on app background in dark mode.

text: Give every step an alpha variant and use alphas (not opaque greys) for borders, hover overlays and translucent panels.
why: An alpha step composites to the right colour over any surface, so one token survives card-on-background and dark mode.
check: overlay/border tokens are `rgba`/`#rrggbbaa`; no opaque grey borders on cards.

text: Draw component outlines as `0 0 0 1px <gray-a3|a6>` spread shadows layered with soft drop shadows, and redefine the whole shadow stack for dark mode with stronger black alphas.
why: A shadow-border does not change box size, and alpha tint adapts to the surface; dark shadows need more opacity to read.
check: card/popover computed `border-width: 0` with a `box-shadow` containing a 1px spread; dark theme shadow alpha greater than light.

text: Define control sizes as a single ladder where size N sets height, font-size-N, radius-N and padding together (Button 24/32/40/48, TextField 24/32/40) and allow responsive size props.
why: One decision per control instead of four, and mixed controls on one row align without manual tweaks.
check: measure `height` of Button/Input/Select of the same size; must match within 0px.

text: Multiply all spacing, font-size and line-height tokens by one `--scaling` factor (0.9, 0.95, 1, 1.05, 1.1) to offer density without redesign.
why: Keeps proportions identical while letting a dense admin and a comfortable settings page share components.
check: token values equal base x scaling; no px literals in components.

text: Express shape with one multiplier (`--radius-factor`: none 0, small 0.75, medium 1, large 1.5, full 1.5 + `--radius-full`) over a 6-step base (3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16px), and let panels (Card, Dialog, Popover) inherit the theme radius rather than take a prop.
why: A brand's shape language is one switch; panels with their own radius props drift.
check: all component radii resolve to `--radius-N`; none hard-coded.

text: Focus ring is `outline: 2px solid var(--focus-8)` with `outline-offset: 2px` (and Radix uses accent step 8), shown on :focus-visible for every interactive element.
why: One token, consistent in every hue, visible against both surfaces.
check: tab through page; each focusable element gets a 2px outline offset 2px; contrast of ring vs adjacent >= 3:1.

text: Do not modify the vendor scales; add a separate named custom scale (12 steps light + dark + alpha + surface/indicator/track/contrast) for a brand hue and alias it to `accent`.
why: Hand-edited steps break the contrast guarantee and the pairing between steps.
check: custom scale complete: 12 solid, 12 alpha, 4 helper tokens in each mode.

text: Name every colour token as a surface plus its readable foreground (`--primary` / `--primary-foreground`) and always apply them as a pair (`bg-primary text-primary-foreground`).
why: The pair guarantees legible text on that surface and lets a theme change both with one edit.
check: every `bg-X` class has a matching `text-X-foreground` in the same element; lint tokens list for pairs.

text: Derive the radius ladder from one base token with fixed multipliers (0.6, 0.8, 1, 1.4, 1.8, 2.2, 2.6) and have components consume the ladder only.
why: A single edit re-shapes the entire UI; hard-coded radii drift.
check: computed `border-radius` of all components belongs to {0.6,0.8,1,1.4,1.8,2.2,2.6} x --radius (or full).

text: In dark mode make borders and input fills translucent white (10% and 15%) instead of opaque greys, and raise card/popover one lightness step above background (oklch 0.205 on 0.145).
why: Alpha edges composite correctly on any surface and keep hairlines consistent across nested layers.
check: dark `--border` and `--input` have alpha < 1; card L > background L.

text: Use one focus recipe for all focusable controls: border changes to `ring` colour plus a 3px ring at 50% opacity; invalid uses the same shape in destructive at 20% (40% dark).
why: Predictable focus/invalid affordance without per-component design; a visible non-colour-only change (width + border).
check: tab to each control: computed `box-shadow` ring width 3px; `aria-invalid` toggles ring colour.

text: Give every control a size ladder with equal-square icon siblings (nova: xs 24, sm 28, default 32, lg 36, icon 32, icon-xs 24, icon-sm 28, icon-lg 36) and drive density by choosing the style preset, not by per-instance padding.
why: Alignment across rows is automatic; overriding padding breaks inner spacing (icon padding variants).
check: Button/Input/Select heights equal for the same size tier.

text: Add new semantic tokens in three steps: define under `:root` and `.dark`, expose with `@theme inline { --color-X: var(--X) }`, and pair with `-foreground`.
why: Keeps the contract (Tailwind utilities + dark override) intact for custom status colours (success, warning) the base set lacks.
check: every new `--X` has `.dark` value, `@theme inline` mapping and a foreground.

text: Use `ring-1 ring-foreground/10` (not a hard border) for card/popover outlines and keep floating surfaces on `--popover`.
why: Foreground-derived alpha adapts to every base colour and theme; separate popover token lets overlays differ from cards.
check: card computed box-shadow has 1px spread; popover uses popover bg token.

text: Dialogs: max-width `calc(100% - 2rem)` on mobile, `sm:max-w-sm` default, p-4 with gap-4, footer bleeds to edges (`-mx-4 -mb-4 bg-muted/50 border-t`), duration 100ms zoom-in 95 + fade.
why: Predictable mobile gutter, footer separation, fast enter.
check: dialog width at 375px = 343px; footer has muted bg and top border.

text: Express typography with Tailwind steps and a short documented role list (h1 36/40 extrabold tracking-tight; h2 30/36 semibold; h3 24/32; h4 20/28; p 16/28; small 14/20 medium; muted 14 muted-foreground) and set rendered-markdown rhythm from three controls: size, leading, flow.
why: A handful of roles beats a sprawling scale; rhythm controls keep prose consistent across blog, docs and chat.
check: heading/body computed sizes match the role list.

text: Treat colour as roles with allowed adjacencies: use a background only at the page level and never stack backgrounds; put cards, tables, banners and modals on surface colours; use fills only on small areas (buttons, badges); use borders for tables; use icon colours only for standalone icons.
why: Strict adjacency keeps hierarchy legible in a dense UI and keeps contrast guarantees valid.
check: DOM audit: element using a fill token has area below a threshold (for example < 5% viewport) and is not a full-page or full-card background; no nested `bg` tokens.

text: Use `on-fill` text and icon tokens only on their own fill (for example `text-success-on-bg-fill` only on `bg-fill-success`); never put plain `text` on a fill.
why: On-fill pairs are contrast-tuned per fill; mixing "might not pass minimum contrast ratio".
check: pair table: every text over a `bg-fill-*` background uses the matching `*-on-bg-fill` token; computed contrast >= 4.5:1.

text: Give each semantic role one job and a refusal list: critical = impossible, blocked or error only; warning = needs intervention (strongest non-blocking); caution = stalled or not started, never announcements; success = everything is OK, never promotions; info = tips and incentives, never urgent; brand = one primary action per area.
why: If red or yellow is used decoratively, merchants stop trusting it; scarcity keeps the role legible.
check: visual / content review: critical colour appears only with an error/blocked message; at most one `bg-fill-brand` control per region.

text: Choose density per task: high density (tables, index pages, option lists, popovers) with 28px controls and 13px body; low density (focused editing) with larger targets and one card per context; never switch density suddenly inside an action list and never put a high-density table inside a low-density text card without a separate card.
why: Density signals the kind of work; unexpected shifts break scanning rhythm.
check: within one list/card the set of row heights has one value; table card contains no free-form long text blocks.

text: Divide surfaces with nested tinted surfaces (list or 2x2 grid, symmetric); reserve horizontal divider lines for data and index tables.
why: Lines everywhere create visual noise and make a UI look like a document; tinted insets group without extra ink.
check: count of `border-top/bottom` separators inside non-table cards = 0; inset surfaces use `bg-surface-secondary` or `tertiary`.

text: Make nested radii strictly smaller than the parent (card 12px with inset 8px or 4px) and do not change the radius of buttons or badges to fit a container.
why: Concentric corners read as purpose-built; equal radii at different depths look like misalignment.
check: computed `border-radius` of any child with a visible background < parent's radius.

text: Name spacing by multiplier of the 4px base (`space-100` = 4px, `space-400` = 16px), restrict space tokens to margin/padding/gap, and prefer semantic tokens (`space-card-padding`, `space-button-group-gap`, `space-table-cell-padding`) used only on the CSS property they name.
why: A name that equals the maths removes lookup errors; semantic tokens let a component change spacing in one place.
check: all padding/margin/gap values multiples of 4 (allow 2 and 6 half-steps from scale); no space token used for `width`/`height`.

text: Align all line-heights to a 4px multiple (12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 40, 48) and use tabular numerals for currency and any numeric table column; never fake it with a mono font.
why: Stable bounding boxes make vertical rhythm predictable; tabular digits align decimals.
check: computed `line-height` % 4 = 0; `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` on `td`/price spans.

text: Use shadows and bevels only on important interactive objects, in one consistent style, with few layers per screen; darken on press, brighten when raised or active; do not use layering as the first emphasis tool and do not invent unique inset styles for footers.
why: Overused depth turns the page into clutter; consistent lighting is what makes depth read as physical.
check: distinct `box-shadow` values per page <= 4 families; pressed state darker than rest.

text: Animate one element with a meaningful direction (deeper = right-to-left, back = left-to-right), keep feedback motion simple (a checkbox tick, not a scaling halo), avoid per-element staggered page transitions, and use a spinner that spins rather than a static hourglass.
why: Many simultaneous moves disorient; motion that contradicts spatial direction misleads.
check: visual; at most one animated property group per transition; durations from {50..500ms} tokens.

text: Ship a mobile theme as a diff on the same tokens: below 768px raise body-md from 13 to 16px (lh 24), heading-md to 16px, controls one step taller (28 to 32, 32 to 36), card gap 8px, and replace bevels with 1px ring borders.
why: Touch needs larger text and targets; keeping one token vocabulary avoids a second design system.
check: computed body font-size >= 16px and button height >= 32px at 375px width.
source: polaris-tokens `light-mobile` theme; styles.css Polaris-Button size media rules

text: Write buttons as a short imperative in sentence case with no article and no punctuation ("Add tags", "Save", not "Save product" or "Add a tag(s)"); use an icon-only or plus-sign label when the icon is universal; put a red button only on actions that are hard or impossible to undo; lead with one primary action.
why: Predictable, minimal labels are scanned faster and reduce choice paralysis.
check: regex on button text: Title Case, leading articles, trailing punctuation.

text: Write errors as: what is wrong, what to do, specific data, no "invalid", no over-apology, no "we" unless the platform caused it; multiple errors lead with the fix ("To save this product, make 2 changes:" then a list); place the error next to what needs fixing; red for must-fix-now, yellow for workflow warnings.
why: Error text is a task instruction; jargon and apologies add reading time without fixing anything.
check: regex: `invalid`, `Sorry`, `Oops`; each error contains an imperative verb.

text: Do not move focus programmatically without a user action, except to interrupt; move focus to an overlay the user opened, to the error summary after a failed submit, and to content a same-page link points at.
why: Unexpected focus jumps break screen-reader and keyboard flow.
check: code review: `.focus()` calls only in handlers tied to a user event or error submit.

text: Respect the system's licence boundary: when a third-party system forbids lookalikes (Polaris requires non-Shopify apps to be dissimilar and visually distinct), borrow principles and number ranges only and diverge in palette, shape language and type voice.
why: Legal exposure and, separately, sameness: this engine's first principle is divergence.
check: licence field recorded in the system profile; direction file lists what differs.

text: Pair every background role with a named foreground role and use no other text colour on it: page surface -> on-surface-1..3; accent-container -> on-accent; error/warning/success/info-container -> on-{state}; and document the allowed foreground steps next to each background step.
why: Contrast becomes a property of the pair, not of a designer's eye, and survives theme and dark-mode changes.
check: In the token file every `*-container` has an `on-*` partner; computed contrast of each pair >= 4.5:1 light and dark (script over all pairs).
source: v1 new-global-styling-hooks-guidance (Surface, Container, On Surface, Accent Containers); cosmos.global.tokens.css

text: Split the border colour by role: `border-1` (decorative dividers, may be about 1.7:1) and `border-2` (interactive controls, >= 3:1 and in practice about 6.7:1 light / 3.4:1 dark). Interactive elements use border-2; presentational ones use border-1; disabled uses a dedicated disabled-border.
why: WCAG 1.4.11 applies only to UI component boundaries; separating the tokens stops decorative lines from being over-darkened.
check: Contrast of `input, button, select` border vs surface >= 3:1; of `hr, .divider` unconstrained but flagged if > 4:1 (too heavy).
source: guidance page (Border Colors); tokens: border-1 `light-dark(#c9c9c9,#444)`, border-2 `light-dark(#5c5c5c,#757575)` [computed 1.66 / 6.69 light]

text: Mirror the lightness ladder for dark mode and keep one pivot step identical across modes; reference steps by semantic tokens so a component never contains a dark-mode branch. Emit values with CSS `light-dark()`.
why: A single declaration serves both modes and the pivot guarantees a mid-tone that reads on both light and dark surfaces.
check: No `@media (prefers-color-scheme)` inside component CSS; every colour token in the theme file is `light-dark(a, b)` or a pivot (assert a == b); palette dark step = light step at 100-N within 1 hex step.

text: Express density as comfy/compact value pairs on spacing and font-size tokens (spacing-var-N, font-scale-var-N), switched in one place, and collapse only the mid-to-large part of the type scale in compact (16 -> 14, 20 -> 16, 24 -> 20; small sizes unchanged).
why: Users with data-heavy screens want a global switch; keeping small type fixed protects legibility.
check: Token file has a compact value for each `*-var-*`; compact never drops body text below 13px or interactive targets below 24px.

text: Resolve component properties through a three-step var() fallback (component hook, shared role hook, global token) and never reassign global tokens inside a component.
why: Brands override at the lowest altitude that satisfies them; reassigning a global breaks every other consumer and future system updates.
check: CSS contains no `--g-*: value` declarations outside the theme file; component rules use `var(--c-x, var(--s-y, var(--g-z)))`.
source: v1 guidance page ("Do not reassign globals"); slds2.base.css `.slds-card`

text: Pick the container radius at theme level (20px Cosmos / 4px Lightning Blue) and let cards, modals, popovers read it from one shared token; buttons read a separate shared button radius (pill vs 4px); inputs 8px (4px).
why: Roundness is a brand decision; per-component pixel values drift apart.
check: Distinct border-radius values <= 5; container-radius token referenced by every card-like surface.

text: Separate containers by surface tone when shadow and border are zero: a white container-1 on a `#f3f3f3` surface-2 page is enough; add shadow-2 (or a 1px border-1) only in themes that opt in.
why: Cosmos cards are borderless and shadowless; adding both a hairline and a wide shadow is the generic card tell.
check: Each card has at most one of: border, shadow, tone-shift as separator (visual).

text: Key feedback to icon + text, never hue alone, and choose the status palette per theme (error hue is pink in Cosmos, red in Lightning Blue); keep container fills at step 90 light / 30 dark with on-state text at step 40 light / 90 dark.
why: Re-hued semantics break habit; fixed step recipes keep contrast across hues.
check: Status elements contain an svg/icon or a text label; container/text contrast >= 4.5:1.

text: Name durations on a short semantic list with frame counts (immediately 50ms/3f, quickly 100ms/6f, promptly 200ms/12f, slowly 400ms/24f) and keep toasts at 4.8s (short) or 9.6s (medium); do not hard-code easings in components (SLDS does, which is its weakness).
why: A short named set removes timing drift; frame annotations tie values to 60fps rendering.
check: Every `transition-duration` is one of {0, 50, 100, 200, 400}ms or uses the token; easing values reference a token.
source: cosmos.global.tokens.css duration tokens; slds2.base.css (hard-coded cubic-beziers = counter-example)

text: Use rem-based spacing/sizing/font tokens so layout follows user font size, and give measure tokens in `ch` (content 20/45/60ch; headings 20/25/35ch).
why: Respects browser text-size settings; `ch` caps line length without media queries.
check: No `px` in padding/margin/font-size tokens; paragraph `max-width` in ch between 45 and 75.

text: Allow exactly one high-attention element or group per view: one filled accent action, one emphasized (shadowed) container group; every other control uses the neutral/gray style and selected nav items must not compete with the primary action.
why: Attention is a signal-to-noise budget; two loud elements cancel each other.
check: Count elements with the accent fill + elements with elevated shadow per viewport screenshot; fail if > 1 accent-filled button or > 1 emphasized container group (visual + `[data-accent]` count).

text: Group with proximity before borders: separate sections with a spacing step (e.g. items `spacing-75` 4px, section gap `spacing-400` 24px, card groups `spacing-300` 16px / `spacing-500` 32px) and a section title; add a divider or border only when spacing cannot do it, and use at most two border widths (2px, 1px dense).
why: Borders fill and disrupt negative space; proximity is the cheaper, calmer grouping cue.
check: Count of distinct border widths <= 2; number of elements with a visible border per card group; ratio of inter-group gap to intra-group gap >= 2.

text: Pick spacing from a perceptually stepped scale (1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 56, 64, 80, 96) and grow small gaps with component size (base-gap 4px in extra-small/small controls, 6px medium to extra-large, 8px for 2XL+; accessory-gap 3 -> 9px).
why: Fixed 8px multiples crowd small components and make large values indistinguishable (4 to 8 is +100%, 72 to 80 is +11%).
check: All margin/padding/gap values belong to the scale above (tolerance 0); adjacent steps differ by 10-100%.

text: Use the Major Second (x1.125) type scale from a 14px base: 10, 11, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 25, 28, 32, 36, 40, 45, 51, 58, 65, 73px; take sizes only from this list.
why: Custom sizes break the hierarchy relationships the styles were built on.
check: Every computed `font-size` is in the list; headings use Heading (weight 800), titles 700, body 400, detail 500 uppercase +0.06em.

text: Set Body and Code line height to 1.5x; give Heading, Title and Detail per-size even-pixel line heights from 130% down to 115% (14 -> 18, 20 -> 24, 28 -> 32, 36 -> 42, 73 -> 84); never fully justify text; aim for about 70 characters per line (50-120 hard range).
why: Tight display lines vs open reading lines; line height must shrink as size grows.
check: `line-height / font-size` for `p` = 1.5; for h1-h3 between 1.15 and 1.3; `text-align` not `justify`; `max-width` of paragraphs 50-120ch.

text: Use tabular numerals for numbers in components and tables, right-align numeric columns, and reserve all caps for Detail text (11-18px, weight 500, +0.06em, gray-600) or long-form marketing.
why: Equal digit width stops values jittering; all caps harms accessibility inside components.
check: `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` on table cells and counters; `text-transform: uppercase` only on elements with letter-spacing >= 0.05em.

text: Use only the supplied colour steps and never transform them (no lighten/darken/opacity hacks); build tints and shades by choosing another step. Pair roles by index: text on a layer uses gray-700..1000 (light) and the matching step in dark; colour fills with white text use the 900/800 index, and yellow/orange/chartreuse/celery fills take black text.
why: Steps are perceptually uniform and contrast-tested; programmatic changes break both.
check: No `color-mix`, `lighten()`, `rgba()` derived from tokens in component CSS; contrast of each text/background pair >= 4.5:1 (3:1 for large and non-text).

text: Never rely on colour alone: every colour-coded state (negative, positive, notice, informative) carries a label or icon; two-tone pairs use the 100 step for background and the 900 step (light) for the glyph.
why: CVD users cannot separate red/green/orange by hue; Spectrum flags two-tone pairs as not CVD safe.
check: Each element using a status colour contains text or an svg/icon.

text: Build page surfaces from layers: base gray-25, layer-1 gray-50, layer-2 (gray-25 light / gray-75 dark), pasteboard (gray-100 light / gray-25 dark), elevated (gray-25 / gray-75 plus drop shadow) and map each to a distinct dark-theme value rather than inverting.
why: Dimensionality has to survive the theme switch; a layer is a role, not a colour.
check: Page uses <= 4 distinct background tokens; each has a dark counterpart in the token file.

text: Compose shadows from three layers (key = edge, transition, ambient = depth) in black, give containers no shadow by default (emphasized, hover, elevated, dragged are the only four), and triple the opacity in dark theme (8/12/16% -> 24/36/48%); omit the shadow when an overlay already separates the element.
why: A three-layer shadow keeps the edge crisp while the depth stays soft; dark needs more opacity; overlay + shadow double counts.
applies: SaaS app UI | landing page cards.
check: `box-shadow` values on page match one of four tokens; layer count 3; dark alpha ~3x light.

text: Radius scales with component size and nests: small controls 4px, most components 8px, panels/large cards 10px, dialogs 16px, full (height/2) for buttons, avatars, search; when nesting use inner = outer - gap for focus rings, optical balance elsewhere.
why: Larger objects carry larger radii so gaps look even; a formula mismatch in cards looks worse than optical tuning.
check: Child radius <= parent radius in nested boxes; distinct radii <= 6.

text: Use density as a property of collections and containers only: compact = spacing tokens one step down, spacious = one step up (e.g. table item padding compact spacing-100 8px / regular spacing-200 12px / spacious spacing-300 16px; card edge-to-content medium 12 / 16 / 20); do not make buttons or text fields taller to "be spacious" (use the size ladder instead).
why: Density and size are orthogonal; conflating them destroys the size hierarchy.
check: Control heights stay on {20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 56, 64}; table row padding is one of the three densities.

text: For every component write the state-support table (Default, Hover, Down, Keyboard focus, Disabled, Selected, Dragged, Error) and mark unsupported states explicitly; an unsupported state is a decision recorded, not a gap.
why: Teams otherwise improvise missing states differently.
check: Spec file for each component contains all eight state keys with supported/not-supported values.

text: Button content standard: verb label, 1-2 words (max 4), < 20 characters, sentence case, no punctuation, same word as elsewhere in the flow ("Sign up" not "Submit"); min width 2.25x height; horizontal padding = half the height; pending state only for actions expected under 5 seconds and only after a 1 second delay.
why: Labels name the outcome; the delay avoids spinner flicker.
applies: landing page | forms | SaaS app UI.
check: Button text length <= 20 chars, no trailing punctuation, starts with a verb (lint list); computed `min-width >= 2.25 x height`.

text: Build colour ramps in a perceptual space with equal lightness per step across hues, and publish the pairing rule: steps >= 5 apart for small text (4.5:1), >= 4 apart for icons and large text (3:1), valid on the lightest tint of each hue.
why: Contrast becomes a property of the step numbers, so any designer can pick a compliant pair without a checker, and tinted backgrounds are safe.
check: for every hue, compute contrast for step pairs (n, n+5) >= 4.5 and (n, n+4) >= 3.0 against white and against step 50.

text: Keep an RGB-triplet twin for every ramp colour (`--c-500-rgb: 84, 105, 212`) so alpha variants are `rgb(var(--c-500-rgb) / .5)`.
why: Alpha overlays then stay on-palette without a second token set.
check: every ramp token has a `-rgb` sibling; no hard-coded rgba() colours outside tokens.

text: Tint shadows with the brand's cool hue and stack two layers: a large soft one with negative spread and a small tight one; do not use a single grey blur.
why: Coloured, spread-negative shadows read as part of the surface palette and avoid the muddy halo of black shadows.
check: card box-shadow has >= 2 layers, first layer colour hue within 20 degrees of the brand hue, spread negative.

text: If using a light display weight (300) in headings, pair it with negative tracking scaled to size (-0.01em at 20-34px, -0.02em at 32-48px, -0.025em at 56px) and keep UI controls at 400 or above.
why: Thin strokes need tight tracking to hold a headline together; thin buttons lose affordance.
check: h1-h3 weight 300 requires letter-spacing <= -0.01em; `button`, `a.button` weight >= 400.

text: Do not set body copy in weight 300 below 17px with a mid-tone slate text colour unless contrast is at least 4.5:1 and the font is a display-quality grotesk; otherwise use 400.
why: Stripe's own body (15-16px, 300, #50617a) is only 6.3:1 and thin; copying it with a default font fails legibility.
check: body p at weight < 400 and size < 17px flagged; contrast >= 4.5:1.

text: Pick one ink, one body grey, one accent and one button grammar per site and assert it across every template; Stripe's inconsistency (#061b31 vs #0a2540 ink, #533afd vs #635bff purple, 4px vs pill buttons) is a defect to avoid.
why: Template drift is visible to the eye and costs trust, especially in finance.
check: distinct set of text colours with > 50 uses has <= 4 members; accent hex count == 1 (plus tints); button radius set size 1.

text: Compute readable foreground colours (`on-primary`, `on-background`, `on-danger`) as tokens from the fill, never let a consumer pick the text colour.
why: Brand colours vary in lightness; automatic on-colours keep AA when themed.
check: each fill token has a paired `on-*` token and contrast >= 4.5:1.

text: For third-party or white-label surfaces, expose three tiers (theme, variables, rules), accept only token values (no arbitrary CSS) for spacing, colour and type, and make state-dependent styling automatic where overriding would confuse behaviour.
why: Constrained customisation preserves accessibility and consistency across thousands of integrations.
check: theming API surface: finite variable list, typed values, no raw CSS escape hatch for contrast-critical properties.

text: Use 1px structural frame lines and a single bleeding art object for editorial pages rather than boxed cards everywhere; place inverse (dark navy) bands to break long light runs.
why: Structure becomes the decoration, letting one gradient carry the brand.
check: visual; page has <= 1 full-bleed art object per fold and <= 2 inverse bands in the first 3 screens.

text: Derive every semantic colour (background, foreground, card, popover, muted, accent, border, input, ring, status) from a short list of theme inputs in OKLCH; themes are files that set inputs, never lists of finished colours.
why: Keeps ratios (elevation, text contrast, border strength) identical across themes and lets one hue change re-skin the product.
check: theme file declares at most 12 inputs; grep that no semantic token in a theme file is a literal colour except stepped scales.

text: Split the accent into four tokens with separate contrast jobs: ink (small text and indicators, 4.5:1), plate (button fill under its own foreground, 4.5:1), bright (focus ring, selected state, 3:1 non-text), fixed brand (identity surfaces only).
why: A single accent cannot be both a readable text colour and a button fill in both modes; in dark the readable ink is too bright to be a plate.

text: Express elevation as `background lightness + signed step * ratio` with shared ratios (1, 1.5, 2, 3) and a step per theme (dark +0.025, light +0.024 from a soft-grey canvas), so higher surfaces are lighter in both modes.
why: One direction of elevation in both modes avoids dark-mode inversion bugs; a soft-grey light canvas leaves headroom to brighten toward white.
check: card, popover, secondary lightness strictly increase; light canvas L <= 0.995 (not pure white) when elevation uses brightening.

text: Give status colours one shared chroma and clamp each hue to its perceptual category, anchored at mode-specific lightness; choose on-fill text by a hard flip at L 0.62.
why: Warning must always read amber and destructive always red under any brand hue; shared chroma keeps them from out-shouting each other; the flip guarantees legible text without per-colour picks.

text: Define focus as two shared recipes (offset ring for controls, inset outline for dense rows), colour it from the bright accent at about 55% alpha, and keep outline and ring properties out of transition lists.
why: Consistent focus is recognised instantly; transitioning it delays feedback for keyboard users; inset avoids clipping in tables and flush surfaces.
check: every `:focus-visible` style resolves to one of two recipes; `transition-property` on interactive elements excludes outline-*, box-shadow ring when used for focus.

text: Give every control a complete state set in the spec: rest, hover, focus-visible, disabled (opacity .5, pointer-events none), invalid (aria-invalid bg and border plus hover and focus variants), read-only; and let unavailable-with-reason actions stay focusable.

text: Write the UI copy rules next to the component rules: action verbs on buttons, sentence case for labels and headings, title case for page names, one sentence for tooltips, no exclamation marks outside destructive confirmations, no marketing vocabulary.
why: Voice drift is as visible as spacing drift and is checkable.
check: lint button labels (starts with a verb), reject `!` in toasts except destructive, reject words from the avoid-list.

text: When migrating tokens, ship a compatibility alias file that maps old names onto the new semantics, forbid new references to it, and delete entries as consumers move.
why: Prevents big-bang rewrites while keeping the new model clean.
check: grep: zero new references to names listed in compat.css in files changed in the last N commits.

text: Size controls from a named ladder and keep one ladder per product layer; do not mix two ladders in one surface (Supabase has 26/34/38/42/50px legacy and 36/40/44px shadcn layers coexisting; treat that as a defect to avoid).
why: Mixed ladders produce adjacent controls that differ by 2-4px.
check: set of control heights on one screen has at most 3 values and all come from one ladder.
