text: Start with user needs: research, analyse data, talk to users; do not assume, and remember that what users ask for is not always what they need.
why: Building without needs means building the wrong thing.
check: process: brief states the user need and evidence before visual design.

text: Do the hard work to make it simple: simplicity of use matters more than the look of simplicity; reject "it has always been that way".
why: Making something look simple is easy; making it simple to use means removing underlying complexity.
check: count of steps, fields, and decisions per task versus the previous version (should go down).

text: Iterate: release small, test with real users, add what works, delete what does not, and be willing to scrap a failing prototype.
why: Iteration reduces risk and turns failures into lessons.
check: process: at least one tested iteration recorded in evals.

text: Treat accessibility as part of good design: be inclusive, legible and readable even if it costs elegance; design for needs, not audiences.
why: Those who most need a service often find it hardest to use.
check: run the a11y checklist (A11Y-xx) on every page.

text: Understand the context of use (library, phone, first-time web user) and design for people, not for a screen; build services, not just pages.
why: Context drives constraints (small screen, bad connection, stress).
check: brief names the usage context and device; test at 375 px with throttled network.

text: Be consistent, not uniform: reuse the same language and patterns; deviate only when research says it is better, then share why.
why: Familiarity lowers effort, but a rule book must not freeze improvement.
check: the same action has the same label and component across the product (grep repeated verbs: "Continue" vs "Next").

text: Do less: reuse and link rather than rebuilding; keep to the irreducible core; and minimise environmental impact (principle 11, added 2 April 2025).
why: Less to build, run, and carry.
check: page weight and request counts versus budget; remove features without evidence.

text: Ask one question per page by default; put the question in the `<label>` or `<legend>` and make that the page heading (`<h1>`) so screen readers hear it once. When asking several related things, use a statement heading instead and style each label or legend for scanning.
why: Focus on the specific question and one hearing for screen-reader users.
check: on single-question pages: `h1` is inside `label` or `legend`; on multi-question pages `h1` is a statement and not inside a label or legend.

text: Every question page has a back link, a page heading and a "Continue" button; the button is labelled "Continue" (not "Next") and aligned to the left edge of the form.
why: Users do not trust browser back; the left-aligned primary action is not missed.
check: page has `a.back-link` before `main`, one `h1`, and a `button` with text "Continue" whose left edge equals the form column's left edge.
source: patterns/question-pages/ > How it works, Back link, Continue button; components/button.

text: Do not break the browser Back button: Back returns to the previous page in the state the user saw. Exception: after one-time actions such as payment, show a sensible message instead of letting the action repeat.
why: Predictability and safety.
check: step through a flow, press Back: values restored, no duplicate submit.

text: Only ask for information you need and only once per journey; pre-populate or offer carried-forward answers instead of re-asking. Allow "I do not know" where valid.
why: Each field costs completion.
check: audit duplicate field names across steps (same `autocomplete` token twice in one journey = flag).
source: patterns/question-pages/ > When to use, How it works.

text: Mark optional fields with "(optional)" in the label (or legend for radios and checkboxes); never mark mandatory fields with asterisks.
why: Most fields are required, so flagging the exceptions is quieter and clearer.
check: no `*` in label text; optional inputs have "(optional)" in the label.
source: patterns/question-pages/ > When to use this pattern.

text: Use a progress indicator only if testing shows the form is still hard without one; use a simple "Question X of Y" style and only include the total if it is reliable. Avoid the stepper that shows all steps, lets you jump back, and marks the current one.
why: That stepper is often unnoticed, takes space, scales poorly on mobile and is hard to label (one team removed a 12-step indicator with no effect on completion).
check: step-indicator element lists <= 1 step label (current) or a "Step X of Y" text.

text: Avoid range sliders; if used, provide a non-drag way to choose a value.
why: Hard to use for some people; WCAG 2.5.1 Pointer Gestures.
check: every `input[type=range]` has an accompanying number input or buttons.

text: Every text input has a visible label placed above the input, short and direct, in sentence case, without a trailing colon.
why: A persistent label is read reliably by all users.
check: `label` is a block above its `input` (label bottom <= input top); label text does not end in `:`.

text: Do not use placeholder text for labels, hints or examples.
why: It vanishes when typing (a problem for memory conditions and review), some screen readers skip it, and default placeholder colours often fail contrast.
check: `input[placeholder]` count 0 where the label is missing; if a placeholder is present, contrast >= 4.5:1.
source: components/text-input > Avoid placeholder text; components/textarea > How it works.

text: Hint text is a single short sentence without a full stop, for help most users need, contains no links, and is attached to the input via `aria-describedby`. For long explanation use body content above a specific question label instead of a hint.
why: Screen readers read the whole hint on every focus; links in hints are not announced as links.
check: `.hint` length < 100 characters, does not end with `.`, contains no `a`; has an id referenced by the input's `aria-describedby`.
source: components/text-input > Hint text; patterns/question-pages/ > Hint text and Asking complex questions.

text: Size inputs to the expected content: fixed-width inputs for known lengths (postcode, phone) and fluid-width classes (full, three-quarters, two-thirds, half, third, quarter) otherwise; fixed widths are sized for 20, 10, 5, 4, 3 and 2 characters.
why: Width signals the expected answer length.
check: postcode and similar fixed-length fields have `max-width` within ~1 ch of expected; no full-width input for a 4-digit answer.

text: For whole numbers use `type="text"` with `inputmode="numeric"`; for decimals use `inputmode="decimal"`; avoid `input type="number"`; for negative numbers use plain text input without `inputmode`.
why: `type=number` allows scroll-wheel increments and gives no feedback on bad input; some mobile keypads cannot enter negatives.
check: `input[type=number]` count 0; numeric answers have `inputmode`.

text: For long codes or sequences the user will not have memorised, style the text to separate characters (letter spacing); not needed for phone numbers or postcodes.
why: Helps visual checking.
check: code inputs have `letter-spacing` > 0 and often `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`.

text: Prefixes and suffixes (such as "£", "kg") sit outside the input, are never the only description (the label or hint must state the unit too), and validation must tolerate users typing the symbol themselves.
why: Screen readers do not announce prefixes; users double-type symbols; browser icons can overlap inner content.
check: prefix element is a sibling of the input with `aria-hidden=true`; label names the unit.

text: Use `autocomplete` tokens (for example `postal-code`, `bday-day`, `bday-month`, `bday-year`) on inputs that match an input purpose.
why: WCAG 1.3.5 Identify input purpose, AA.
check: inputs for name, email, address, DOB, tel have the right token.
source: components/text-input > Use the autocomplete attribute; components/date-input.

text: Never disable copy and paste in text inputs or textareas.
why: People paste from other sources.
check: no `onpaste` preventDefault (same check as VWI-11).
source: components/text-input; components/textarea > Do not disable copy and paste.

text: Avoid `maxlength`: it truncates silently (including pasted text), blocks usual formatting such as spaces in postcodes, and confuses assistive technology and voice control. If a limit is technical, state it in the hint and only error after normalising the value; for long text use the character count component.
why: Silent truncation loses data.
check: `[maxlength]` on free-text inputs count 0 (allowed on fields whose limit is physically fixed like a 6-digit code).
source: components/text-input > Avoid restricting the length of a user's input.

text: Disable spellcheck (`spellcheck="false"`) on names, emails, reference numbers and NI-style numbers.
why: Red lines on non-words mislead.
check: matching inputs have `spellcheck=false`.
source: components/text-input > How and when to spellcheck.

text: Do not use HTML5 validation: add `novalidate` to forms and do not put `required` on inputs; implement server-side validation always, and add client-side validation only when research shows a need.
why: Browser bubbles cannot be styled or placed consistently or proven accessible; client rules can be bypassed or fail.
check: `form[novalidate]`; `input[required]` count 0; server returns the same errors without JS.
source: patterns/validation > Turn off HTML5 validation, Client side and server side validation. Note the tension with the A11Y/engine practice of `aria-required`; see section 5.

text: Validate when the user submits or moves to the next step, not when they leave a field. Avoid validating before they finish typing unless research shows net benefit (the character-count component is the exception).
why: Early validation punishes slow typists and screen-reader users.
check: blur an empty required field: no error appears; click Continue: errors appear.
source: patterns/validation > When to tell the user about validation errors.

text: Accept input in different unambiguous formats and strip noise before validating (spaces, hyphens, brackets, dashes, full stops, invisible characters, characters from dictation or accidental copy-paste padding); reject only what cannot be correct or is too ambiguous (for example month "13").
why: Format errors are hard to see and fix.
check: submit a postcode with and without space, a phone number with brackets and dashes, a value with trailing spaces: all accepted.
source: patterns/validation > When to use, How it works.

text: On a failed validation redisplay the form with all fields as the user filled them (both valid and invalid answers), prefix the page `<title>` with "Error: ", show an error summary at the top and move keyboard focus to it, and show error messages beside the fields.
why: Users can see, edit and avoid retyping.
check: after invalid submit: `document.title` starts with "Error: "; `document.activeElement` is the summary; field values preserved.
source: patterns/validation > How to tell the user about validation errors; components/error-message.

text: The error summary is shown whenever there is any validation error (even one), is the first thing in the main container (below breadcrumbs or back link, above `h1`), has the heading "There is a problem", and links each error to its answer: to the field for single inputs; to the first field in error for date inputs (or the first field if unknown); to the first radio or checkbox for groups.
why: Orientation and quick navigation for keyboard and screen-reader users.
check: summary `h2` text equals "There is a problem"; each `a[href^="#"]` target resolves to an input id; summary precedes the `h1` in DOM order.
source: components/error-summary > When to use, How it works, Where to put the error summary.

text: Error summary messages use the same words as the messages next to the fields.
why: Consistency lowers cognitive effort and makes sense out of context.
check: text of each summary link equals text of its field error (minus the hidden "Error:" prefix).
source: components/error-summary > How it works; components/error-message > Be consistent.

text: Place the field error message in red after the question and hint text, add a red left border to the form group to link message and question, and (for multi-field questions like dates) add a red border to the specific field in error. The error message component includes a visually hidden "Error:" prefix for screen readers.
why: Spatial and non-visual association.
check: `.error-message` follows `.hint` in DOM order; contains visually hidden "Error:"; has a text colour contrasting >= 4.5:1; form-group has a border-left of 5px in error colour.
source: components/error-message > How it works; styles/colour (error #ca3535). Border width 5 px from govuk-frontend settings (`$govuk-border-width-form-group-error: 5px`).

text: Write errors that say what happened and how to fix it, in plain English, in positive terms, mirroring the label's wording ("How many hours do you work a week?" gives "Enter how many hours you work a week"). Avoid jargon, "forbidden", "illegal", "you forgot", "please", "sorry", "valid/invalid", "oops", and generic text such as "This field is required", "Answer the question", "Select an option", "An error occurred".
why: Specific messages work out of context and recover users.
check: lint every error string against the banned word list; ensure it contains a word from the label.
source: components/error-message > Match up error messages to labels, Be clear and concise, Be specific.

text: Do not repeat a hint's example inside the error if the example is already on screen. Prefer imperative form for empty fields ("Enter your first name") and a description for limit failures ("First name must be 35 characters or less"), used consistently.
why: Avoids clutter; consistent grammar.
check: empty errors start with "Enter|Select"; limit errors start with the field name.

text: Use template messages per field type. Text input: empty "Enter [x]"; too long "[x] must be [n] characters or less"; too short "[x] must be [n] characters or more"; both "[x] must be between [n] and [n] characters"; banned characters "[x] must not include [chars]"; unknown allowed set "[x] must only include [allowed]"; not a number "[x] must be a number, like 30"; not whole "[x] must be a whole number, like 30"; low "[x] must be [n] or more"; high "[x] must be [n] or fewer"; range "[x] must be between [a] and [b]"; money "[x] must include pence, like 123.45 or 156.00" or "must not include pence, like 123 or 156".
why: Proven wording tested in live services.
check: string match against the templates.

text: Radios: empty yes/no "Select yes if [x]"; two non-yes/no options "Select if [x]"; more than two "Select [x]". Checkboxes: nothing selected with options "Select if [x]" or without options "Select [x]"; none plus another checked "Select [options] or select '[none label]'". Select: tell the user to select an option, named. Date: empty "Enter [x]"; incomplete "[x] must include a [day/month/year]"; impossible "[x] must be a real date"; future/past "[x] must be in the past" and relatives (today or in the past, in the future, today or in the future, same as or after/before, between).
why: Consistent messages per control.
check: string match.
source: components/radios, checkboxes, select, date-input > Error messages.

text: For multiple date errors, show the highest priority: missing or incomplete first, then information that cannot be correct (month 13), then other failures; highlight only the failing field(s) and name the field in the message.
why: One clear fix at a time.
check: with two errors, only one message appears per date question.

text: Never use an error message to tell users they are ineligible, lack permission, or hit a service problem; take them to an explanatory page with next steps (or the problem-with-the-service, page-not-found, service-unavailable pages).
why: Errors are for fixable input mistakes.
check: error component usage restricted to validation; eligibility failures route to a page with `h1` and next-step links.
source: components/error-message > When not to use; patterns/validation > When not to use.

text: Track how often each error is seen, to improve content, A/B test variants or redesign the journey.
why: Error frequency finds weak questions.
check: analytics event per error type exists.

text: Button text is sentence case and describes the action ("Save and continue", "Continue", "Start now", "Sign in", "Pay", "Add another", "Confirm and send" or "Accept and send" when legal text must be agreed, "Sign out"); add words when needed ("Add another address").
why: Specific action labels reduce hesitation.
check: button text matches sentence case regex; no generic "Submit", "OK", "Click here".

text: Use one default (primary) button per page; use secondary buttons sparingly; simplify the page or split it rather than adding many calls to action.
why: More than one main call to action weakens all.
check: count of primary-styled `button` per view = 1.

text: Start buttons on a start page are links (`<a>`), not form buttons, and use the primary action wording "Start now"; green start buttons raised click-through in testing.
why: They navigate; evidence from GOV.UK testing.
check: `a.start-button` has `href`, `role=button`; computed colour is the success/green button style.
source: components/button > Start buttons, Research (green improved click-through).

text: Warning (red) buttons are only for serious, hard-to-undo destructive actions, used very sparingly; use another button style for the initial action and a warning button for the final confirmation; never rely on red alone (the text and context must make the consequence clear).
why: Frequent red buttons lose meaning; colour alone is not accessible.
check: count of destructive buttons per page <= 1; text names the consequence ("Delete account").

text: Avoid disabled buttons; they have poor contrast and confuse users. Use only if research shows they help.
why: No explanation for being disabled.
check: `button:disabled` count on idle pages = 0.
source: components/button > Disabled buttons. Agrees with VWI-15.

text: On dark backgrounds use the inverse (white) button and keep white against its background at 4.5:1 or better; group two or more buttons in a button group; align the primary action to the left edge of the form.
why: Legibility, spacing, scan path.
check: contrast white vs background >= 4.5; sibling buttons are wrapped in a flex container with gap.
source: components/button > Buttons on dark backgrounds, Grouping buttons.

text: Prevent accidental double submission: use `data-prevent-double-click="true"` when research shows duplicates, give feedback (spinner or modal) on slow connections, and also protect server-side.
why: Double clicks come from old habits, slow feedback and motor impairments.
check: double-click the submit button: one request.
source: components/button > Stop users from accidentally sending information more than once.

text: Radios are for one choice from a list; checkboxes for several (or one on/off). Always put the control to the left of its label, and group in a `fieldset` with a `legend` that states the question.
why: Left placement helps magnifier users; groups are announced with the question.
check: `input[type=radio], input[type=checkbox]` left edge < label left edge; each group inside `fieldset > legend`.
source: components/radios and checkboxes > How it works.

text: Do not pre-select radios or checkboxes in questions; add a hint such as "Select one option" or "Select all that apply" because the visual difference alone is not enough.
why: Pre-selection causes missed questions and wrong answers.
check: `input:checked` on initial render of a question page: count 0.

text: Order options alphabetically by default; order by popularity only with extreme caution (bias); include "None of the above" or "I do not know" where valid, shown last after a divider ("or"); a "none" checkbox repeats the key part of the question and unchecks the others.
why: Predictable scan order, no bias.
check: option labels sorted alphabetically (locale-aware) unless justified; "none" option is last.
source: components/radios > How it works; checkboxes > Add an option for 'none'.

text: Use inline radios only for exactly two short options; they still stack on small screens. Do not conditionally reveal questions inside inline radios.
why: Layout and clarity.
check: inline radio groups have 2 options and each label < ~20 characters.

text: Conditionally reveal only a short, simple related question (not other content); if it is complicated or multi-part, move it to the next page.
why: Revealed content may not be announced (a known WCAG 4.1.2 gap); testing showed screen-reader users coped only with simple ones.
check: revealed region contains one field.
source: components/radios, checkboxes > Conditionally revealing a related question, Known issues.

text: Add per-item hints only as single short sentences without full stops and without links; use the smaller radios/checkboxes only on information-dense screens or filters.
why: Standard size is more noticeable; small ones suit repeat use.
check: hint length; standard control size otherwise (control box 40 px with 44 px touch target; small 24 px, per govuk-frontend SCSS).
source: components/radios, checkboxes; govuk-frontend `radios/_mixin.scss` ($govuk-radios-size 40px, touch gutter 4px, small 24px).

text: Use a select only as a last resort in public services; first ask questions to reduce options or use radios. Do not pre-select in questions (settings may pre-select), and do not support `select multiple`; use checkboxes instead.
why: Users struggle: cannot close, try to type, confuse focus with selection, pinch-zoom, miss scrolling.
check: `select` count minimal; `select[multiple]` count 0.
source: components/select > When to use, How it works, Research.

text: Ask for memorable dates with three fields (day, month, year) in a fieldset, accept month names and abbreviations, never auto-tab between fields, use `bday-day/month/year` autocomplete for date of birth, and use valid example dates in the hint.
why: Teacher-training service saw errors fall sharply after accepting month names; auto-tab collides with keyboard control.
check: date question has 3 `input`s inside `fieldset > legend`; "jan" and "January" accepted; no `keyup` handler that moves focus.

text: Do not use the date input when users probably do not know the exact date; do not use a calendar for known dates.
why: Wrong input type for recall.
check: review.

text: Textarea height is proportional to the expected answer via `rows`; use the character count only when there is a real reason (evidence of over-long answers or a legal/technical limit), set the limit above what most users need, optionally show the count only past a threshold (the page's markup example is `data-threshold="75"`, i.e. 75% of the limit; its live demo says the count appears past 850 of 1000), and let users exceed the limit then show an error rather than truncating.
why: Preserves pasted text and avoids stress.
check: textarea `rows` matches expected length; no `maxlength`; count is below the field and announces on pause.
source: components/textarea > Use appropriately-sized textareas; components/character-count > How it works, Avoid narrow limits. The 75% and 850-of-1000 figures are demo values, not recommendations [unverified].

text: Use a summary list (`dl`) for key-value facts and answers; row actions use "Change" links with visually hidden context ("Change name"), and each row keeps its separating border unless there are no actions; do not use it for tabular data.
why: Borders tie action to row for magnifier users; hidden text gives context.
check: `dl > div > dt + dd`; each action link has accessible name including the key; rows have `border-bottom` when actions exist.
source: components/summary-list > How it works, Adding actions, Removing the borders.

text: Show a check-answers page before final submission: page title says what to do, 'Change' links per answer that return to the check page after editing, unanswered optional questions show 'Not provided', the final button names the action ('Confirm and send' or 'Accept and send'), and it makes clear the transaction is not complete until confirmed.
why: Raises confidence and cuts errors.
check: summary list exists on penultimate step; change links preserve state.

text: Confirmation pages confirm completion (green panel with a title and a reference number), say what happens next, link to likely next services, offer a way to save a record, and still work when bookmarked; interactive elements inside the green panel must reach 3:1 contrast.
why: Reassurance and next steps.
check: page has `h1` in a panel, reference text, and a next-steps section; reload the URL: still useful.

text: Use accordions only with evidence that users benefit from hiding sections; test the content without one first; never hide content all users need, never nest an accordion, tabs or details inside another, and never use one to split a series of questions.
why: Many users miss collapsed content.
check: `[aria-expanded]` containers nested inside each other count 0; essential copy not collapsed by default.
source: components/accordion > When to use, When not to use.

text: Accordion section headings are buttons in sentence case with short descriptive labels; summary lines only when essential and very short; sections start closed (unless a section must be open), can be remembered open via session storage, and are never disabled.
why: Long names are hard to navigate by screen reader; disabled controls confuse.
check: `button[aria-expanded]` text length < 60 characters; no `[disabled]`.

text: Choose among the three reveal patterns by need: accordion for several sections viewed together or many sections; tabs for quick switching between a few, first tab most useful, labels short enough not to wrap, each tab starting with a heading that repeats its label; details for one or two short, low-importance pieces.
why: Right affordance for the content.
check: tabs list fits on one row at 1440; every panel starts with `h2/h3` matching the tab.

text: Tabs are not page navigation and not for content users must compare or read in order; the selected tab is stored in the URL fragment (`#tab_united-kingdom`) so Back moves to the previous tab; without JavaScript (and on small screens) tabs render as a headed list with a table of contents.
why: Hidden content breaks comparison; URL state allows deep links.
check: switching tabs updates `location.hash`; Back restores previous tab.
source: components/tabs > When not to use, How it works. Matches VWI-25.

text: Use a notification banner sparingly, before the page `h1`, same width as the content, with `role="region"` and `aria-labelledby`; at most one per page (combine messages); never for validation errors; blue for service-wide or elsewhere-in-service news, green for outcomes with `role="alert"` and a heading such as "Success" (not colour alone), and remove green banners on the next page.
why: Banners are often missed; overuse worsens that.
check: banner count <= 1; green banner has `role=alert` and a text heading.
source: components/notification-banner > How it works, Reacting to something the user has done.

text: Use inset text sparingly to set apart a quote or aside; use warning text (with a visually hidden "Warning" and an exclamation icon) for legal or important consequences.
why: Inset text is often overlooked.
check: inset blocks per page <= 2; warning text contains hidden "Warning" label.

text: Provide a cookie banner (accept or reject) when non-essential cookies are set; show it on every visit until a choice is saved; after a choice show a confirmation with a Hide button; store the preference for 1 year; place it right after the opening `<body>` and before the skip link; do not make it sticky (`position: fixed`) so it cannot obscure focused content (WCAG 2.4.11).
why: Consent and focus visibility.
check: banner is the first body child; computed `position` != fixed/sticky; cookie `Max-Age` ~ 31536000 s for the preference.

text: Banner copy names the service, stays short and accurate, and is the same whether or not JavaScript is enabled; with progressive enhancement, ship all possible messages hidden with the `hidden` attribute and focus the confirmation (`tabindex="-1"`, `role="alert"`) when the user chooses. Also publish a cookies page listing each cookie by category (essential, functional, analytics); do not bury it in terms.
why: Transparency and no re-consent loops.
check: banner heading contains the product name; cookies page exists and is linked in the footer.
source: components/cookie-banner > What to cover; patterns/cookies-page > Preparing, Writing.

text: Include a skip link immediately after the opening `<body>` (or after the cookie banner); it is visually hidden until keyboard focus and must not be wrapped in `nav` or moved into the header. Include a back link before `<main>`, use "Back" by default or "Go back to [page]" in complex journeys; never combine a back link with breadcrumbs.
why: Order of bypass; one wayfinding aid at a time.
check: first focusable is the skip link; `a.back-link` precedes `main`; breadcrumbs and back link not both present.
source: components/skip-link > When to use; components/back-link > How it works.

text: Footer: copyright and licence statement, links named "Privacy", "Accessibility", "Cookies" and "Terms and conditions"; place help links consistently across pages (WCAG 3.2.6); only add secondary navigation if you want users to leave the service. Use the GOV.UK header or footer only on GOV.UK domain services; others build their own.
why: Predictable legal and help links.
check: footer contains the four link texts; help link position equal across pages.
source: components/footer > Adding links; components/header > When not to use; Brand refresh note.

text: Header: keep the header simple and consistent at the top of every page; the service name and navigation live in the Service navigation component, not in the logo bar; avoid navigation links when the service is a linear journey (use a task list instead).
why: Wayfinding for non-linear services only.
check: nav links absent from linear funnels.
source: components/header > How it works; patterns/navigate-a-service > When not to use.

text: Table: use `caption` as the title, `th` with `scope`, right-align number columns, never for layout; reduce data or split tables; paginate only if it helps performance or use, never with infinite scroll, show page number in `<title>` ("Search results (page 1 of 4)") and hide previous on page 1 and next on last.
why: Comparison, accessibility, keyboard behaviour.
check: `td` numeric columns `text-align: right`; table has caption.
source: components/table > How it works; components/pagination > How it works.

text: Page not found: title "Page not found - [service] - GOV.UK" style, neutral non-blaming content (check typed address, check pasted address, contact option); problem-with-the-service (500): title and `h1` "Sorry, there is a problem with the service", say what happened to the user's answers, show contact options; use one page for all unexpected problems and show it only briefly, then switch to a service-unavailable page.
why: Recovery paths, no blame.
check: 404 and 500 templates exist with next-step links.

text: Interruption pages are rare: use only when there is evidence of need (irreversible action, conflicting answer, or critical information that would be missed), keep the panel short, with a single continue button and a back link; no other components in the panel.
why: They get less effective the more often they appear.
check: interruption count per flow <= 1.
source: patterns/interruption-pages > When to use, How it works.

text: Passwords: be consistent about restrictions everywhere, prefer a second factor over extra complexity, do not force periodic changes, do not reveal whether the username or password was wrong, do not keep a failed attempt's password in the input, allow 5 to 10 attempts before locking or extra checks, and never block paste.
why: Security without user hostility.
check: login error text identical for bad username and bad password; failed attempt clears the password field.

text: Body text is 19 px with a 25 px line height on both large and small screens; body-small is 16 px / 20 px (use sparingly; most copy stays at 19 px); lead paragraph 24 px (large screens), one per page. All type-scale line heights are multiples of 5 px; use relative units so type resizes on zoom.
why: Legibility and vertical rhythm.
check: computed body `font-size` >= 16 px (>= 19 px for long reading text on GOV.UK-style pages); `line-height` / `font-size` ~1.3 for 19/25.

text: Use headings by structure and style them by class: `h1` as heading-l (36/40 large screens, 27/30 small) on question pages, heading-xl (48/50 large, 32/35 small) for long-form pages; h2 heading-m (24/30 large, 21/25 small); h3 heading-s (19/25); write headings in sentence case; use a caption above a heading for the section name.
why: Consistent hierarchy.
check: computed sizes of `h1-h3` match the scale; heading text is sentence case.

text: Spacing uses a 5 px-based scale: 0, 5, 10, 15, then responsive steps (unit 4: 15 small / 20 large; 5: 15 / 25; 6: 20 / 30; 7: 25 / 40; 8: 30 / 50; 9: 40 / 60); units 0 to 3 are identical on all screens; breakpoint for the large scale is wider than 640 px.
why: Predictable rhythm.
check: margins and paddings on components are members of {0,5,10,15,20,25,30,40,50,60}.

text: Design small-screen first, single column; main content sits in a two-thirds column (or two-thirds plus one-third) so lines stay at most about 75 characters; default max page width 1020 px (the page says 1020 px; the frontend SCSS setting reads 960 px, see section 5); gutters 30 px.
why: Readable line length and consistent grid.
check: characters per line of body text <= 75 on desktop; main column width <= 2/3 of container.
source: styles/layout > Screen size, Using the grid system; govuk-frontend `settings/_measurements.scss` ($govuk-gutter 30px).

text: Links are blue and underlined by default; the linked text excludes trailing full stops; remove underlines only when context makes the link obvious (nav bars); external-site links name the organisation instead of using an icon; avoid new tabs, and if used put "opens in new tab" in the link text and add `rel="noreferrer noopener"`; on dark backgrounds use white links with >= 4.5:1.
why: Predictability, security (tabnabbing), a11y.
check: `a[target=_blank]` has `rel` noopener and link text includes "opens in new tab"; in-text links underlined.

text: Lists: bulleted lists have a lead-in line ending in a colon, items start lowercase and have no full stops; numbered lists are used when order matters, with full-stop endings; add extra spacing when items wrap over many lines.
why: Consistent scanning.
check: visual and copy lint.

text: Colour: use semantic functional colours (text #0b0c0c, secondary text #484949, link #1a65a6 with hover #0f385c, visited #54319f, active #0b0c0c, border #cecece, input border #0b0c0c, focus #ffdd00 with #0b0c0c text, error #ca3535, success #0f7a52, brand #1d70b8, surface #f4f8fb); text and interactive elements meet WCAG 2.2 AA contrast; reserve the focus yellow for focus only.
why: Predictable meaning across components.
check: compute ratios of each text/link pair above against its background (text, secondary text, link and visited colours should pass 4.5:1 on white; the border grey #cecece is decorative and does not); focus colour not used for decoration.
source: styles/colour > Functional colours. Hex values as shown on the page on 2026-10-08 (v6 brand refresh).

text: Focus style: a 3 px yellow (#ffdd00) outline with a dark (#0b0c0c) underline or ring so the focused element is unmistakable on any background; form inputs get an inset 2px dark border plus the yellow 3px outline; box components use a 4 px yellow ring with an 8 px dark outer ring.
why: High-contrast focus.
check: focused element has outline width >= 3px and an adjacent dark or yellow contrasting ring.
source: govuk-frontend `helpers/_focused.scss` and `settings/_measurements.scss` ($govuk-focus-width 3px) (code read, not a design-system prose page).

text: Form control dimensions: text input height 40 px with a 2 px border (dark), no rounded corners, 19 px text; button text 19 px with a 2 px bottom shadow, padding 8 px / 10 px; radios and checkboxes 40 px with a 44 px touch target; small variants 24 px.
why: Large, predictable controls.
check: `input` height ~40 px; radios 40 px; button height around 40 px including the shadow.
source: govuk-frontend `input/_mixin.scss` (height 40px, padding 5px, border 2px), `button/_mixin.scss` (padding 8px 10px, shadow 2px), `radios/_mixin.scss`. Derived from SCSS, not prose [unverified for final computed button height].

text: Include the page template basics: a `lang` on `html`, a skip link, the header, a `main` with the page content, a footer, JavaScript loaded at the end of body, and a `govuk-frontend-supported` class set by script so enhanced components only run where supported.
why: Progressive enhancement and a baseline of semantics.
check: `html[lang]`, skip link, `main`, `footer` present; scripts at end of body.

text: Treat WebGL/WebGPU post-processing as a deliberate, scarce hero or section effect: one canvas per page section, never behind long text, always with a static CSS/image fallback and a `prefers-reduced-motion` freeze.
why: the author's own scenes make laptops "sound like a jet engine" at high resolution; a canvas is main-thread plus GPU cost, and the ambition is justified only when the effect is the point of the page.
applies: landing page heroes, portfolio, brand pages.
check: count `<canvas>` elements with a WebGL context per viewport <= 1; a `<picture>`/CSS fallback exists; animation loop pauses on `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` and when the canvas is off-screen (IntersectionObserver).

text: Pick the control by what the toggle means. A checkbox suits on/off data that is submitted with a form and not mistaken for a choice; a `button` with `aria-pressed` (or `role=switch` with `aria-checked`) suits an immediate-effect toggle; radio pair inside `fieldset`/`legend` suits an explicit on/off choice. Do not use links for toggles.
why: Checkboxes and radios read as data inputs; buttons are the expected element for in-interface state changes.
check: `a[aria-pressed],a[role=switch],a[aria-checked]` count 0; `[aria-pressed]` and `[role=switch]` only on `button` elements.

text: A toggle button is `<button type="button">` with `aria-pressed` set to an explicit `"true"` or `"false"` at all times; the absence of the attribute means "not a toggle". `type="button"` stops accidental form submission.
why: ARIA state attributes are strings; a missing attribute loses the state announcement.
check: `button[aria-pressed]` value in {`true`,`false`}; `form button:not([type])` count 0 for toggle buttons; clicking flips the value.

text: Never change the label and the pressed state at the same time. Either keep a fixed label ("Notify by email") and flip `aria-pressed`, or flip the label (Play/Pause) with no pressed state.
why: A pressed "Pause" or an unpressed "Play" creates a double negative, and voice users speak what they see.
check: Playwright: click, record `textContent` and `aria-pressed` before/after; assert not both changed.

text: Show toggle state with more than colour (inset/outset shadow, icon, text "on/off", position), draw the pressed look from the attribute selector `[aria-pressed="true"]`, and give it a focus style that does not shift layout (outline or box-shadow).
why: WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color; coupling style to the attribute guarantees the visual and exposed states agree.
check: computed style difference between `aria-pressed=true/false` in at least one non-colour property (border, shadow, text, icon, transform); focus does not change element's `getBoundingClientRect()`.

text: For list-of-settings switches that display "on/off" text, give each switch a unique accessible name from the setting text (`aria-labelledby` pointing at the setting's span), put them in a list, and use `role="switch"` with `aria-checked`. Visible "on/off" spans do not form the name.
why: Identical "on / off" names are meaningless in isolation and unusable for voice control; lists give grouping and counts.
check: all `[role=switch]` accessible names unique and not "on"/"off"; `aria-checked` explicit.
source: https://inclusive-components.design/toggle-button/. [engine note] Switch role support was uneven in 2017; see `adrian-roselli.md` AR-14 for the later checkbox-versus-button decision.

text: Structure a card as a list item (`li` in a `ul`) containing a heading whose text is a link to the destination; make the whole card clickable by stretching the link with `a::after { content:""; position:absolute; inset:0 }` on a `position: relative` card. Do not wrap the whole card (heading, text, image) in one `<a>`.
why: One link with a concise unique name; the list gives count; wrapping everything creates a verbose accessible name and block-in-inline markup problems.
check: `.card :is(h1,h2,h3,h4) a` exists; `a:has(h2, h3, p)` count 0 inside cards; computed `::after` of card link is `position:absolute` with all four insets 0 and the card is `position:relative`.

text: Card link text must be unique and descriptive (use the card's title). Visible "Read more" calls to action should be decorative and linked to the real link with `aria-describedby` (the decorative element can be `aria-hidden="true"` and still serve as a description), not additional links.
why: Link lists and voice commands need distinct names; extra links add tab stops.
check: in each `ul` of cards, `a` text values are unique; no card contains two links to the same URL.

text: Keep tab stops per card to the minimum. A secondary link (author) may exist, raised above the stretched link with `position: relative` (no `z-index` needed if later in source) and given extra padding so its hit area is not tiny. Do not turn cards into miniature pages.
why: Keyboard users pay for every stop; mis-clicks on overlapped targets trigger the wrong action.
check: focusable elements per `.card` <= 2; secondary link target >= 24x24 (`L7`) and sits on top via hit-test at its centre.

text: Give the whole clickable card a visible focus state with `.card:focus-within` (box-shadow or outline) that matches its hover state, and remove the fallback link underline only inside the `:focus-within` block. Keep `:hover` out of the same selector list as `:focus-within` so an unsupported selector does not drop the hover style.
why: A keyboard user should see the same card-sized affordance a mouse user sees.
check: `A3`: focus the card link, assert `.card` computed outline/box-shadow changes.

text: If the card is clickable, show it: pointer cursor and a hover style. If clickability depends on JavaScript, add the cursor and hover with JavaScript so they never lie when script fails. When enhancing with a JS click proxy, ignore clicks that take longer than about 200 ms between mousedown and mouseup so text can still be selected; the pseudo-element stretch trade-off is that text becomes unselectable.
why: Perceived affordance must match function; selection vs click is an accessibility trade-off.
check: `getComputedStyle(card).cursor === 'pointer'` for clickable cards (`S2`); for JS proxy variants no card has the cursor with JS disabled.

text: Make cards tolerate content: flex-column cards with `flex-grow: 1` on the text, `margin-top: auto` on the last text element to pin attribution to the bottom, a consistent margin between children, equal heights via grid, `object-fit: cover` on the image box (accepting crops, curate images so the centre is the subject), text container capped near 60ch, minimum column about 15rem.
why: Interfaces that break with long or short content restrict what editors can write.
check: `S7`/`L12`: render with 1-word and 200-char titles, missing image: bottoms align, no overflow.

text: If the card image is informative and should visually precede the heading, put the text (starting with the heading) before the image in the DOM and use flex `order` to place the image on top. Decorative images keep `alt=""` and can stay first.
why: Headings start sections; an informative image before the heading belongs to nobody for heading navigation.
check: for cards with `img[alt]:not([alt=""])` the heading precedes the image in DOM order.

text: When generating `id`s for `aria-describedby`/`aria-labelledby` in loops, make them unique and stable (slug of the title), not random, so snapshots stay deterministic. Add extra vertical gap between single-column cards on narrow screens so scrolling does not trigger cards (the example uses 4.5rem).
why: Duplicated ids break references; random ids break snapshot tests; larger gaps reduce accidental taps.
check: axe `duplicate-id-aria`; `aria-describedby`/`aria-labelledby` ids all resolve.

text: Prefer visible text labels and clear body copy to tooltips. Use a tooltip only when space really is scarce (dense toolbars) and a toggletip only when the help cannot sit inline.
why: Tooltips hide information from touch and keyboard users and from anyone who never hovers.
check: count of `[role=tooltip]` per page (soft <= 3); icon-only buttons have an accessible name regardless of tooltip.

text: Do not rely on the `title` attribute for information. It is not shown for keyboard or touch users and is unevenly announced.
why: Reliable only on a few form elements in some screen readers.
check: `button[title]:not([aria-label]):not(:has(*))`, `a[title]` where title differs from text, `abbr[title]` flagged for review; `title` that repeats the link text removed.

text: A real tooltip follows hover and focus: place a `role="tooltip"` element next to the trigger, show it on `:hover` and `:focus`, hide on Esc, and connect it by role: `aria-labelledby` when it is the control's name, `aria-describedby` when it is extra detail (then provide a separate accessible name such as visually hidden text). `aria-labelledby` can list several ids to include a notification count.
why: Name vs description determines what is announced first and what is optional.
check: focus the trigger: tooltip visible; press Esc: hidden; pointer can move onto tooltip without it vanishing; trigger has `aria-labelledby` or `aria-describedby` pointing to an existing id.

text: A toggletip (click-triggered info bubble, usually an "i") is a `<button type="button">` plus an empty live region (`role="status"`) in the DOM beforehand. On click, clear the region, then after a short delay (about 100 ms) insert the bubble text; close on Esc, blur or outside click. Do not use `aria-describedby` for the bubble content.
why: If screen readers already have the description, activating the button seems to do nothing; the live region announces on demand. The delay makes repeated clicks re-announce.
check: `[data-toggletip]` (or equivalent) is a `button`; sibling `[role=status]` exists with empty text at load; click inserts text and `aria-describedby` is absent.

text: No interactive content (close buttons, links, confirm buttons) inside tooltips or toggletips. Use a dialog or popover with focus management for that.
why: Hover/focus-triggered content disappears before it can be reached.
check: `[role=tooltip] :is(a,button,input,select,textarea)` count 0 and the toggletip bubble likewise.

text: Treat tooltips as unreliable on touch (focus and press happen together so the tip shows only while pressed). Offer inline text for newcomers, a toggletip, or a first-tap-explains mode instead.
why: Touch has no hover.

text: Do not build tabs unless the use case benefits. A table of contents with same-page links, or an accordion, is simpler and more robust. Do not style a link list as tabs, and never use tab styling or tab semantics for site-wide navigation or router views.
why: Users who see tabs expect arrow-key behaviour and in-page switching; a link navigates and moves focus.
check: if `[role=tablist]` exists, a justification note in the spec; `nav [role=tab]` count 0.

text: A real tab interface: container `role="tablist"`; each tab `role="tab"` with `aria-selected`; each panel `role="tabpanel"` with `aria-labelledby` pointing at its tab; inactive panels hidden; selected tab has `tabindex` default (0) while others have `tabindex="-1"`; Left/Right arrows move and activate tabs; Tab moves into the active panel; Shift+Tab returns to the selected tab. Optionally Down arrow focuses the panel (give the panel `tabindex="-1"` and a focus style) so screen-reader users do not skip it. If the tab list is `ul`, wrap with `role="presentation"` on `li`.
why: Tabs are a composite widget; roving tabindex keeps one tab stop for the tablist.
check: keyboard script: Tab to tablist (one stop), ArrowRight selects next and shows its panel, Tab goes into the panel, Shift+Tab returns to selected tab; `[role=tab]` count equals `[role=tabpanel]` count; exactly one `aria-selected=true`.
source: https://inclusive-components.design/tabbed-interfaces/. [engine note] The article builds tabs from `<a>` links (progressive enhancement from a table of contents). For new JS-first work use `<button role="tab">`; the keyboard model is unchanged.

text: For single-page-app views use real links, then move focus to the new view's heading (`tabindex="-1"`) or labelled region and update `<title>` to `App | View`. Do not mark views as tabpanels.
why: Views are page-like; a link and focus move tell users the context changed.
check: after click, `document.activeElement` is the new heading/region and `document.title` changed (see `WDA-19`).

text: When tabs do not fit, collapse the tab list into a single column of options (selected one clearly marked) rather than converting to an accordion; if the number of tabs is unknown or large, use an accordion at all widths.
why: Tab-to-accordion hybrids are complex and use different ARIA and keys.
check: at 320 px the tablist has no horizontal overflow (`L1`) and still has one stop.

text: Put a real ``), not `role=button` on the heading, and not a click handler on the heading. Reset button styles with `all: inherit` and restore a focus style.
why: The button supplies focus, Enter/Space activation, and the heading remains in the outline (the screen reader announces both).
check: `:is(h1,h2,h3,h4,h5,h6)[role=button]` count 0; `[aria-expanded]` elements are `button` or `summary`; each is inside a heading when used for sections.

text: Set `aria-expanded` on the control (button), not on the controlled content, initially `"false"` when collapsed, and hide collapsed content with the `hidden` attribute (or equivalent `display:none`). `aria-haspopup` does not apply to disclosures.
why: State belongs to the control the user is on; hidden content is not focusable.
check: `[aria-expanded]:not(button,summary,[role=button],[role=tab],[role=combobox])` count 0; for each button, the controlled element is `hidden` iff `aria-expanded=false`.

text: Do not rely on `aria-controls` (supported mainly by JAWS). Place the revealed content immediately after the control in the DOM so screen reader and keyboard users meet it next; if you add `aria-controls` it is harmless but verbose.
why: Source order is the universal association.
check: controlled region is `nextElementSibling` (or immediate following sibling of the heading) of the control's container.

text: Use SVG plus/minus (or chevron) icons that are `aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"`, drawn with `currentColor` (so forced-colors/high contrast change them), and driven by `[aria-expanded]` selectors. The icon or label should reflect the action the button will perform.
why: State is already conveyed to AT; the icon is for sighted users and must survive high contrast.
check: `svg` inside disclosure buttons has `aria-hidden="true"`; `fill` / `stroke` computed to `currentColor`; `A18`.

text: Offer expand-all and collapse-all as two separate buttons inside a labelled list (`ul aria-label`), never one toggle, because sections can be in mixed states.
why: A single toggle cannot describe mixed state.
check: two buttons present when > 5 sections.

text: If a URL hash targets a collapsed section, open it and focus its button on load, and update the hash when the user opens a section so links are shareable.
why: Deep links must work when content is hidden.
check: load `/page#section-id` and assert the section is expanded and `document.activeElement` is its button.

text: Make the baseline readable without script: headings and prose are visible; script (or a web component with `open` attribute that mirrors `aria-expanded`) adds the button and hides content. Prefer not to ship interactive-looking buttons that do nothing when script fails.
why: Robustness; editors write plain prose.
check: with JS disabled content is visible and no dead buttons exist.
source: https://inclusive-components.design/collapsible-sections/. [engine note] Modern alternative: native `<details>`/`<summary>` (with `name` for exclusive groups) fulfils this; see `adrian-roselli.md` AR-12/AR-13.

text: Site navigation is `nav > ul > li > a`, with nested lists for sub-navigation. Do not apply `role=menu|menubar|menuitem` or `aria-haspopup` to it.
why: ARIA menus are for application commands and demand the desktop keyboard model; links in a menu lose their link role.
check: `nav [role=menu],nav [role=menubar],nav [role=menuitem],nav [aria-haspopup]` count 0 (`A15` item 8).

text: Avoid hover/focus-reveal dropdown submenus as the only route to sub-pages; on touch, the first tap both opens and follows the link. Provide a table-of-contents `nav` on each top-level page (list of links with a heading and `aria-labelledby`), consistent in position, as the robust alternative; if everything fits on one page, link to section ids (target `tabindex="-1"`).
why: Works for every input, and exposes structure instead of hiding it; helps users with cognitive load.
check: `S4` (no content reachable only via hover); each top-level page has a sub-nav list.

text: A small-screen navigation menu button lives inside the `nav` as a `button` with `aria-expanded` and the link list immediately after it (hidden when collapsed); without JavaScript the nav is simply visible. Add `[hidden]{display:none}` as safety for older browsers.
why: Screen reader users jumping to the nav landmark must find the button inside it; first link next in focus order replaces unreliable `aria-controls`.
check: `nav > button[aria-expanded]` and the `ul` is its next sibling; toggling flips `hidden`; button outside `nav` fails.

text: An application menu button (true menu): `button[aria-haspopup][aria-expanded]` opens `role="menu"` containing `menuitem` (or `menuitemradio`/`menuitemcheckbox` with `aria-checked`), items `tabindex="-1"`. Keys: Enter, Space or Down on the button opens and focuses first enabled item (or the checked item); Down/Up move with wrap; Up on the button closes; Esc closes and returns focus to the button; choosing an item closes, returns focus to the button and may announce the result in a live region.
why: This mimics native menus; arrow keys keep Tab free to leave.
applies: command menus in apps (not site nav).
check: `A15` keyboard script for menus; `menuitem` count > 0 inside `[role=menu]` only; focus after Esc equals the trigger.

text: Do not turn a `<select>` into navigation (change event that navigates).
why: Unexpected change of context on input fails WCAG 3.2.2.
check: `select` change listeners that set `location` flagged.

text: Do not sacrifice expected focus behaviour to avoid JavaScript (the checkbox hack cannot manage focus, keyboard model or announce expansion state properly). A JS-free nav menu is acceptable only because the content is plain links.
why: Vanity JS-free builds that break usability are net negative.
check: `input[type=checkbox]` used as menu toggles flagged in review.

text: Split messages into two kinds: requests for action (dialog or inline disclosure, with focus moved to the controls) and FYI messages (polite live region, focus not moved). Never move focus to a status message.
why: Focus means "something to operate here"; stealing it interrupts the user's task.
check: Playwright: trigger a toast, assert `document.activeElement` unchanged and a `role=status`/`aria-live=polite` region received text.

text: Live regions must exist before you add content; use `role="status"` (with `aria-live="polite"`) for most messages, `alert` only for urgent ones; avoid `aria-atomic="true"` unless the whole region should be re-read; for streams use `aria-relevant="additions"`; silence regions in hidden tabs (set `aria-live="off"` / `role="none"` when `document.hidden`).
why: Announcement behaviour depends on the region being primed; hidden tabs otherwise chatter.
check: `[role=status]` present in initial HTML; on `visibilitychange` regions toggle.

text: Give users control over notification verbosity in a settings screen (per type, using standard checkboxes/radios, headings allowed inside `legend`), and do not announce everything that changes. Only announce what the user is engaged with.
why: Aural noise cannot be averted like visual noise.
check: settings page lists each notification type with a control.

text: Differentiate message types with content (a text prefix such as "Error:" or "Info:") and optionally icons; never by style, colour, shape or position alone. Icons need alternative text (visually hidden text, since `aria-label` and SVG `<title>` do not auto-translate) and `currentColor` fills for high contrast.
why: WCAG 1.4.1; translation tools ignore aria-label.
check: each message container contains text identifying its type; svg icons `aria-hidden` plus adjacent `.visually-hidden` text.

text: Prefer self-dismissing (about 5-10 s) over per-message close buttons for FYI notifications, but only when the information remains discoverable elsewhere (list of online users, awards on the profile). (opinion)
why: A dismiss button adds an element to find, operate and manage focus for.
check: each toast references a persistent location or the message log.
source: https://inclusive-components.design/notifications/. [engine note] Conflicts with WCAG 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable and Roselli's advice; see section 5 and `adrian-roselli.md` AR-07/AR-08.

text: Only tabular data goes in `table`. Header cells are `th` (`scope="col"` or `scope="row"` for row headers), every table has a `caption` (headings may sit inside it) or an immediately preceding heading, and avoid the deprecated `summary`. Within a `figure` a `figcaption` serves.
why: Screen readers read column/row headers while moving across cells; the caption is announced on table navigation.
check: each data table: `th` count >= 1, `caption` or `figcaption` or `aria-label[ledby]`; `td`-only header rows fail; `table[summary]` count 0.

text: Remove table semantics from layout tables with `role="presentation"` (or `none`) and prefer CSS layout in new work. Visual tables need clear cell divisions, highlighted headers, left-aligned text; zebra striping is optional.
why: A layout table read as data is confusing.
check: `table` without `th` and without `role=presentation|none` flagged.

text: Make wide tables responsive by letting the wrapper scroll horizontally (`overflow-x:auto`), never by changing `display` on table parts. If the wrapper actually overflows, give it `tabindex="0"` and a name (the article uses `role="group"` and `aria-labelledby` the caption id); only add the tab stop when `scrollWidth > clientWidth`; add a visible "(scroll to see more)" hint in the caption when scrollable.
why: Keyboard users cannot scroll an unfocusable region; a tab stop on a non-scrolling region does nothing.
check: for each `.table-container`: if `scrollWidth > clientWidth` then `tabindex="0"` and an accessible name; else no `tabindex`; computed `display` of `table`, `tr`, `td` unchanged at 320 px.
source: https://inclusive-components.design/data-tables/. [engine note] Role/name requirement was revised in 2026; see section 5 and `adrian-roselli.md` AR-17.

text: For very narrow viewports it is acceptable to render an equivalent alternative structure (caption as `h2`, row header as `h3`, columns as `dl`) in a separate DOM block shown with CSS at small widths; both blocks derive from the same data.
why: One-column reading beats scrolling a table at 320 px; separate DOM keeps table semantics intact.
check: at 320 px exactly one of table or list structure is visible (`display:none` hides from AT too).

text: Sortable column headers contain a `button` ("sort by Year"), and the sorted column's `th` carries `aria-sort="ascending|descending"` (works best with explicit `role="columnheader"`); show direction with SVG arrows (`currentColor`), and expose three icon states: sortable, ascending, descending. Do not provide sorting where the data set is tiny.
why: `aria-sort` reports state; the button label teaches the control.
check: `th button` exists in sortable column; exactly one `th[aria-sort]` after sort; click toggles asc/desc.
source: https://inclusive-components.design/data-tables/. [engine note] Roselli's later guidance removes `aria-sort` from unsorted headers and adds a live announcement (AR-19).

text: Use ARIA `grid` only when cells must be reached by arrow keys by non-screen-reader users (a date picker), not for ordinary data tables.
why: Grid is an interactive composite widget; tables are static with interactive children allowed.
check: `[role=grid]` count > 0 requires arrow-key script in the component spec.

text: A slider should never move without a user action: no auto-advance, no timers. Movement is by scrolling, swipe, arrow keys or buttons only.
why: A pause button returns control only after the harm of unexpected motion; WCAG 2.2.2 merely requires the pause mechanism.
check: open page, wait 15 s, assert `scrollLeft` unchanged and no `setInterval`-driven transform (Playwright `page.clock`).
source: https://inclusive-components.design/a-content-slider/. [engine note] Stricter than the existing `A11`/`A12` rules.

text: Build the base with native horizontal scroll (`overflow-x: scroll` on a list of slides); make it keyboard-operable with `tabindex="0"`, give it `role="region"` plus `aria-label` (so the name is supported), a visible focus style, and instructions revealed for hover, focus and touch (referenced via `aria-describedby` for the focus message). Detect touch by the first `touchstart` event, not by device capability.
why: A scrollable region is focusable only if you make it so; multi-input devices exist.
check: scroller has `tabindex=0`, a role and name, `:focus` outline; ArrowRight scrolls it.
source: https://inclusive-components.design/a-content-slider/. [engine note] 2026 guidance says role/name may be optional; AR-17.

text: Use a list for slides and `figure`/`figcaption` for media; lazy-load later slides (IntersectionObserver with an empty placeholder `src`, `<noscript>` fallback) because the first slide gets almost all the attention (the cited study: 1% clicked a feature, of which 89% were the first position); keep the scroller height predictable so loading does not shift layout.
why: Performance and honest ranking of content.
check: `I4`, `P2`; first slide `img` eager, others lazy.

text: Previous/next buttons are optional enhancements that build on scrolling: real buttons in a `ul[aria-label]` group, each with its own accessible name, large touch targets, `scroll-snap` where supported; only render them if the enhancement works.
why: They aid affordance and snapping, but must not replace native scroll.
check: `button` names "previous"/"next" present; target >= 44 px on coarse pointer (`L7b`); scroll position after click aligns to a slide.

text: When slides are links, take off-screen slide links out of tab order with `tabindex="-1"` (not `aria-hidden`), restoring them when visible, so keyboard users reach the controls quickly and never focus invisible items.
why: Invisible focusable content is a failure; `aria-hidden` on focusable content breaks the fourth ARIA rule.
check: off-screen links `tabindex=-1`; `[aria-hidden] a` count 0.

text: An in-page theme toggle is a button with `aria-pressed` and a visible "on/off" text that is `aria-hidden` (so it does not contradict the state), persisted in `localStorage`, placed in a landmark that is not `main` (header or footer) in the same place on every page. Only render it if the technique is supported.
why: Users should find it again; unsupported features should not be offered.
applies: sites with a manual theme switch.
check: `button[aria-pressed]` inside `header,footer,nav`; same DOM position across routes; value persists after reload.
source: https://inclusive-components.design/a-theme-switcher/. [engine note] Pair with system preference: `prefers-color-scheme` first, manual override stored second (existing 2.8 rule).

text: The article's `filter: invert(100%)` dark theme (root inverted, images/videos re-inverted, `background-color: inherit` fallback) is an economical hack but not a design-quality dark mode; treat it as legacy. Prefer token-based themes (`color-scheme`, custom properties, `light-dark()`).
why: Inversion shifts hues and shadows; tokens give contrast control.
check: `S6`; `filter: invert` on `html` flagged.

text: Support Windows high contrast / forced colours: no background images for content, inline SVG icons with `currentColor`, test with the forced-colors media query.
why: Backgrounds are stripped; content images must be `` with `alt`.
check: `A18`; informative images are `img` not `background-image`.

text: Only ship nice-to-have features when the performance and complexity cost is small, and feature-detect before showing the control.
why: If it cannot be done efficiently, a net negative.
check: control hidden when `CSS.supports` fails.

text: Give each major component a heading whose level reflects belonging (depth in the outline), put it in a `section` labelled by that heading (`aria-labelledby`), use a `ul` for items, and design an empty state (text plus pointer to the input) that appears with CSS (`ul:empty + .empty-state`).
why: Headings and lists provide navigation and counts; empty states teach new users.
check: heading before list inside the section; empty fixture renders the empty state; axe `region`.

text: Every input has a real label. A visually hidden label (or `aria-label`) is acceptable only when something else visible names the input (an adjacent "Add" button); placeholders do not count and must have higher contrast than browser default and a distinguishing style. Keep inputs in a `<form>` so Enter submits.
why: Placeholders vanish and are unreliable; a form element gives submit-on-Enter.
check: `A10`; `::placeholder` contrast >= 4.5:1 (`A2`).

text: Confirm user actions that update the page with a visually hidden polite live region message when the visible change is already clear (for example "{name} added."), instead of moving focus or duplicating a visible banner.
why: Equivalent experience for screen reader users without noise for others.
check: `[role=status]` text updates after the action and visible UI also changed.

text: Icon-only delete/remove buttons get an accessible name that includes the item (`aria-label="delete Learn Haskell"`); the icon is SVG via `<use>` and `aria-hidden`.
why: Identical "delete" names are not distinguishable.
check: repeated action buttons in a list have unique accessible names.
source: https://inclusive-components.design/a-todo-list/. [engine note] Roselli prefers visible/hidden text or `aria-labelledby` over `aria-label` for translation (AR-27).

text: After deleting the focused item, move focus deliberately: to the first remaining item's control, or if the list is empty to the component heading (`tabindex="-1"`), and announce the outcome in a polite status region so it follows the focus announcement (an assertive alert would override it).
why: Browsers drop focus to the document, forcing keyboard users to re-tab from the top.
check: Playwright: delete item, assert `document.activeElement !== document.body`.
source: https://inclusive-components.design/a-todo-list/. [engine note] Roselli advises the previous analogous control instead of the first (AR-24).

text: Provide a confirmation dialog when deletion is critical; casual deletions may be recoverable by trial and error.
why: Cost of error decides friction.
check: destructive buttons trigger `dialog` or provide undo; `visual`.

text: Make the gap between related items clearly smaller than the gap between unrelated groups: label-to-field and heading-to-body gaps at most about two thirds of the gap between neighbouring groups. [engine note] the ratio is ours.
why: Nearness is read as belonging, before any border or colour is noticed.
check: for each label/field pair and heading/paragraph pair, measure the distance to its own content and to the next group; inner gap divided by outer gap is 0.67 or lower.

text: To bind a group of elements, put them inside one shared boundary (border or background) and make sure nothing unrelated shares that boundary. Use a container only when spacing alone is not enough, and use it sparingly.
why: Elements sharing an enclosed area are seen as one unit; it overrides weaker cues like colour or spacing.
check: group members share an ancestor element with a visible border, background or shadow that non-members do not share; count of nested containers per section at most 2 `[engine note]`.

text: Elements that behave alike must look alike (colour, shape, size, orientation); elements that behave differently must differ. In particular, links and nav items must be visually distinguishable from body text.
why: Visual sameness is read as shared function.
check: all `a` in body copy have an underline or at least 3:1 contrast against the surrounding text colour; all primary buttons share one computed background and radius; non-interactive text does not reuse the link style.

text: Connect things that belong together with a visible line, frame or arrow (timelines, steppers, flow diagrams, grouped controls), and use a connector to carry the eye from one element to the next.
why: A physical link is a stronger grouping cue than nearness or similarity.
check: `visual`; for steppers, each step node is joined by a line/segment element.

text: Prefer the simplest shape or figure that conveys the meaning; reduce illustrations, icons and layouts to one clear overall form rather than many competing parts.
why: The eye resolves complex or ambiguous images into the simplest interpretation, so complexity is wasted or misread.
check: `visual`; squint/blur the render (about 8 px radius) and confirm the layout resolves into two or three obvious shapes.

text: Limit the number of simultaneously visible choices in any decision, split complex tasks into steps, and highlight a recommended option; do not take simplification so far that meaning disappears.
why: Decision time rises with the number and complexity of alternatives.
check: count of sibling choices (nav links, CTAs, plan cards, radio options) per decision group; flag more than 7 nav links, more than one primary CTA per viewport, or more than 4 pricing tiers without a highlighted default `[engine note]`.

text: Where users must compare options (plans, products), provide side-by-side comparison, a featured default, and filtering or search up front instead of one long undifferentiated list.
why: Too many options reduce decision quality and satisfaction with the outcome.
check: pricing section has a comparison layout, exactly one highlighted tier, and 4 or fewer cards visible without scrolling `[engine note]`; catalogues have a filter or search input.

text: Break content into visually distinct groups with a clear hierarchy (modules, rules between groups, headings) so users can scan to the part that matches their goal.
why: Grouped information fits working memory and is faster to scan than a flat stream.
check: no run of more than 5 consecutive paragraphs without a heading, list or visual break; no ungrouped list longer than 7 items `[engine note]`.

text: Organise content into smaller chunks; do not treat 7 plus or minus 2 as a hard cap or as the reason to cut useful features.
why: Short-term capacity is limited and varies with expertise and context.
check: `visual`; lists above about 7 items are grouped or subheaded rather than truncated.

text: Put the memory burden on the system: show what the user has already seen or entered (breadcrumbs, visited-link colour, order summary, sticky table headers, carry values forward) instead of asking them to recall it.
why: People hold about 4-7 chunks for 20-30 seconds and are far better at recognising than recalling.
applies: SaaS app UI | forms | landing page.
check: pages deeper than two levels have breadcrumbs or a visible current-location marker; multi-step flows repeat chosen options in a summary; long tables keep header row visible (`position: sticky` on `thead th`).

text: Remove elements that consume attention without helping the task (decorative clutter, duplicate controls, competing emphasis) and reduce the information that has to be carried between steps.
why: Intrinsic load (the task itself) is fixed; extraneous load (the interface) is the part a designer controls, and total load beyond capacity causes missed details and overwhelm.
check: count of visually emphasised elements (filled buttons, badges, coloured banners) per viewport at most 3 `[engine note]`; one primary action per screen.

text: When two designs solve the task equally, ship the one with fewer elements, fields and assumptions; remove elements until further removal would break the function.
why: Complexity avoided is cheaper than complexity managed.
check: `visual` removal test: delete each element in turn and confirm whether the task still works; flag elements whose removal changes nothing.

text: Absorb the irreducible complexity in the system (smart defaults, autofill, inferred values, sensible presets), not in the user's head; do not design for an idealised rational user.
why: Every process has a core of complexity that someone must handle; making users handle it multiplies the cost by the number of users.
check: form fields have defaults or `autocomplete` values where inferable; optional settings are hidden behind a default.

text: Shorten the real duration of a task to match what users expect it to take; use autofill and saved data for critical fields so forms are not padded out.
why: Tasks fill the time they are given; a longer path is perceived as the task, not the design.
check: inputs for name, email, address, phone, card carry the correct `autocomplete` token; step count at or below the number the user would predict `[engine note]`.

text: Accept a wide range of input formats and normalise them yourself (spaces, dashes, case, country codes, trailing whitespace); define clear boundaries and give clear feedback when input truly cannot be used.
why: Users do not know your internal format; rejecting reasonable variants creates avoidable errors.
check: phone, card, postcode, date and email fields accept formatted input without `pattern` rejecting spaces or dashes; trim whitespace before validating; type with `inputmode` where relevant.

text: Use the layout and interaction conventions people already know (logo links home, search icon, cart top right, checkout sequence, standard form controls); change a familiar pattern only with a reason, and offer a transition path when you must change.
why: People transfer expectations from the many other sites they use.
check: header logo is an `a` pointing to `/`; primary nav is at the top; standard controls (`input`, `select`, `button`, checkbox, radio) are real elements, not custom look-alikes; `visual` for the rest.

text: Match the interface to users' mental models: use the words, grouping and order they use, and validate with interviews, journey and empathy maps rather than internal assumptions.
why: Users apply a compressed model of how a system works; the closer the interface is to it, the less must be learned.
check: `visual` plus research; labels use terms found in user language (card sorting or support transcripts), not internal product names.

text: Do not rely on manuals or mandatory tutorials; provide help in context (tooltips, inline hints, empty-state guidance) so people who start acting immediately can learn on the way.
why: Users are driven by their immediate task and skip documentation up front.
check: first-run screens allow the primary action without dismissing a tour; help is attached to the control (`aria-describedby`, hint text).

text: Make the single most important item or action visually distinct from its peers, and use restraint so emphasised items do not compete or resemble ads; never rely on colour alone, and consider motion sensitivity when using motion to stand out.
why: In a set of similar items, the odd one is noticed and remembered; many odd ones cancel the effect.
check: at most one primary-emphasis element per group (one filled primary button, one highlighted pricing card); emphasis differs by more than colour (weight, size, shape, border); animated emphasis disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

text: Guide attention deliberately: do not style content like advertising or place it in ad-typical zones (banners, right rail), and avoid several changes happening at once that compete for a user's eye.
why: People filter out whatever does not match their goal, and miss changes when cues are weak or simultaneous.
check: no key content in a right-hand rail styled as a card with ad-like proportions; when state changes (toasts, counters, validation) occur, no more than one unrelated change animates in the same 300 ms window `[engine note]`.

text: Place the most important items at the start and end of lists and navigation; put the least important in the middle.
why: People remember the first and last items in a series best.
check: primary CTA or key destinations are first or last in the nav; the least-used destinations occupy middle positions; `visual`.

text: Make targets large enough to hit, spaced apart, and placed where they are easy to reach; keep the primary action near the user's attention and thumb zone.
why: Acquisition time rises with distance and falls with target size; small tight targets cause errors.
check: interactive elements are at least 44 by 44 CSS px with at least 8 px between neighbours `[engine note]` (the site gives no numbers); primary mobile CTA sits in the lower half of the viewport.

text: Give feedback to every action within 400 ms; for longer work, show progress or a skeleton immediately and use perceived-performance tricks. Do not add artificial delay to fake effort.
why: Below roughly 400 ms the user and the system do not wait on each other, which keeps attention and productivity high.
check: time from input event to first visual change at most 400 ms (measure with Event Timing / `PerformanceObserver`); async actions show a pending state (`aria-busy`, spinner, skeleton) within 100 ms.

text: Balance challenge and skill: show feedback for every action, remove needless friction, and make features discoverable so the user is neither bored nor blocked.
