text: Make every flow fully keyboard operable and follow the WAI-ARIA APG pattern for each widget (tabs, menu, dialog, combobox and so on).
why: Keyboard, switch, and screen-reader users depend on the standard key contracts.
check: Tab and arrow through each widget; every control reachable and operable without a pointer; compare keys to the APG pattern page.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Interactions > Keyboard; README "Keyboard works everywhere".

text: Every focusable element shows a visible, unobscured focus indicator; use `:focus-visible` (not bare `:focus`) and add `:focus-within` for grouped controls; sticky headers, footers, banners and overlays must never cover the focused element.
why: Visible focus is the keyboard user's cursor; `:focus-visible` avoids distracting pointer users.
check: Tab through the page at 375 and 1440 px; for each stop, computed outline or box-shadow is non-empty, and `document.elementsFromPoint(centre)[0]` is the element or a descendant.

text: Manage focus for overlays and dynamic UI: trap focus inside modals, move focus in when something opens, return it to the trigger on close, as the APG pattern prescribes.
why: Without it focus is lost behind the overlay.
check: open a dialog, press Tab 20 times, focus stays inside; close, `document.activeElement` is the trigger.

text: Never write `outline: none` (or `outline: 0`) unless a visible replacement focus style is present on the same selector.
why: It silently removes the only focus cue.
check: scan stylesheets for `outline: none|0|transparent-only` without a `:focus-visible` rule giving `box-shadow`, `outline`, or `border` change.

text: Hit target at least 24 px in both axes; on mobile (coarse pointer) at least 44 px. If the visual element is smaller than 24 px, expand the hit area with padding or a pseudo-element rather than enlarging the visual.
why: Small targets cause mis-taps and fail motor-impaired users; hit area and visual size are independent.
check: `getBoundingClientRect()` (plus pseudo-element hit area) of buttons, links, inputs, icon buttons: width and height >= 24; under `pointer: coarse` emulation >= 44.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Targets & Input; README "Match visual & hit targets".

text: On mobile, `<input>`, `<select>` and `<textarea>` font-size must be at least 16 px (alternative the README gives: a viewport meta with `maximum-scale=1`, which conflicts with VWI-07, so prefer the 16 px fix).
why: iOS Safari auto-zooms and pans the page on focus when the font is smaller.
check: computed `font-size` of every form control at 375 px viewport >= 16px.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Targets & Input; README "Mobile input size".

text: Never disable browser zoom: no `user-scalable=no`, no `maximum-scale=1` in the viewport meta.
why: Low-vision users rely on pinch-zoom (WCAG 1.4.4).
check: `meta[name=viewport]` content does not match `/user-scalable\s*=\s*(no|0)|maximum-scale\s*=\s*1(\.0)?\b/`.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Targets & Input; README "Respect zoom".

text: Set `touch-action: manipulation` on controls to prevent double-tap zoom delay.
why: Removes the legacy tap-delay ambiguity on touch screens.
check: computed `touch-action` on `button, a, [role=button], input` equals `manipulation` (or `auto` with zoom still enabled and no 300 ms delay measured).

text: Set `-webkit-tap-highlight-color` deliberately so the tap flash matches the design (soft).
why: The default grey flash on iOS/Android clashes with custom surfaces.
check: computed `-webkit-tap-highlight-color` on interactive elements is not the UA default on custom-styled controls.

text: Inputs must be hydration-safe: they never lose focus or typed value when the framework hydrates; an input with `value` must have `onChange` (or use `defaultValue`).
why: Typing before hydration is common on slow devices; losing it is data loss.
check: type into an input immediately after load on a throttled CPU; value and focus remain after hydration; no React "value without onChange" warning in console.

text: Never block paste in `<input>` or `<textarea>` (no `onpaste` preventDefault).
why: Blocks password managers, 2FA codes and accessibility tools.
check: grep for `onpaste` handlers calling `preventDefault`; programmatic paste event is not cancelled.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Forms; README "Don't block paste".

text: A loading button shows a spinner and keeps its original label (no label swap to "Loading").
why: Layout and meaning stay stable.
check: while loading, button text node still equals the idle label and width is unchanged.

text: Enter submits when a text input has focus (if many controls, treat the last control as the submitter); in `<textarea>` Enter inserts a newline and Cmd/Ctrl+Enter submits.
why: Matches platform expectations.
check: focus the input, press Enter, submit event fires; in textarea Enter does not submit, Ctrl+Enter does.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Forms; README "Enter submits", "Textarea behavior".

text: Keep the submit button enabled until the request starts; then disable it, show a spinner, and send an idempotency key.
why: Prevents double submits without hiding validation feedback.
check: submit button has no `disabled` before first submit on an empty form; `disabled` becomes true only after the request begins.

text: Do not pre-disable submit on an incomplete form; let the user submit so validation surfaces.
why: A dead button gives no hint what is missing.
check: on a pristine form, `button[type=submit]:disabled` count is 0.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Forms; README "Don't pre-disable submit".

text: Accept free text and validate afterwards; never block keystrokes (for example, do not drop non-digits in a numeric field without explanation).
why: A swallowed keystroke gives no feedback.
check: type a letter into a numeric field: the character appears and a message explains, or input is accepted and trimmed visibly.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Forms; README "Don't block typing".

text: Show errors inline next to their field; on submit, move focus to the first field in error.
why: Proximity ties the message to the control; focus move tells keyboard and screen-reader users where to go.
check: submit invalid form: `document.activeElement` is the first `[aria-invalid=true]`; each error element is a sibling or `aria-describedby` target within 1 field-gap of its input.

text: Give every field a meaningful `name`, an `autocomplete` token, the right `type`, and the right `inputmode`.
why: Enables autofill and the correct on-screen keyboard.
check: every `input` has non-empty `name`, `autocomplete` (not `off` for identity/address/payment) and `type` consistent with the label (email, tel, url, number, search).
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Forms; README "Autocomplete & names", "Correct types & input modes".

text: Disable spellcheck on emails, codes, usernames and similar fields (`spellcheck="false"`).
why: Red squiggles on non-prose values are noise.
check: `input[type=email], input[name*=user], input[name*=code]` have `spellcheck=false`.

text: Placeholders end with an ellipsis character and show an example value or pattern (for example `+1 (123) 456-7890`, `sk-012345679…`).
why: Signals that the field is empty and shows format.
check: `placeholder` of text inputs ends with `…` (U+2026) and is not a label substitute.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Forms; README "Placeholders signal emptiness", "Placeholder value".

text: Warn before navigation when unsaved changes would be lost.
why: Prevents silent data loss.
check: edit a field then trigger route change or reload; a `beforeunload` or in-app confirm appears.

text: Be compatible with password managers and 2FA: allow pasting one-time codes, use `autocomplete="one-time-code"` on OTP fields, and avoid auth-like names (such as `password`) on non-auth fields like Search (use `autocomplete="off"` there).
why: Wrong tokens cause managers to pop up on the wrong fields or fail on the right ones.
check: OTP input has `autocomplete=one-time-code` and accepts paste; search input has no `name` containing `pass` or `user`.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Forms; README "Password managers & 2FA", "Don't trigger password managers for non-auth fields".

text: Trim input values before validating, to survive trailing whitespace from text-replacement and expansion input methods.
why: An invisible trailing space produces a baffling error.
check: submit `"a@b.co "` (trailing space): accepted.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Forms; README "Text replacements & expansions".

text: Checkboxes and radios have no dead zones: the label and the control form one continuous hit target, and clicking a `<label>` focuses or toggles its control; every control has a `<label>` or equivalent association.
why: Gaps between the box and the text make people miss.
check: `label[for]` or wrapping label exists for each control; hit area of label+control has no gap (`elementFromPoint` at the midpoint between box and text returns label or input).
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Forms; README "No dead zones on controls", "Labels everywhere", "Label activation".

text: Persist UI state in the URL (filters, tabs, pagination, expanded panels, anywhere `useState` stands for shareable state), so share, refresh, Back and Forward all work.
why: Deep links and restore.
check: change a filter or tab, reload: same state; copy URL into a new tab: same state.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > State & Navigation; README "URL as state", "Deep-link everything".

text: Back and Forward restore the previous scroll position.
why: Prevents losing place in long lists.
check: scroll 2000 px, navigate away, go Back: `scrollY` within 50 px of before.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > State & Navigation; README "Scroll positions persist".

text: Navigation uses `<a href>` or the framework `<Link>`, never `<div onClick>` or `<button>` for navigational links, so Cmd/Ctrl-click, middle-click and context menu work.
why: Preserves browser behaviours and semantics.
check: elements with navigational click handlers and no `href`: count 0; `a:not([href])` count 0.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > State & Navigation; README "Links are links".

text: Use optimistic UI when success is likely: update immediately, reconcile with the server response, and on failure show an error and roll back or offer Undo.
why: Perceived speed.
check: with the network blocked, the action reverts with an error and/or an Undo control.

text: Destructive actions require a confirmation step or provide an Undo window.
why: Irreversible actions need a safety net.
check: trigger each delete or remove control: a confirm dialog or an Undo toast appears before data is gone.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Feedback; README "Confirm destructive actions".

text: Announce async updates (toasts, inline validation) through a polite `aria-live` region.
why: Screen-reader users otherwise miss them.
check: toast container or validation message has `aria-live="polite"` or `role=status` (not `assertive` for routine info).
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Feedback; README "Announce async updates".

text: Menu options that open a follow-up step and loading states end with an ellipsis character ("Rename…", "Loading…", "Saving…", "Generating…").
why: The ellipsis signals more input or work in progress.
check: menu items that open dialogs end with `…` (U+2026); busy labels end with `…`.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Feedback; README "Ellipsis for further input & loading states".

text: Spinners and skeletons use a show-delay of roughly 150-300 ms and a minimum visible time of roughly 300-500 ms, so fast responses do not flicker (React `Suspense` does this automatically).
why: A 80 ms flash of a spinner reads as a glitch.
check: throttle a mocked request to 100 ms: no spinner appears; to 400 ms: spinner shows for at least 300 ms.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines README > Interactions "Minimum loading-state duration" (not in AGENTS.md).

text: Delay the first tooltip in a group; show subsequent peer tooltips instantly.
why: Avoids tooltip spam while scanning, but keeps scanning fast.
check: hover first icon: tooltip appears after a delay (typically 300-700 ms); move to neighbour within 300 ms: appears with 0 delay.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Touch & Drag; README "Tooltip timing". Exact delays not given [unverified].

text: Use `overscroll-behavior: contain` inside modals and drawers.
why: Stops scroll chaining to the page behind.
check: computed `overscroll-behavior` of dialog or drawer scroll containers is `contain` or `none`.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Touch & Drag; README "Overscroll behavior".

text: To suppress desktop rubber-band bounce, set `overscroll-behavior: none` on `<html>` only inside `@media (pointer: fine)`; keep coarse-pointer defaults so mobile pull-to-refresh survives; test hybrid touch devices because `pointer` reports the primary input and `none` also disables scroll chaining and native swipe navigation.
why: Avoids breaking mobile gestures.
check: `html` computed `overscroll-behavior` is `none` only when `matchMedia('(pointer: fine)')`.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Touch & Drag; README "Desktop rubber-banding".

text: While dragging, disable text selection and set `inert` on the dragged element so hover and selection do not occur at the same time.
why: Prevents accidental selection and hover flicker.
check: start a drag: `user-select: none` is applied to the body or list and the dragged node has `inert`.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Touch & Drag; README "Clean drag interactions".

text: Every drag, swipe, pinch or path gesture also has a tap/click and keyboard alternative, unless the gesture is essential.
why: WCAG 2.5.7 Dragging Movements.
check: each gesture-only control has a button or key equivalent reachable by Tab.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Touch & Drag; README "Gestures have alternatives".

text: If something looks clickable it must be clickable: no part of an apparently interactive surface is a dead zone, and controls have clear affordances and generous targets.
why: Guessing where to click is a failure.
check: hover cursor is pointer on the entire visual card or row that appears interactive; `elementFromPoint` over its padding returns the interactive element.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Touch & Drag; README "No dead zones", "Design forgiving interactions".

text: Autofocus on desktop screens that have a single primary input; rarely on mobile (the keyboard opening causes layout shift).
why: Speed on desktop, stability on mobile.
check: `[autofocus]` present on single-input desktop screens; absent at 375 px.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Autofocus; README "Autofocus for speed". Conflict with a11y checklist: see section 5.

text: Internationalise keyboard shortcuts for non-QWERTY layouts and show platform-specific modifier symbols.
why: Shortcuts bound to physical key letters break on other layouts.
check: shortcuts use `event.key` or layout-aware mapping; on macOS UI shows the Cmd symbol, on Windows Ctrl.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines README > Interactions "Locale-aware keyboard shortcuts" (not in AGENTS.md).

text: Honour `prefers-reduced-motion`: ship a reduced variant or disable the animation.
why: Vestibular safety (WCAG 2.3.3).
check: emulate `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`; transforms, parallax and auto-play motion are removed or replaced by fades; grep CSS for an `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block.

text: Implementation preference order: CSS, then Web Animations API, then JS libraries; avoid main-thread JS-driven animation when CSS can do it.
why: Compositor-run CSS stays smooth under main-thread load.
check: review: animation libraries are only used where CSS cannot (gesture-driven, physics).

text: Animate only compositor-friendly properties (`transform`, `opacity`); never animate layout properties (`top`, `left`, `width`, `height`).
why: Layout properties trigger reflow and repaint every frame.
check: inspect `transition-property` and `@keyframes` for `top|left|right|bottom|width|height|margin|padding`; count 0.

text: Never use `transition: all`; list the exact properties (typically `opacity`, `transform`).
why: `all` unintentionally animates layout-affecting properties.
check: computed `transition-property` equals `all` on any element: count 0.

text: Animate only to clarify cause and effect or to add deliberate delight; choose easing to match what changes (size, distance, trigger).
why: Decorative motion without meaning is noise.
check: visual review per animated element: can you name the cause-effect it explains.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Animation; README "Necessity check", "Easing fits the subject".

text: Animations are interruptible and input-driven; autoplay is allowed only for muted, non-essential loops; any autoplaying motion longer than 5 seconds that sits beside other content has pause, stop, or hide controls.
why: WCAG 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide.
check: any `animation-iteration-count: infinite` or autoplay video with duration > 5 s has a reachable control; `video[autoplay]` has `muted`.

text: Set the correct `transform-origin` so motion starts where it physically should (popover grows from its trigger, not from its centre).
why: Origin carries spatial meaning.
check: computed `transform-origin` on popovers and dropdowns matches the anchor side.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Animation; README "Correct transform origin".

text: For SVG animation, apply transforms to a `<g>` wrapper and set `transform-box: fill-box; transform-origin: center`.
why: Safari historically miscalculates SVG transform origins.
check: animated SVG children sit inside a `g` with `transform-box: fill-box`.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Animation; README "Cross-browser SVG transforms".

text: When scaling text, animate a wrapper not the text node; if smoothing artefacts persist add `translateZ(0)` or `will-change: transform` to promote a layer.
why: Text anti-aliasing changes under transforms.
check: visual: no text shimmer during scale.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines README > Design "Text anti-aliasing & transforms" (not in AGENTS.md).

text: Adjust optically by +/-1 px where perception beats geometry (icon next to text, play triangles, rounded shapes).
why: Geometric centre often looks off.
check: visual at 2x zoom.

text: Every element aligns deliberately to a grid line, baseline, edge or optical centre; no accidental placement.
why: Accidental offsets read as sloppiness.
check: compare `left` / `top` of siblings in a group: deltas are 0 or a deliberate token.

text: Balance icon and text lockups by adjusting weight, size, spacing or colour (a thin icon stroke may need a heavier stroke next to medium text).
why: Mismatched stroke weights fight visually.
check: icon stroke-width relative to adjacent text weight: visual.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Layout; README "Balance contrast in lockups".

text: Verify layouts at mobile, laptop and ultra-wide; simulate ultra-wide by browser zoom at 50%.
why: Layouts fail at the extremes.
check: screenshots at 375, 1440 and 2560 px wide.

text: Respect safe areas with `env(safe-area-inset-*)` for notches and insets.
why: Content hidden under notches and home indicators.
check: fixed header/footer have padding using `env(safe-area-inset-top|bottom)`; viewport meta has `viewport-fit=cover` when used.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Layout; README "Respect safe areas".

text: No unwanted scrollbars: fix the overflow rather than hide it. Test on macOS with Show scroll bars set to Always to see the Windows view.
why: Overlay scrollbars on macOS hide overflow bugs.
check: `document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= innerWidth`; list elements with `overflow:auto` that have no overflow.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Layout; README "No excessive scrollbars".

text: Let the browser size things: prefer flex, grid and intrinsic sizing over measuring in JS.
why: Avoids layout thrash.
check: grep for `getBoundingClientRect`/`offsetWidth` driving layout state in render paths.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Layout; README "Let the browser size things".

text: Prefer inline help; use tooltips only as a last resort.
why: Tooltips are hidden, hover-only, and not touch friendly.
check: count of `[role=tooltip]` / `title` carrying essential info = 0.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Content & Accessibility; README "Inline help first".

text: Skeletons mirror final content exactly (same dimensions and structure) to avoid layout shift.
why: Prevents CLS on load-in.
check: skeleton block size vs loaded block size delta <= 1 px; CLS 0 across the swap.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Content & Accessibility; README "Stable skeletons".

text: `<title>` reflects the current context (page, state, route).
why: Orientation for tabs, history, and screen readers.
check: `document.title` changes on route change and is unique per page.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Content & Accessibility; README "Accurate page titles".

text: No dead ends: every screen offers a next step or recovery path; design empty, sparse, dense and error states for each.
why: Users stall on blank or error screens.
check: empty-state and error-state screenshots exist; each has a primary action or link.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Content & Accessibility; README "No dead ends", "All states designed".

text: Use typographic (curly) quotes and avoid widows and orphans (`text-wrap: balance` on headings, `pretty` on paragraphs).
why: Polish and tidy rag.
check: text nodes contain no straight `"` between words; headings have computed `text-wrap: balance`.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Content & Accessibility; README "Typographic quotes", "Avoid widows/orphans".

text: Use `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` (or a monospace such as Geist Mono) wherever numbers are compared or update in place (tables, prices, counters).
why: Proportional digits make columns jitter.
check: computed `font-variant-numeric` includes `tabular-nums` on `td`, counters, price cells.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Content & Accessibility; README "Tabular numbers for comparisons".

text: Status is never colour-only: pair with text labels; icons convey the same meaning in text for non-sighted users.
why: WCAG 1.4.1.
check: each status colour element also has visible text or an accessible name.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Content & Accessibility; README "Redundant status cues", "Icons have labels".

text: Accessible names exist even when the visual design omits labels; icon-only buttons have a descriptive `aria-label`; decorative elements are `aria-hidden`; verify in the accessibility tree.
why: Screen readers need names.
check: every `button, a, input` has a non-empty computed accessible name; decorative `svg` has `aria-hidden=true`.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Content & Accessibility; README "Don't ship the schema", "Accessible content", "Icon-only buttons are named".

text: Use the real ellipsis character `…`, not three periods.
why: Typographic correctness and single glyph for truncation.
check: regex `\.\.\.` in visible text: count 0.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Content & Accessibility; README "Use the ellipsis character".

text: Headings: set `scroll-margin-top` so anchored headings clear sticky headers; provide a "Skip to content" link; keep a hierarchical `<h1>`-`<h6>` outline.
why: Anchor jumps otherwise hide under fixed bars; skip link serves keyboard users.
check: `h2[id], h3[id]` computed `scroll-margin-top` >= sticky header height; first focusable is a skip link; heading levels never jump by 2.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Content & Accessibility; README "Anchored headings", "Headings & skip link".

text: Layouts survive user-generated content of short, average and very long length; text containers use `truncate`, `line-clamp-*` or `break-words`; flex children that must truncate carry `min-w-0`; empty strings and arrays render without broken UI.
why: Real data breaks tidy mockups.
check: inject a 40-character unbroken token and a 400-character string into each text slot: no overflow beyond parent (`scrollWidth <= clientWidth + 1`).
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Content Handling; README "Resilient to user-generated content".

text: Format dates, times, numbers, delimiters and currencies for the user's locale (`Intl.DateTimeFormat`, `Intl.NumberFormat`); detect language from `Accept-Language` and `navigator.languages`, never from IP or GPS.
why: Locale conventions differ; location is not language.
check: grep for hard-coded `toFixed`/`MM/DD` formatting in UI strings; locale detection code does not use geo-IP.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Content & Accessibility; README "Locale-aware formats", "Prefer language settings over location".

text: Mark brand names, product names, code tokens and identifiers with `translate="no"`.
why: Browser auto-translate garbles them.
check: `[translate=no]` on logo text, `code`, API keys.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Content & Accessibility; README "Shield verbatim content from translation".

text: Prefer native elements (`button`, `a`, `label`, `table`) before ARIA.
why: Native semantics are free and robust.
check: `[role=button]` on a `div` count 0 where a `<button>` works.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Content & Accessibility; README "Semantics before ARIA".

text: Media has captions for speech and meaningful sounds, transcripts for audio-only, and descriptions for essential visuals; media controls are keyboard operable; decorative media is hidden from assistive tech.
why: WCAG 1.2.x.
check: `video` has `track[kind=captions]`; decorative video has `aria-hidden=true` and no controls.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Content & Accessibility; README "Accessible media".

text: Glue units, shortcuts and brand names with non-breaking spaces (`10 MB`, `⌘ K`, `Vercel SDK`).
why: Stops awkward line breaks inside a unit.
check: regex `\d (MB|GB|KB|ms|px|%)` with a normal space in visible text: count 0.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Content & Accessibility; README "Non-breaking spaces for glued terms".

text: Network mutations (POST, PATCH, DELETE) complete in under 500 ms.
why: Above this the UI feels laggy and needs optimistic handling.
check: measure p95 of mutation requests < 500 ms.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Performance; README "Network latency budgets".

text: Virtualise large lists (more than 50 items) with a virtual-list library or `content-visibility: auto`.
why: DOM size drives layout cost.
check: any list container with > 50 children has virtualisation or `content-visibility: auto`.

text: Preload only above-the-fold images; lazy-load the rest; give every image explicit dimensions to prevent CLS.
why: LCP and layout stability.
check: `img` below the first viewport has `loading=lazy`; every `img` has `width`/`height` or `aspect-ratio`; above-fold hero is not lazy.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Performance; README "Preload wisely", "No image-caused CLS".

text: Add `<link rel="preconnect">` (with `crossorigin` when needed) for asset and CDN origins; preload critical fonts with `<link rel="preload" as="font">` and `font-display: swap`; subset fonts via `unicode-range` and limit variable axes to those used.
why: Cuts DNS/TLS latency and font flash, and shrinks font bytes.
check: head contains preconnect for each third-party origin used above the fold; `@font-face` has `font-display: swap` and `unicode-range`; preloaded font has `crossorigin`.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Performance; README "Preconnect to origins", "Preload fonts", "Subset fonts".

text: Use `<video autoplay muted loop playsinline>` rather than animated GIF for loops, provide a still or reduced-motion alternative, and for short non-essential loops add an H.264 MP4 `<source>` in `<picture>` (gated by `prefers-reduced-motion`) so Safari treats it as an image.
why: Video is far smaller than GIF; reduced-motion users get a still.
check: no `img[src$=".gif"]` with duration > 1 s; `video[autoplay]` has `muted playsinline loop` and a `poster`.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Performance; README "Video over animated GIF", "Safari video-as-image".

text: Batch DOM reads and writes to avoid forced reflow; move long tasks to Web Workers; keep controlled inputs cheap per keystroke (prefer uncontrolled).
why: Main-thread blocking harms INP.
check: performance trace: no long tasks > 50 ms on keystroke; no layout thrash pattern (read-write-read loops).
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Performance; README "Minimize layout work", "Keystroke cost", "Don't use the main thread for expensive work".

text: Profile with CPU and network throttling, with extensions disabled; test iOS Low Power Mode and macOS Safari; track re-renders (React DevTools or React Scan).
why: Fast dev machines hide real costs.
check: process: profile run records throttling settings.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Performance; README "Device/browser matrix", "Measure reliably", "Throttle when profiling", "Track re-renders".

text: Set `color-scheme: dark` on `<html>` for dark themes so scrollbars and native controls get dark UI; set `<meta name="theme-color">` to match the page background.
why: Native chrome otherwise stays light.
check: `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).colorScheme` contains `dark` in dark theme; `meta[name=theme-color]` equals body background.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Dark Mode & Theming; README "Set the appropriate color-scheme", "Browser UI matches your background".

text: Native `<select>` gets an explicit `background-color` and `color`.
why: Windows renders dark-mode selects with unreadable defaults.
check: computed `background-color` and `color` on `select` are set tokens in both themes.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Dark Mode & Theming; README "Windows `<select>` background".

text: Guard date/time rendering against hydration mismatch (server and client output must agree).
why: Hydration errors cause flashes and lost state.
check: no hydration mismatch warnings in console with timezone set differently from server.

text: Build shadows from at least two layers (ambient plus direct light); combine borders and shadows, with semi-transparent borders for crisper edges.
why: Single-layer shadows look flat; translucent borders adapt to any background.
check: computed `box-shadow` on cards/popovers contains >= 2 comma-separated layers; border colour has alpha < 1.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Design; README "Layered shadows", "Crisp borders".

text: Nested radii: child radius <= parent radius and concentric (child = parent radius minus the gap).
why: Mismatched curves look off.
check: for each rounded child inside a rounded parent: `childRadius <= parentRadius - padding` (approx).

text: On non-neutral backgrounds tint borders, shadows and text toward the background hue.
why: Neutral grey on a tinted surface looks dirty.
check: hue of border colour within about 30 degrees of the surface hue when surface chroma is above ~0.02 (OKLCH).
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Design; README "Hue consistency". The 30 degrees and 0.02 values are my own thresholds [unverified].

text: Use colour-blind-friendly palettes in charts.
why: About 8% of men have colour-vision deficiency.
check: simulate protan/deutan/tritan; series remain distinguishable (use shape or label too).

text: Check contrast, and prefer APCA over WCAG 2 for perceptual accuracy; hover, active and focus states increase contrast relative to rest.
why: WCAG 2 ratios misjudge dark mode and thin type.
check: compute APCA Lc and WCAG ratio for text pairs (no numeric APCA floor is given in the source); state colours have higher contrast than rest colours.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Design; README "Minimum contrast", "Interactions increase contrast".

text: Avoid banding when fading to dark colours with CSS masks; use background images for such fades.
why: 8-bit gradients band on dark values.
check: visual: no visible steps in a dark gradient fade.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines AGENTS.md > Design; README "Avoid gradient banding".

text: Use active voice and action-oriented phrasing ("Install the CLI", not "The CLI will be installed"); write in second person; keep nouns consistent; be concise.
why: Faster scanning and clearer ownership.
check: copy lint: passive "will be/is being" phrases flagged; first-person "we/our" flagged in UI strings.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines README > Copywriting "Active voice", "Action-oriented language", "Write in second person", "Keep nouns consistent".
section: 2.12 Copywriting (Vercel-specific, the README says these are brand choices, not universal)

text: Use numerals for counts ("8 deployments"); show currency consistently with either 0 or 2 decimals in a given context, never mixing; separate number and unit with a non-breaking space ("10 MB").
why: Scannability and consistency.
check: regex for spelled-out counts; price column has uniform decimal count.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines README > Copywriting "Use numerals for counts", "Consistent currency formatting", "Separate numbers & units".
section: 2.12 Copywriting (Vercel-specific, the README says these are brand choices, not universal)

text: Errors are positive and guide the exit: state what to do, not just what failed ("Your API key is incorrect or expired. Generate a new key in your account settings."); labels are specific ("Save API Key", not "Continue").
why: Users need a next action.
check: each error string contains an imperative verb or link; button labels are not generic ("Submit", "Continue") on API forms.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines README > Copywriting "Default to positive language", "Error messages guide the exit", "Avoid ambiguity".
section: 2.12 Copywriting (Vercel-specific, the README says these are brand choices, not universal)

text: Use consistent placeholders for sample values (strings `YOUR_API_TOKEN_HERE`, numbers `0123456789`).
why: Familiarity for developers.
check: grep placeholder values for ad-hoc samples.
section: 2.12 Copywriting (Vercel-specific, the README says these are brand choices, not universal)

text: Vercel brand choices (not universal): Title Case (Chicago style) for headings and buttons in product UI, sentence case on marketing pages; `&` instead of "and".
why: House style.
check: decide per brand style card; for Larpo see section 5.
source: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines README > Copywriting "Headings & buttons use Title Case", "Prefer `&` over `and`".
section: 2.12 Copywriting (Vercel-specific, the README says these are brand choices, not universal)

text: Every `input`, `select`, `textarea` has a visible `<label for>` (or wrapping label), placed above the control; keep label text short ("Email address" over "Enter your email address").
why: Screen readers announce it, tap/click on it focuses the control, and research cited by the course favours top labels for scan speed.
check: axe `label`; Playwright: for each control `label.getBoundingClientRect().bottom <= control.top + 2` at 390 px width; no control with only `placeholder` or `aria-label` (`A10`).
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/forms + https://web.dev/learn/images (+ web.dev lazy-loading, iframe lazy-loading, preload-responsive-images, replace-gifs-with-videos, image CDNs articles)

text: Never use `placeholder` as the label or to explain the field; put format help in an element beneath the control and link it with `aria-describedby`.
why: Placeholder vanishes on typing, looks prefilled, defaults to low contrast and makes it hard to see which fields remain.
check: static: `[placeholder]` controls all have a label; computed placeholder colour contrast >= 4.5 if kept (`::placeholder`).
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/forms + https://web.dev/learn/images (+ web.dev lazy-loading, iframe lazy-loading, preload-responsive-images, replace-gifs-with-videos, image CDNs articles)

text: Group related controls (radios, checkboxes, address blocks) in `<fieldset>` with a `<legend>` as its first child.
